1. Resume Shortlisting

2. Aptitude

3. Group Discussion

4. Technical + HR Round 1

5. HR Round

6. Technical + HR Round 2

Round 1: Resume Shortlisting Round [100+ candidates had applied.]

The students who wished to appear for KPMG's process had to fill out the form provided by the
company on their platform, which was HirePro. We could choose only one role between IPCG and
Digital Trust; I chose Digital Trust. We were asked details regarding our active backlogs (those who had
active backlogs weren't allowed for the further process) and our CGPA's (strictly above 6.0 throughout
the engineering tenure). Other than the aforementioned restrictions, all the students who applied and
filled out the form correctly were allowed to continue the process.
Note: Having a high CGPA opens a lot of doors, especially during placements and, to some extent,
higher studies. Be consistent in your academics, and it'll pay off in the long run. If you have any
pending backlogs while you're reading this, please make sure to clear them as soon as possible because
they'll cause you a lot of trouble during placements. There isn't a single company on campus that
entertains poor academics.

Round 2: Aptitude Round [93 candidates appeared for this round.] [Time: 55 minutes]

The aptitude round was conducted in online mode on the HirePro platform. It lasted for about 55
minutes, the test had a total of 45 questions which were divided into 3 sections which were: Analytical
Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Verbal Ability. We were able to navigate between sections and
there was no time limit per section. In my opinion, the quality of the questions asked was of medium
difficulty.
I'd prepared for the aptitude round using the following materials:

1. CareerRide's Quantitative Aptitude Playlist:

[https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpyc33gOcbVA4qXMoQ5vmhefTruk5t9lt]

2. IndiaBix: [https://www.indiabix.com/]

3. Quantitative Aptitude by R.S. Aggarwal. [Link for the same.]

Following any one of these resources would be more than enough vis -à-vis aptitude tests for on-campus
placements. Companies only ask basic questions in their filtering tests.

PPT: We were called at 10:30 AM on the 1st of October for the pre-placement talk; a few candidates
didn't show up for the process, which was noted by the TPC's, and those candidates were given
demerits.
The pre-placement talk lasted for 30 minutes, as we'd been asked to attend IPCG's PPT too, so we
already had an idea about KPMG and the role for which we're applying. The PPT was taken by the HR
and partner; the partner talked about the role for a while and then asked us if we had any questions. I
asked a few questions regarding the responsibilities and career growth.
I was taking notes, and since I kept interacting with the team during the PPT, I was noticed by all of
them.

Round 3: Group Discussion [29 candidates appeared for this round.] [30 seconds of ideation time + 10

minutes of group discussion + 1 minute for conclusion]
The candidate pool was divided between IPCG and DT after the test; the division was done on the basis
of the candidate's preference and their resume. The IPCG group had their process a day before ours.
For digital trust, we were divided into 3 panels of 10 candidates each. My panel had very active members;
the topic given to us was "Phenomenon of Influencer Marketing." The panellists/judges for this GD were
the same partner who took the PPT at KPMG with over 14 years of experience and a director. I took a
total of 2 entries and h ad very good points and referenced with real -life examples (which is the most
important aspect in a GD). Firstly, I talked about the loyal fan base of an influencer and how greatly it

affects the sales of any product that they market. Then I talked about the fact that start-ups are able to get
great exposure due to the same and how it has given the start-ups the much-needed platform early in their
business and that they can target the fan bases who would genuinely be interested in their products by
talking with the influencers. I also talked about a few negative aspects of the same: many influencers have
started buying followers in order to reach fame quickly, which has negatively affected the overall social
media space and has opened up a lot of attack vectors for threat actors. I also referenced the recent (Beer
Biceps) Ranveer Allahbadia's case that, due to fame, there's also the over looming threat of being victim
to a cyberattack.
Points to remember : Apart from your content, your performance and approach  to group discussions
leave an impression on the panellists. As the panellists are the ones to take your interviews, it's important
to actively participate in the GD, communicate your thoughts, listen to your peers, and always be
supportive and positive during the GDs. If someone is struggling to recall any phrases or words, do help
them out, as it leaves a very positive impression and is also a sign that you're actively listening to them.
If, perhaps, you happen to disagree with any points, have a very res pectful tone during the same; also, if
you try to enter and happen to be interrupted, let the other party go first. As this happened to me, I said,
"I'd like to hear your point first and would like to go after you." This shows respect and politeness.
After the GD, the panellists asked us to conclude; he pointed out 2 people to give the conclusion; they
hadn't spoken much or at all during the GD, hence the reason. Everybody in my panel performed pretty
well. Since my colleagues were struggling with English, they switched to Hindi/Marathi during their
entries, which is absolutely fine. The panellists pointed out as well that it's nothing to be ashamed of if
you're not fluent with English and if you'd like to speak in Hindi or your regional language instead. Your
voice modulation/enunciation, GD etiquette, and poise matter more during a GD than your control over
English.
Note: Before the GD began, the partner/panellist had asked us for our resume, and after the GD ended,
he immediately pointed out two people whose resume, in comparison to the rest of the participants, was
extremely lacking, their resume formatting was poor, and that he isn't happy with them at all. He tried
to reason with them further but gave up after their casual responses.
This set the tone for the further rounds that the team is not here to mess around or have fun.
A total of 17 candidates were shortlisted for the further processes. Four candidates from IPCG were
further added to the list on the recommendation of their interviewers, which had happened a day before.

Most of my interview rounds were skipped due to my GD performance. Keep this in mind and do well in
your GD itself.

Round 4: Technical + HR Interview 1 [21 candidates appeared for this round.] [20 minutes]

My interview was conducted by the same partner I mentioned earlier, along with his colleague, a director. I
entered the room and put my hand forth for a firm handshake; this again leaves a good impression. I
asked to take a seat, and they started the interview by asking my introduction. In the introduction, I
emphasized more on my cybersecurity skills and the relevant industry experience which I'd gained during
my internships, as well as the soft skills I'd developed through both work and extracurricular activities.
My interview was mainly taken by the director; he was focusing more on my resume and the wordings
that I'd used and told me to elaborate on them. Throughout the duration of the interview, I remained
calm and composed, focused on the questions, and answered them promptly. As I knew the inside out of
the resume, I was able to understand the terminology that they were using (the terms that they used were
specific to cybersecurity only, such as "hardening guidelines," "configuration management," and
"improving the security posture.") The director further grilled me on the technical aspects of my
resume; he wanted to know the kind of work I did during my internships down to the minute details.
He also asked me, why not continue on with that company and why KPMG? I'd prepared extensively
for this question, so I confidently answered it. They liked that, and they also wanted to check if I'd leave
KPMG after the duration of my internship. I answered the same as well, that I'd definitely continue with
KPMG after my internship.
Overall, they only wanted to take a gander in seeing how well I maintain my composure during serious
situations and how this would translate into my work once I joined. Finally, they asked me about the
people whom I worked with during my internships and if it's alright to call my manager and ask him for
my review. I confidently told them to go ahead; they liked that too. After which they asked me how
confident I am about this interview. I told them that I'm pretty confident that I'll make through; they
appreciated that very much and then asked me to go for the HR interview.
The director was solely focusing on my resume throughout the interview, I'd been told by my seniors
that they wish to see how well you perform under pressure, as consulting is a stressful job.
Note: A few of my improvement areas: I could've been calmer and registered each question first before
answering it, all of which only comes through rigorous practice.
There was no formal list sent out for the further shortlists; I'm not aware of how many were shortlisted
for the further rounds. Many of the candidates did not perform well in their interviews, which was
highlighted by the team to the TPCs. Around 4 were instantly rejected after their first round.
The first Techno-HR round was pretty easy for the rest of the people, as all of them were asked CCN
fundamentals and basic cybersecurity questions; practicing the same a few days before the interviews
would be sufficient.

Study material for Cybersecurity:
Computer Networks:
Atul Sharma's playlist. Focus more on Cisco Packet Tracer and OSI layers as both shall build your
fundamentals.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2mvn4eOOVZo
NetworkChuck's playlist for CCN fundamentals. He makes studying CCN very fun.
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLIhvC56v63IJVXv0GJcl9vO5Z6znCVb1P

Cybersecurity: Study OWASP Top 10, basic attack vectors like CORS, XSS, CSRF and so on. Also,
study viruses, botnets, malware and ransomware attacks. Be up to date on current events for
cybersecurity.
Practicing DVWA Labs and Metasploitable2 Labs shall give you an in-depth idea about the attacks.
OWASP Top 10: https://www.hacksplaining.com/
DVWA Labs: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLHUKi1UlEgOJLPSFZaFKMoexpM6qhOb4Q

Round 5: HR Interview [~12 candidates appeared for this round.] [25 minutes.]

I was told by the HR manager that this would be my last round and that they're happy with my
performance so no further rounds would be conducted for me, but she'd asked me to stick around if I'm
free for the rest of the day, that is.
After my Techno-HR round wrapped up, I was immediately called for the HR round. The HR manager
who was taking my interview was very chill, and she asked me about my day, how my previous
interview went, and the toughest question that they'd asked. I responded in a formal manner though, and
she seemed pretty satisfied with my answers. She then proceeded to ask me about my family, where I'm
from, and which location I'd prefer.
After which she proceeded to ask me about my weaknesses and what went wrong in my previous
interviews, which was holding me back from being placed. I realized that this was one of the deciding
questions for this interview, so I gave a very humble and serious answer: Throughout this placement
journey, I had to do a lot of self-introspection; hence, after each interview I started listing out what went
wrong and what I should improve on, following which the most recent interview that I couldn't crack
was of Barclay's Bank, where I believed that one of my improvement areas should be confidence, so I
practiced for the interviews to improve my confidence. I gave more interviews to my friends and in
front of the mirror in order to be more fluent during the interviews. She seemed very happy with this
answer; furthermore, she asked me if I'm interested in higher studies, to which I replied that I'm more
interested in pursuing the cybersecurity certifications rather than the MBA or MS. She seemed satisfied

with the answer and told me that I'm done for the day and if she needs anymore details, she'd call for
me, and whether I'd have any questions for her, I asked her about the career growth in my role, and she
answered it.
Overall, the interview was very chill, and I was the one driving it; this led to me being much more
relaxed than my previous one. This was the end of the entire process for me.
A few of my friends were being interviewed late into the night; the entire process lasted till 8 PM. I
stayed around to accompany my colleagues and asked them about their experience. The third round,
which was the Techno-HR 2, was the hardest for the rest; the interviewers were grilling them a lot, and
hence no one was confident about the results, but we kept our heads high and hoped for the best.

The results were announced two days after the process, a total of 6 people were selected and I was
one of them!

Pointers for Placement Processes:

1. Try to attempt seriously for the processes of most (or all) the companies, regardless of the role.

You'll get an idea of the interview processes and the kind of pressure that you'll be under during
the entirety of the process which shall prepare you for the next process or your target company.
KPMG was my 4th interview and the 1st company with my dream role, the role for which I'd
prepared extensively for about a year.
Once you start giving more interviews, you get an idea about the kind of questions are asked and
how you should tackle such questions and what kind of answers they're expecting on their end.
After participating in the interviews, try to write down a similar transcript as this, so you'll
understand where exactly you went wrong and where exactly you require more improvement.
Not everyone is born perfect, the more your practice the closer you shall get to cracking
interviews.

2. Do participate in national level competitions. A lot of my interviewers focused on my case study

competitions and extra-curricular tournaments which I'd participated in, rather than my
internships which was pretty surprising but understandable as they're more familiar with their
area of expertise rather than mine. The same opens up different dialogues during your interviews
which may result in your favor.

3. Do not lose hope. Placements are draining but you should never lose hope. You'll definitely get

placed, luckily for me I had a lot of well-wishers consisting of my family and friends and they

were always backing me up during my journey. Please do not hesitate to call up your family
members or friends during placements, as placements take up most of your mental space, we
must let lose sometimes and hence go for a couple of outings as you'll feel lighter and more
motivated for the next process.
Further pointers for placements in general:
Placement season is quite taxing, mentally and physically as well, but they're part and parcel of
engineering. You can treat them as a part of your development/improvement journey which was what I
did or look at them as a line item and try to tackle them as soon as possible.
I tried my level best for a few companies but their requirements were different. I still didn't lose hope
and neither should you. Being selected and getting placed on-campus becomes one of your highlights in
your engineering tenure, if you do not get selected in your dream company or your dream role, it's
absolutely fine because we still have our entire lives ahead of us to strive for the best and we must
always reach for the stars.

Contact Details:
You can connect with me on my LinkedIn handle: [https://www.linkedin.com/in/advait-khaire/].
I'm also available on WhatsApp: +91 7304943830
If you wish to call me, please send me a message on WhatsApp.

All the very best! You can do it.

journey.prep:
1. The placement process can indeed be a challenging experience, but with each failure comes the

opportunity to learn and grow. This was my fourth interview, and while I wasn't initially a very patient
person, the process taught me the value of patience and the understanding that what is meant for you will
eventually come your way. It's important not to lose hope and to keep trying until the very end. The first
round, typically the online assessment, can feel unpredictable for most companies, as many candidate s
solve all the questions but only a few are shortlisted. If you don't clear the first round, keep practicing and
don't be discouraged. Over time, you will get shortlisted. In the meantime, ensure you are well -prepared
by covering all relevant topics and acquiring essential skills.

2. I prioritized overall development and avoided focusing on one specific area. Through my projects and

DSA problem-solving, I developed both the necessary technical skills and aptitude. In my first year, I
participated in various committees and NGOs, and in my third year, I took on the role of Girls' Class
Representative (CR), which further enhanced my profile. Many candidates tend to have similar
backgrounds, so it's important to offer something unique. Firms like KPMG, in particular, value
candidates with a distinct, forward-thinking mindset.

3. Placements often mostly an element of luck, but your hard work is equally important. Trust the process

and consistently put forth your best effort.

You can feel free to connect with me on LinkedIn : https://www.linkedin.com/in/rupali-sawale-00b169261/

1.     Aptitude Round

The online assessment test was aptitude based a nd consisted of 45 questions on hire pro platform there were
three sections Analytical Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Verbal Ability, with 15 questions
in each section . All the questions were of medium level  and there was no specific time constraint for sections.

For the aptitude I would suggest solving questions on IndiaBix platform and careerride youtube playlist
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnc9ojITRg4&list=PLpyc33gOcbVA4qXMoQ5vmhefTruk5t9lt .

2. Group Discussion [21 candidates appeared for this round ]

This round was a Group Discussion (GD) with 9-10 participants in each panel. The topic given to us was
"Electric Vehicles in India: Why are they used, and what is their impact?" We were provided two minutes
to think, during which I began noting down key points. Initially, I focused on pollution caused by vehicles.
As the discussion progressed, other candidates talked about pollution and the affordability of electric
vehicles in rural areas. I chose to highlight the depletion of fuel as a more pressing conce rn than the
financial aspect. At the end of the discussion, each participant was given the opportunity to conclude with
a single statement. It's important to note that if you're unfamiliar with the topic or don't have many points
to contribute, it's perfectly acceptable to observe others and respond accordingly. My advice is to maintain
confidence, speak only relevant points, maintain fluency,  and ensure proper body posture throughout the
GD.

3. Technical Round 1 (30-35 mins approx)

My interview was primarily focused on my resume. The interviewer was approachable and supportive
throughout the process. He started with the usual question, "Introduce yourself," and then asked for a brief
overview of one of my full stack projects, which w as a group project. Then asked about my role in the
project. After providing a detailed explanation, he shifted to security -related questions about the project,
asking how I would secure the website and the steps I would take to ensure its safety.
Since my resume was technical based, the discussion moved toward data science. He asked me to define
data analytics and inquired about the subjects covered in my data science coursework. He also noticed my
interest in both data science and web development and asked why I was pursuing a role  in cybersecurity.
I responded thoroughly, taking about 2-3 minutes to explain my reasoning.
Later, he asked some basic questions about computer networks. Although I hadn't specifically studied
cybersecurity or revised topics from computer networks  but still , I was able to answer his questions  on
computer networks , and he also offered guidance when needed.
One piece of advice: Avoid attempting to answer questions you're unsure of. Interviewers are experienced
and knowledgeable, and they prefer concise, relevant responses rather than unnecessarily drawn -out
answers.

4. HR Round  (15-20 mins approx)

The HR round was quite relaxed as well. She began by asking about my previous rounds and the name of
the interviewer who conducted my technical interview. Since she had been part of my panel during the Group
Discussion (GD), she inquired why I hadn't spoken earlier and only contributed later. I explained that the
initial discussion was centered around fin ancial topics, so I took a moment to consider more significant
concerns. I also mentioned a few points I had planned to discuss but couldn't due to time constraints.
Following this, she asked about my family background and why I wanted to join KPMG.
She concluded the interview by asking if I had any questions for her. I inquired about the work culture at
KPMG, and we had a discussion on this topic for about five minutes

4.   Technical Round 2 (Interview with KPMG's Director and Partner) (2 5-30 mins approx) [6

candidates got offer]
This round was a mix of both HR and resume-based questions. The interviewers were quite approachable
and began with the typical "Introduce yourself" question . They then asked about the three project I had
submitted and proceeded to ask basic-level questions related to computer networks.
Given that one of my projects involved machine learning, they inquired about the difference between
machine learning and artificial intelligence. They also asked me about the Convolutional Neural Network

(CNN) algorithm, which was mentioned in the same project.

The interview then shifted to HR-related questions, such as my family background, why I was interested
in the role, and where I see myself in the next five years.
The results were announced on October 3rd, 2024, and I was one of the six candidates who received an
offer.

1. Aptitude Round

2. Group Discussion

3. Technical Round 1 (Interview with Technical Head)

4. HR Round (Interview with HR manager)

5. Technical Round 2 (Interview with KPMG's Director and Partner)

Round 1:

1. Aptitude Round (55 mins)

The assessment took place online via the HirePro platform and consisted of 45 questions, divided evenly
across three sections: Analytical Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, and Verbal Ability, with 15 questions
in each section. Notably, there was no specific time constraint for each section. Overall, I found the
difficulty level to be moderate. Following this round, 21 candidates were shortlisted. For those who find
the Quantitative section particularly challenging, I suggest checking out the following playlist for
preparation: Quantitative Aptitude Playlist. Additionally, Indiabix offers a wide range of practice questions
that can be useful for preparation.

2. Group Discussion [21 students appeared for this round]

Our group discussion (GD) panel consisted of 9 -10 candidates. My panel was filled with good speakers.
The topic assigned to us was "EV in India". Since it was a bit common subject, we were given 2 minutes
to gather our thoughts. I quickly jotted down key points on paper, considering how EV impacts different

sectors and is used differently by individuals. I also touched upon the Benefits of EV in both Public and
Private Sector, while highlighting its positive contributions. I ensured that my arguments were backed by
real-life examples and statistics --one of which was about that now a days EV vehicles are becoming
affordable for middle class families by giving example of Tata Nexon EV model. A GD isn't just about
speaking, it's also about listening and engaging with the ideas of fellow participants. After about 10
minutes of a healthy discussion, each of us was given 1 minute to conclude, where we were expected to
summarize and state whether we supported or opposed the topic.
After this round, some students were selected for the next phase, with some candidates advancing from
my panel.
Here are a few tips that helped me succeed:

1. Participate in mock GDs: Make sure you engage in mock GDs conducted by  our Teachers in initial

semesters in soft skills sub jects and also by your Training and Placement Office (TPO) before
placements. These sessions give you valuable experience and highlight areas where you can improve,
based on evaluator feedback and self -reflection. The more you practice, the better you'll get.
Personally, my habit of reading and communicating regularly, combined with my experience leading
student organizations, helped me excel in this round.

2. Balance communication with substance : Communication skills are crucial in a GD, but they must

be backed by valid arguments and a well -rounded perspective. If you're not confident in your
knowledge of the topic, stay calm, listen to your fellow panellists, and build on their points rather than
staying silent.

3. Focus on listening and maintaining positive body language : Many candidates focus only on

speaking without truly listening to others or maintaining positive body language, which can harm their
performance. Most of the time, you'll be listening, so avoid turning the discussion into a heated debate.
Stay polite and maintain the group's decorum.

4. Clarify any doubts: If you're unsure about the topic or its scope, don't hesitate to ask the evaluator

for clarification before you start brainstorming.

3. Technical Round 1 (30 mins approx)

This round was completely resume based. They asked me to give a brief introduction about myself after
which I was asked to explain my projects one by one. My entire resume was made for the non-Tech role.
It mainly consisted my  Educational Background, Courses that I had done through college an d my own,
Projects, Internship experience , Skills, Extra - Curricular Activities. I had taken Barclays Cyber Shala
course which was offered by college, it helped me a lot in this process as the role demanded Cyber Security
knowledge and experience, so it had given me both. So, I would request you guys to go for it. Most of the
questions were asked on Cyber Security atleast for me, here he asked me scenario based questions on what
would I to do, basic Cyber Security questions. Then he asked about the Projects and the skills that I had I
mentioned.

4. HR Round (Interview with HR manager) (20 min approx)

This round was like most of the HR roun ds. It consisted all the frequently asked HR questions. I started
with my Introduction, later I was asked about my family background, the place form where I come from.
Then they started asking me HR questions some of them were like "Will you be comfortable if an LGBTQ
works in your team? " for which I answered yes and said that it will be okay as at the end of the day the
impact that we created matters. Later she asked  me "How many days in a week would you love to work
form Office ? ".  Then certain  frequently asked behavioural  questions were asked. Refer this link for
standard HR Questions with answers which my senior  had prepared -
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ukWKckgkcs99Ww5S5OI9diirGgHwgP9e/view?usp=sharing

5. Technical Round 2 (Interview with KPMG's Director and Partner) (20 min approx)

This started with my Introduction. Later they asked about my projects and Internship that I had done. Then
they started as king me CCN questions wh ich most of them I was able to answe r. Prepare for CCN
questions (GFG preferred) also if time permits go through all the Computer Fundamentals subjects. It will
really help y ou. Then the y asked me "Why shoul d we hire you  ?". They tested my knowledge and
confirmed that whatever I had mentioned on my resume was true.

night to get us placed.

The placement season is very hectic. Your friends will get placed before you and you might feel left out and dejected. Aptitude Round (55 mins)
Group Discussion (20 mins (can end before) + conclusion)
Technical Round (depends on the panel)
HR (5 - 10 mins)
Director (depends on the panel)
The process goes on throughout the day, so be prepared accordingly.

1. Aptitude Round [ 100+ candidates appeared for this round ]

Basic quant/arithmetic questions
If you're preparing for CAT, this will be very easy for you
You might not be able to complete all the questions. That's alright. Just make sure the ones you've done are correct
Tip: Work with assumptions to make your calculations easy
Practice: IndiaBix, GeeksForGeeks

2.     Group Discussion [ 48 candidates appeared for this round ]

The topic is given on the spot. You'll have 2 mins to gather your thoughts. Carry a notebook to jot down your points.
We were assigned For and Against roles for the particular statement. In the middle of the discussion, we were asked to speak for the other side without taking any time to think about the points.

Tips:

Jot down the points for both sides so you can have the advantage of speaking first when the sides are switched.
If someone else discusses a point that you had jotted down earlier, grab that opportunity to say that you agree with their point and provide some additional information for the same.
It's okay not to be the first one to speak; what is important is the you deliver without fumbling and back your points with valid facts.
Practice: TPO GD sessions and communication skills lectures in your first-year

3.    Technical Round [ 18 candidates appeared for this round (6 panels - 3 from each panel) ]

For my panel, this was a thoroughly resume-based round
If you are unaware of the answer to a question, calmly say so. Although this does not always work, what is important is to not panic. The moment you panic, it's game over.
Make sure you are putting all the projects you are confident of. They can be the easiest projects but if you can answer any question that is thrown at you, you will certainly earn some extra points. Besides, these projects will boost your confidence.
I had won a case study competition and I put that up in my projects list. I was asked a lot of questions about that and even asked to show the presentation I made.
There were some situational questions in addition to the resume-based ones.

Tips:

It is very important to be aware of your body language and present yourself confidently. For example, I have a habit of fiddling with my thumbs even when I am not anxious. It leaves a negative impression on the interviewer. Instead, I learned to keep my hands on my lap which helped me hide this habit.
This day will be very long, so try your best to be fresh mentally.
Listen to interviews and ask your friends (who you think are better at giving interviews than you) to take some mocks for you.

3. HR Round [ 12 candidates appeared for this round ]

This was a normal HR round. You can refer to videos and look up frequently asked HR questions and prepare their answers beforehand.
One tip is to pay special attention to the PPT. You will find something to ask the HR representative at the end of this round. It is important to show that you are interested in joining the company; asking questions subtly shows your interest.

3. Director Round [ 12 candidates appeared for this round (no rejects from HR) ]

This was the most difficult round. From the moment you enter, the directors are out for your blood. They want to see if you will crack under pressure. The questions can be about literally anything and they will grill you irrespective of your answer. They want to test your promptness and composure.
The only tip I can give you for this round is to be calm.
This round can be really unnerving but if you give this interview as if you are playing a game, this round can be really fun.

4 students were offered the job.

2. [Round 2 Name] (around 40 candidates got shortlisted)

This round happened on 12th August. This was a tech round.
There were 3 panelists. In this round mainly the questions revolved around your projects and your resume.
Each and everything which I put in my resume was asked to me. Each skill, each project. One of my projects was discussed at the start of the round and i had made it in MERN stack. The interviewer asked me why did  I use MongoDB for this. Then he asked me to tell me some of the schemas i had implemented and asked me to make tables in SQL corresponding to those schemas. Related to those tables he asked me 3 4 sql queries involving group by, aggregation, and joining tables.
After that he tried to grill on each skill written in my resume and the interview ended with him telling me to send in the next candidate.
In the end he also showed me one of my submissions in the OA for a coding question and asked me to explain my approach and the code.

Round 1: Online Test

The test had a duration of 60 minutes and was divided into three sections:

1. Verbal Ability - 20 Questions

2. Analytical Ability - 20 Questions

3. Programming Ability - 20 Questions

There was no specific time limit for each section; you were free to solve any section at any point during the
test. Additionally, there was no negative marking for incorrect answers.

• The Analytical Ability section was generally solvable.

• In the Programming Ability section, most questions involved being given an output, and you had to

select the correct code from the provided options that would generate that output. Some questions
were related to DBMS (Database Management Systems).

Round 2: Interview (Tech + HR)

Betore the interview began, we were asked to write code for three questions based on strings. These
questions were relatively easy. After the test was completed, candidates were called one by one for the
interview.
The interview began with me introducing myself, followed by the HR asking about my family background. I
was then asked to explain how I solved the string-based coding questions and what the optimal solutions for
them would be. After that, I was asked to write the code for binary search. The conversation then shifted to
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts, where I was asked about the four pillars of OOP, with a
specific focus on how abstraction is implemented, leading to further questions on related topics. We also
discussed the projects I had worked on and how I implemented them. In the next segment, I was asked to
solve SQL queries. One of the SQL questions involved a self-join, which I found confusing and struggled to
solve completely. Finally, they asked some HR-related questions, including my long-term and short-term
goals.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Important Tips:

• Make sure you know everything about your projects. Spend a good chunk of time explaining the

deatils.

• Practice DSA on leetcode/Hackerrank.

• Know the four pillars of OOP (Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction), and be

able to explain and apply them.

• If you encounter a challenging question, don't panic. Try to explain what you understand about the

problem, even if you can't fully solve it. Interviewers appreciate effort and problem-solving mindset.

• If you have done any internship it will come handy.

1.  Online MCQ Test [Around 150 students appeared for this round]

There was a criteria of 7+ CGPA for applying at BrowserStack and everyone got the HackerEarth MCQ test
link which was valid for 2 days and I have given the test on the 2nd day i.e., on 15th Aug.
It was an online test based on HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DBMS, etc. There were 20 MCQs and we were
given 50 minutes to solve it on HackerEarth. Those questions mainly covered the basics of each subject so it
was pretty easy can be solved in 10 minutes!!
Actually, we didn't have idea that they are also going to conduct hiring process for their sister Company
Edra Labs.

I got shortlisted for Edra Labs (I've no idea on what basis they  divided students as the test was common for
everyone). But I am damn sure they shortlisted students for both companies based on score as well as the
Resume (So make sure your Resume stands out [Internships do help a lot]).

I do remember some of the questions and I am attaching the list of it.
Online Test

2.    Machine Coding Round [22 candidates were shortlised] (Online)

This process was in Online mode on 20/08/2024 around 11.00am the meeting(zoom) started where they gave
brief about what Edra Labs does and what is their Vision. After that they shared the link of Google doc of
problem statement which was basically about creating Restful API with some conditions. After that everyone
was assigned to separate breakout rooms with one Mentor for help and guidance. Around 11:30 we started
working on the Problem statement. Time duration to solve the problem was 2 Hours.  I chose Fa stAPI for
solving as I  recently worked with FastAPI in my internship and I was confident.  I chose MultiThreading
approach to fulfill the requirements.  Mentor visited once to check what I am doing and if I've any doubt
(please ask at least one doubt which makes them believe you've read the problem thoroughly and you're
thinking on your own). In my code one of the logic was taking O(n) time so he told me to try to optimize it to
O(1) or O(log n) Then I made those changes to achieve O(1) complexity . I was able to solve the problem
completely covering all test cases and handling edge cases within 1 and half hour. Then around 1:30 evaluation
started with my mentor. I was able to answer all the doubts he asked. He also told me to do some modifications
during evaluation time and cross questioned me to check if I do completely know about my code.

We were allowed to use Internet but they strictly told to not use any of the code completion tools (e.g. copilot)
But make sure you know what each line of your code even if you're taking help from internet as they can ask
anything during evaluation.

Then around 3.00pm I got call for the next round which was scheduled at 3:50 pm.
Problem Statement

3.  Technical Interview [Around 7 candidates were shortlisted]

Interview started with interviewer giving his introduction and what he does at Edra Labs. Then he asked me
to introduce myself and go through your resume.
Then he went towards asking fundamental questions . What is difference between SQL and NOSQL? When
to choose SQL/ NOSQL and why? What happens exactly when you search google.com and how does it
displays the page (something like that)? I gave answer that firstly DNS will resolve the IP address for
google.com and request will be sent to the server. Then to answer how it displays firstly I answered with the
help of DOM he said somehow correct but what exactly performs so I tried to remember what that single
entity can be so I answered him babel coz I read it in React that for browser to understand JS it uses babel as
React uses JSX. But he was like you're close but not exactly. (I googled it afterwards may be the answer was
engine.) Then he said it's ok and moved to next section.

Then he started questions based on my resume. He asked me, Let's say from the projects you've mentioned
in your resume you have to design one project from scratch how will you do ?? and what extra features you
will add? I chose my E -commerce project, I will first find out the critical and non -critical tasks. Then I will
design the database and then I will decide which database to use (SQL/NOSQL). Then I will decide the
TechStack. After that I'll start coding and then I will think of optimizing as my priority will be achieving the
required functionality.

Then he asked me to explain the project of one of my Internships (I had done 2 internships). Then he asked
me questions like why did you chose this TechStack? What improvements you can do ? How can you scale
and optimize it?

Then he asked me If I am familiar with Machine Learning?
I told that my Major project is in the field of NLP and in previous semester I had Machine Learning subject
so I've idea about it. Then he told me to explain my Major Project and asked questions on that.

After this he gave me one DSA based question. [question link attaching below].
I was able to answer this question but my approach was taking o(n) time. He asked me to optimize it to O(n/2).
I asked him if he can give any hint and he gave me one hint I told him another approach based on hint but then
again it was not covering all test cases and I got stressed and confuse at that time(please don't to this as this
can affect your performance and thinking ability) and was not able to give optimize answer. Interviewer was
so polite he said it's ok I am not expecting you to code it right now as we were discussing all on Notepad.

At this point he was done asking questions and asked If I've any questions for him (Please ask 1-2 question)
i)I asked what does exactly Edra Labs do ? ( As there was no much information about them online because
they started just 8 months back)
ii)I asked if he can brief me on the projects he worked ? (Here I got to know that they're also working on the
NLP projects and that's why he got interested when I mentioned about my major Project in NLP domain I feel
it helped me.)

After interview was done I was on phone call with my friend who was also in the process and had interview
around scheduled explaining about my interview and I remember telling him yaar mera selection nhi hoga as
I was not able to optimize the answer to O(n/2). During the call I got to know someone is calling but I thought
it could be one of my friend but then second time when I looked who is calling it was call from the Edra Labs
so I picked it up and then hopefully I was selected for next round which was scheduled around 6:15.

So don't loose hope !!
This is the list of questions I got one day before my interview from previous experiences that were available
online and most of the questions were same so please refer this and the DSA question I mentioned above is
also in this list ( integer range ke related hai).
Second Round Questions

4.  Technical Interview [Around 3-4 candidates were shortlisted]

Interview started with interviewer introducing himself. He was senior Data engineer at Edra Labs.  Then he
asked me to introduce myself.
Then he asked me about the project that I did in my recent internship. After this he asked me to open the code
that I written for the machine coding round. And he told me to explain the code line by line and he caught one
of the mistake in my code it was not mistake in logic but it actually happened from my end while commenting
the code during optimizing it during machine coding round. By mistake I commented the important line of
code which was to ensure thread safety. Then he asked me what will happened If  parallel requests come to
that API endpoint. I told him theoretically but then he asked me to code it. Honestly I had no idea about
sending parallel requests, at first I literally opened my application in two browsers and I myself got to know
that this is completely wrong. Then I told him that I can write one script and I'll create two threads to send
request to that API endpoint. He told me to write it as I was not sure I asked him if I can take help from internet
he gave the permission. I found 1-2 solutions and I tried copying it as most of the time our approach  is let's
copy first and then see what errors we're facing and then resolve. Then he asked me in between do you know
what this code is exactly doing? I said not exactly but I feel it might be the solution. Then he said if you don't
know anything exactly why are you just blindly copy pasting it and at this point I just lost all my hope thinking
I've made very bad impression. Then he said it's ok I was not expecting you to write working code can you
tell me about what and how much do you know about threads in general. And then I explained everything
about threads like why threads? what is multithreading? What is deadlock? What is mutual exclusion? What
is thread safety? etc,etc. And he was satisfied with all my answers.
Then he asked me about my Major project and interview was done he asked If I have any questions for him.
I asked  same questions about Edra Labs ,their vision and ongoing projects.

around 7:10 I again got call that I've my HR round scheduled at 7:15 which was unexpected !!

IDFC visited around the end of July, conducting their PPT between the 25th and 27th. It was announced that
the recruitment process would include:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Two Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

However, due to the tough decision of selecting between the final eight HR candidates, two additional
technical rounds were conducted with higher technical positions and a Senior Managing Director. In total,
there were six rounds:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Four Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

Round 0 - Online Assessment (160 Candidates)

Over 160 students appeared for the online Assessment. The test was online but was strictly proctored via
camera,microphone, etc on hirepro. The test had three sections: section 1 Aptitude and data interpretation,
section 2 was SQL+Excel + Computer Fundamentals+Math and section three was DSA. Each section was
separately timed and the test was overall 90 mins. First two sections got locked after 45-50 mins and the
remaining time was for coding questions.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The coding section was pretty easy. The two questions asked were:
Question 1 was similar to this :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/find-duplicates-in-an-array/1?itm_source=geeksforgeeks&itm_me
dium=article&itm_campaign=practice_card
Question 2 was similar to this:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/check-if-a-number-is-palindrome/

2. Round 1: Technical Round 1 35-40 students |

This round was all about my resume and the projects I have done. The interviewer took one of the projects
and scaled it to a large level and told me to tell how I would handle the project at such a large scale and also
asked me questions about dev ops because it was on my resume. I was slightly grilled due to my lack of
experience in frontend development but I covered it by convincing the interviewer about my backend and
dev ops skills. It is advised to always keep a smile on your face and have confidence while speaking. If you
don't understand the question do not hesitate to ask the interviewer to repeat it. The round went on for 40-45
mins and was taken after the lunch break.

3. Round 2: Technical Round 2 [12-15 Students]

After my round 1 some applicants were giving round 3 and as I was slightly grilled I thought I was not
getting past round 1 but I was shortlisted for round 2. So never lose hope even though you were grilled
you will get shortlisted. Round 2 was very calm and the interviewer asked me to explain my projects in
depth and asked me about some libraries which were used in them. In short IDFC needs a developer and
they intend to find one via their resume and their experiences. So be very clear about your resume even
though you have lied on the resume make sure you do that concept before the interview.

4. Round 3: HR Round [8 Students]

The HR round was taken online on microsoft teams. In this round I was asked to give my introduction now
in the HR round do not make your intro too technical. After that I was asked about my family
background so I told them about how both my mom and dad are from the commerce field and their
dream was to work in a bank and my dream is to become a software engineer and how IDFC is bringing

IDFC visited around the end of July, conducting their PPT between the 25th and 27th. It was announced that
the recruitment process would include:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Two Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

However, due to the tough decision of selecting between the final eight HR candidates, two additional
technical rounds were conducted with higher technical positions and a Senior Managing Director. In total,
there were six rounds:

1. One Online Assessment (OA)

2. Four Technical Rounds

3. One HR Round

1.
Hechnical Round 1] [ around 36 students appeared this round]
This round was one of the main rounds of the process, lasting around 40-50 minutes. It focused primarily on
my resume, core knowledge, and problem-solving approach. The flow of the interview was as follows:
--- PAGE 2 ---

1. Introduction and Skills:

• The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and outline my skills.

• Based on my introduction, he chose my main programming language (C++) and asked

questions about its concepts, such as pointers, virtual tables, OOP in C++, and the reasons for
choosing C++.
o Despite being more familiar with Java, the interviewer had a solid understanding of C++.

2. OOP Concepts:

• He asked about polymorphism, the reasons for using polymorphism, multiple inheritance, and

its availability in both Java and C++.

• I answered smartly, explaining the concept and the diamond problem associated with multiple

inheritance, which demonstrated my strong foundational knowledge.

3. Project-Based Questions:

• The interviewer inquired about one of my projects, specifically the stock data analysis project

using Kafka and AWS services.
o Questions included why I made the project, its purpose, how it works, and the technologies
used.

• He asked me to explain the project's step-by-step process and architecture.

4. DSA and Real-Life Scenarios:

• The interviewer presented real-life scenarios and asked how I would solve them or which

data structures I would use for efficient solutions.

• There was also a question that you know sql stores data in form of tables, So in physical

memory will that be in tabular format only or how is it stored and retrieved.
Throughout the interview, he emphasized the importance of understanding how things work on a physical
level, such as data storage on databases and hard disks, rather than just knowing the concepts superficially.
Pro-Tip: It's crucial to handle questions you're unsure about effectively. Instead of simply saying "I don't
know," try to relate the topic to something familiar. For example, you can say, "I am not sure/unaware about
this, but as I can relate this to certain CS fundamental concepts, it could be this or that." Moreover, you can
ask the interviewer for help if you're unable to recall something.

2. [Technical Round 2] [ 12 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was more of a technical + HR kind of round. It was pretty relaxed, and the interviewer was very
friendly. Here is a breakdown of the interview:

1. Introduction and Background:

o The interviewer asked me to introduce myself.

• He inquired about my background, specifically how I, being from Jammu, chose to come this

far for my education.

2. Resume Grilling:

• The interviewer asked about my internship, requesting a brief summary of what I did during

that time, how I got the internship, and what benefits I gained from it.
--- PAGE 3 ---

• He asked about my projects and various tools mentioned in my resume, such as Postman and

Docker.

• For Postman, he asked me to explain its usage, what it does, the protocols involved, the

differences between GET and POST requests, what the requests look like, and other related
concepts.
The purpose was to verify that my resume was accurate and to check my conceptual knowledge. This part of
the interview lasted about 20-30 minutes.
Pro-Tip:

• Be calm and do not lie on your resume.

• In your introduction, emphasize the topics you are well-prepared for, as future questions will likely

be based on this.

• If you are not fully prepared about something, remove it from your resume or avoid mentioning it in

your introduction.

3. [HR round] [ 8 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was like a typical HR round. The interviewer asked me to introduce myself but then suddenly
stopped me and gave me around 10 questions to be answered in my introduction, such as:

• Where are you trom?

• Your schooling background

• Your grades

• The games you play

• Extracurricular activities

It was a bit confusing at the time, but I tried to stay calm and answer the questions appropriately. I managed
to answer most of them but forgot a few, so I asked the interviewer what else he needed to know.
Here is how the rest of the interview went:

1. Games and Interests:

• He asked which games I play. I mentioned that I used to play basketball but later got into

online games and now focus on coding.

• He then asked about online games and how I would make or structure a game like PUBG.

• I explained that games are developed on Unreal Engine, which I haven't used, but I

described the basic flow: first, creating the action figures, relating everything to
classes and objects with certain values and methods, and making the arena a real-time
collaborative environment.

2. HR Questions:

• Three strengths and three weaknesses: I ensured my answers were professional and aligned

with the company's needs and my strengths.

• Where do you see yourself in the next five years? Another typical HR question that I

answered thoughtfully.
--- PAGE 4 ---
The interview was conducted online and lasted about 20-30 minutes. My key advice for such rounds is to be
friendly with the interviewer, stay calm, and handle questions effectively.

4. [Technical round 3] [ 8 candidates appeared this round]

This round was not initially planned. Interviews were completed, and the results were supposed to be
announced that night. However, the next day, we received a notification about an additional round. The 8
selected candidates were among the best in the college, and the company initially intended to recruit 5-6
candidates based on their HR head's discussion with the TPO. Since they couldn't decide, they conducted
one more round to finalize the selections.
This additional round was taken by their senior manager to test our technical skills rigorously. It involved an
in-depth grilling on our concepts and projects. Here's how it went:

1. Primary Language Focus:

• The interviewer emphasized my primary language (C++) and asked deep questions about its

concepts such as pointers, memory addresses, virtual tables, template classes, etc.

• I handled this well due to my strong knowledge of C++.

2. Secondary Language:

• He then asked for my second language, which I mentioned was Java.

• He asked about the difference between generics in Java and templates in C++. I couldn't

answer this as I wasn't deeply familiar with Java, but it worked out fine.

3. Project Questions:

o He asked why I chose my projects and what problems they solved.
o Questions on React and JavaScript were also posed, including why I preferred that tech stack.

4. Final Question:

• The last question was why they should prefer me over others. Instead of saying I am better, I

highlighted my strengths and aligned my answer with the job description.

5. [Technical Round 41 [ 8 candidates appeared for this round too ]

This round was conducted by their senior Managing Director (MD) and focused more on technical
knowledge and problem-solving approach. The atmosphere was quite relaxed. Here is a breakdown of the
interview:

1. Introduction and Final Year Project:

• The interviewer asked me to introduce myself.

• As I am currently in my 4th year, he inquired about my major final year project. I mentioned

that I was using a Large Language Model (LLM) in my project.

• He then asked how I would solve the problem if there was no LLM available.

2. Data Structures and Algorithms:

• The interviewer moved on to a DSA problem and asked which data structure I would use to

solve it.

• I explained that I would use a TRIE and illustrated the basic structure on OneNote.

3. HR Question:

• He concluded the interview with a single HR-type question.

--- PAGE 5 ---
The interview lasted about 15 minutes.
Finally, after all these rounds, all 8 students were selected for the Application Engineer position.
Tip: Give mock interviews and practice interviews with your friends. This will help you be prepared for
anything that can be asked in an interview.

The company first conducted a pre-placement talk, which was followed by an online assessment 2 days later.
After that 3 interview rounds were conducted on 30 July followed by 2 interview rounds later.

1. Online Assessment [ 167 students appeared for this round]

The test consisted of 3 sections and each section had a time limit. The first section had 15 questions and was
aptitude based wherein general questions on logical reasoning were asked. The second section had 20
technical questions based on Programming, Excel, SQL and Basic Statistics. The third section had 2 coding
questions which were very easy.

1. Check whether given number is positive and a palindrome

2. For a given array of integers, find an output array which contains the AND operation of every integer

in the original array. After this check whether elements in the new array are repeated.
I fell short of time in the aptitude section, however the technical section went very well for me and I was
able to solve both of the coding problems. I would suggest focusing on the technical part more especially for
the test. I referred to articles on GFG and interviewbit for the topics mentioned.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 38 students appeared for this round]

The interviewer first asked me to introduce myself and elaborate on my college experience. He asked me to
tell about a positive and a negative experience. He then asked me a few questions on a project mentioned in
my resume. He gave some situations and how I would manage them in my project. I had ML projects in my
resume so he questioned about the accuracy mentioned and how I achieved that, the model used, etc. I had
mentioned python as my primary programming language so he then asked questions on python such as
Walrus operator, swapcase function, what does pass do, exception handling in python, docstring, slicing in
python, concatenations, variable types, etc.
(For this part, I would suggest referring to the GFG article on "python most asked interview questions", a
lot of the questions were mentioned in the article. I couldn't answer all of the questions and just told him
that I had not worked previously with this and so did not know about this however I think it is similar to this
thing I worked with. It's okay if you don't know the answer to a question just be honest with the
interviewer.)
--- PAGE 2 ---
He then asked me a few questions on numpy and pandas as I had mentioned them in my resume. He then
gave me a situation where I had to build a food service app and asked me to build a schema of the app and
what considerations I will take while building the app. He then asked me how I would handle excess traffic
on the app. I told him about nginx and how I used it in a project before. He then asked me what architecture
I would use to build the app and to explain the architecture. I asked him if he was referring to MVC to which
he said yes and then I went on to explain to him what MVC is and how different components work together.
He then asked me why I chose python and not Java. He then asked me a few questions on Java based on
syntax and then asked why is Java more used and what are the benefits of Java. He then asked me about the
4 pillars of OOPS and asked me to give applications for 2 of them. He then asked me a few questions on
DBMS. He then asked me about another project I had mentioned in my resume and asked as to why I had
implemented it in a certain way and what is the future scope for it. I explained to him the entire process of
that project and he seemed very interested in it. At the end, I asked him a question regarding the ML used in
features in IDFC and he went on to explain how they use it in various applications. The interview lasted for
around 40-50 minutes.
(Firstly, I would suggest being honest on your resume and making sure you know about everything in your
resume. Try to list projects which are a bit innovative/different and have some unique features. Read up on
your projects before the interview and make sure to know every detail about it/how it is implemented
because they will try to test you majorly on your knowledge on various aspects of the projects.)

3. Technical Round 2[12 students appeared for this round]

The interviewer first asked me to introduce myself and then asked me what skills I was planning to learn in
my remaining year of college and how I would go about learning them. He then asked me the reason for
choosing AI/ML and not going for Comps. I was upfront about it and told him I had no idea about the course
while joining and it was the best I could get based on my percentile. He then asked me about a project and
why I chose it. Then he gave me various scenarios wherein he tried to complicate things and asked me
questions as to how I would solve them. I had a project based on LLMs so then he asked me about my
understanding of LLMs and how they work/function. He then asked me if I had to make a project which
would solve a large-scale problem in India utilizing my current skills, what would I make. I told him about
an app designed for women's safety that I was familiar with. He then asked me to suggest improvements and
if I had limited resources, how would I optimize the app and track well-lit areas. He gave me hints which
helped me arrive at the solution. He then asked me how I would go about implementing some specified
features. He then asked if I had any questions for him and I asked him a similar question that I had asked in
the previous round. He explained on a deeper level how various factors at IDFC work. This round lasted
about 25-30 mins
(What I felt from talking with some fellow interviewees was that they were asking questions based on the
answers given. So be honest and ask for hints if you cannot think of something and explain whatever idea
comes to mind.)

4. a) HR Round [ 8 students appeared for this round ]

This was an online round. The panelists first asked me how I was finding the process and how I felt in the
earlier interview rounds and who had interviewed me earlier. They then asked me to introduce myself and
tell them about my family background, hobbies, etc. The next question was what I knew about IDFC Bank
and what I thought was unique in the bank. They then asked me to elaborate on one of my projects, what
was an experience I gained from it and how I used ML in it. They asked me if I had ever faced a conflict in
--- PAGE 3 ---
my team and how did I resolve it. They then asked me to list 3 of my weaknesses and strengths. The last
question was why should they hire me and what unique qualities did I have. They then asked me if I had any
questions. The interview lasted for about 15-20 minutes.
(Do not forget to ask the interviewer their name after every interview as it might be brought up in HR
rounds. Read up about IDFC bank in advance and note some pointers/take screenshots in the pre-placement
talk when they talk about their vision and values. Prepare sample HR questions and rehearse their answers
beforehand. The ones asked to me were very basic HR questions which I had prepared beforehand and I
advise you to do the same. In weaknesses talk about how you have a weakness which you are improving
on.)
IDFC first planned on selecting 5-6 students however later they wanted to hire all 8 students and therefore
conducted 2 more virtual interviews in the coming days.
b) Techno HR Round [ 8 students appeared for this round]
The interviewer was a senior manager in the company. He began by asking me for my introduction and as I
from it. He asked me what I knew about IDFC. He then asked me what I had studied in college apart from
normalization is used and if I could list all forms and apply it in a real life example. He then asked me to
explain the 4 pillars of OOPS and give an example where OOPS can be used in a real life application. He
asked me some questions on Operating Systems and what is virtual memory and why do we have virtual
memory, etc. He then asked me why Python and not Java and asked the benefits and drawbacks of both
Python and Java. He then asked me if I knew about red-black trees which I did not know about and told him
so. He then asked me to explain to him how a BST works and how BSTs work when alphabets are involved.
He then asked me to list how BST can be applied with an example. He again asked me why they should hire
me and what unique qualities I have that made me stand out. He then asked if I had any questions to which I
asked him his role and what a day looks like in his life. He explained what his exact role was and the
responsibilities he has. This round lasted for around 20 minutes.
(Practice CS fundamentals thoroughly approximately a month or 2 before the placement season. I referred
one shot videos on youtube and tried to solve mcqs on different sites. DBMS & SQL > OOPS > OS > CCN
in that order)
c) Technical Round - 3[8 students appeared for this round]
The interview was conducted by 2 senior developers of the company. They first introduced themselves and
asked me to introduce myself. They then asked me to explain a project I had done and the tech stack used.
They then asked me why C or C++ have a lower execution time than python and if python was an
interpreted or compiled language and why did I prefer python. I answered the same as earlier rounds as it
has more support for ML and DS and has a lot of libraries and is easy to read and understand. They asked a
few more questions based on my resume and then asked application based questions on DSA. They asked
me how would I implement forward and back buttons in chrome, how would I implement panels in Netflix
and how can I implement contact searching. On naming a data structure he then asked more detailed
questions and how it works, etc. I asked them the same questions as the last round and they were very
friendly in replying and interacting overall.
8 students received the offer.
--- PAGE 4 ---

1. Coding Test:

This was conducted on the HirePro platform. It consisted of 15 aptitude questions, 20 technical questions
(SQL, MS Excel, Programming Basics, and Basic Statistics) and 2 coding questions (Both Easy) -

- Question 1: Given an array of numbers and a value k, we first had to find the corresponding AND

array by getting arr[i]&k for every element in the array and then

- Question 2: Given an array of stocks, each stock was represented by a number and the person will

buy the stock if that stock is palindrome and non negative so print yes else print no.
Eg:- stock = [121, -11, 23], output = Yes, No, No
I was able to solve both the coding questions but my aptitude didn't go as well but the technical questions
went well.

2. Technical Round 1: [38 students appeared]

This round lasted around 50 minutes to an hour. My interview was online, and it began with a short
introduction and from there the interviewer asked me some situational questions on React.js as that was my
primary skill. After this he asked me to explain the OOP concept and the 4 pillars along with the question on
why multiple inheritance is not possible in java using classes and how we will implement it using interfaces.
Then he asked me about try catch and why we use it. After this he asked me to explain authentication and
authorization. I explained with the example of a login page and then for authorization I explained JWT
tokens and how we use middleware for auth. Then he said what if we have dynamic user roles and we want
authentication for each role (Eg user1 should not be able to use user2 apis and user2 should not be able to
use user3 apis and so on) I answered by saying that since we have their roles in the Database we can include
user role in the token and for every api we will check in the middleware if the appropriate user is accessing
that api. After this he moved on to DSA, only my panelist was asking DSA questions. They were the
following -

- Given a linked list and two variables m and n, you have to delete n nodes after every m nodes. I

explained using two pointers and keep in mind the edge cases as well when m and n can be null.

- The second question - Valid Parentheses

At the end he asked me a simple aptitude question where I had to find the angle between the hour and
minute hand when the time is 1:30 (135 degree).
--- PAGE 2 ---
Tip: Remember to stay calm and answer the question with examples like when explaining abstraction you
can give an example of abstract class car and an abstract method engine (since every car will have its own
implementation of engine). Also whenever you want some time just ask the interviewer that you need some
time to think it's completely fine and while solving DSA questions keep talking about what you are trying to
do and while writing the code explain the interviewer as you write the code.

3. Technical Round 2: [ 12 students appeared ]

This round was offline and lasted around 30 - 35 minutes. The interviewer began by asking for an
introduction and then he asked me questions about my freelance project which I was working on and asked
why that particular tech stack. I was using MySQL there so he started asking questions about that, like how
are you using Node.js to run SQL queries, how many connections can you keep, are you re creating the
connections for every query or you have established one connection and keep it as it is. He grilled me quite a
bit here but I was able to answer decently. Then he asked about my second work experience and then some
questions about it as well like what was my contribution there etc. Then he said that he was satisfied and got
everything so the interview was done. This scared me a bit since the person before me was interviewed for
more than an hour. So I asked if he had any feedback for me. He said they give the feedback to HR and
based on feedback of every interview they decide if they want to proceed with the candidate but he told me
not to worry as he was happy with the interview. Another question I asked was about the crowdstrike issue
and if that affected the bank.
Tip: Keep a smile on your face throughout the interview. The interviewers are very friendly and you just
need to show them that you know everything that is on your resume.

4. HR Round: [ 8 students appeared ]

This round was online and lasted for 30 - 40 minutes. There were two HR's and they started by asking how
my day has been up till now. Then they asked me to introduce myself followed by questions like what is my
family background, what are my hobbies, what I do for fun, which was the last book I read and what lesson I

1. Resume Shortlisting [All candidates appeared]

The initial stage involved a resume shortlisting process where many candidates submitted their
resumes. The criteria focused on academic performance, relevant projects, internships, and
extracurricular activities. Out of these, 123 candidates were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Aptitude Round Online

• a) Basic Aptitude (25 mins) (26 July 2pm)

The aptitude test covered topics such as probability, work-rate problems, and other standard
quantitative questions. Resources like IndiaBix were helpful for preparation. Out of the 123, 57
candidates were shortlisted for the next Online test that happened around 1 hr later.
b) CS Fundamentals (35 mins)
This section included:

• 4 questions on input-output and basic data structures and algorithms (DSA), focusing on

Java-specific concepts.

• 6 questions on SQL, mostly at an easy level.

After this round, 38 candidates were further shortlisted.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Round 1 Interview [38 candidates appeared]

The first interview round was comprehensive, covering various aspects:

• Introduction and Projects:

• The interview started with the common question, "Tell me about yourself."

• A brief discussion followed on my data analytics project using Python, where I

explained the basic concept and what I did.

• Technical Questions:

• DSA Question 1: Given a sentence as a string, reverse each word and capitalize

the first letter. I proposed two approaches: one using a trimming function and loop
for reversing, and another using the split function in Java.

• DSA Question 2: Input a binary array and count the maximum number of swaps

of Os to make the final array have no consecutive ones. I suggested a brute force
O(n) solution using a simple for loop and checking neighboring values.

• SQL Queries:

• Print details of the student with the highest marks (using subqueries and aggregate

functions).

• Print the top 3 students based on marks (using ORDER BY with LIMIT or

correlated subqueries).

• Print the top 3 students based on marks in each division (using the

DENSE_RANKO window function with PARTITION BY).
They shortlisted 4 students from this round, skipping the second technical round, which was
unusual compared to previous years.

4. HR Round

• The HR interview focused on behavioral and situational questions:

• What do you know about EDS?

• Why do you want to be a part of us?

o How is the process going?
o How many other companies have you applied to before this?
o Are you aware of the role and responsibilities?

• Describe a situation where nobody praised you, and you were on your own.

• Describe a situation where you manage time well.

• Where do you live? (I live in Bhandup, and the company is in Malad with timings

2-11 pm)

• How will you travel? (I said by bike, but she suggested it might be better if I shift

closer, which I said I would consider)
Final Offers: 4 students were offered the job.
--- PAGE 3 ---

1. Online Assessment (61 students shortlisted for the OA)

This was an online assessment consisting of 4 sections conducted on Mettl Tests platform. The duration of the
entire assessment was 45 minutes.

1. SQL based MCQs (10 questions): Some general questions on SQL basics, queries, syntax etc.

2. Computer Fundamentals (10 questions): Mainly OOPs questions of easy difficulty

3. Simple Coding Problem: kth Maximum number in an array

4. Advanced Coding Problem: Longest Common Subsequence

The SQL MCQs were mostly easy/medium although some of the SQL problems were a bit tricky. OOPs
questions were pretty standard ones. Practicing MCQs on online platforms such as GFG was sufficient. I was
able to solve both the Coding problems while having spared time for the MCQs as well. The entire test was
only of 45 minutes however, so speed was key.

2. Tech Interview 1 (19 students appeared for the Interviews)

The interview is mainly about your resume and listed projects/internships. Expect question s based on
programming languages, SQL, questions on core computer subjects DBMS, OOPs, CCN and OS. I was also
asked questions on Python and Python libraries. List vs Arrays vs Tuples, explain the Pandas data frame,
NumPy arrays etc.  These questions are also dependent on the skills mentioned on the resume which is useful
to keep in mind. The round lasted for about 30-35 minutes.

3. Tech Interview 2

The interview started off with 'Tell me about yourself'. Following which I was told to write some SQL queries.
One of the problems were about a transaction table with used_id, date, security_id and the goal was to write a
query to retrieve the security_id and date which had the maximum transactions for that particular security_id.
After providing a solution to the above problem in SQL, I was asked to code for the same problem in any
preferred language and I was able to do the same. This duration of this round was about 40-45 minutes.

4. HR Interview

The HR round was pretty relaxed and light. It started off with where I was from, my interests, hobbies etc.
Rest of the questions were pretty typical HR questions such as 'Strengths/Weaknesses', 'Which was the most
challenging project and the learnings from it', 'Do you have any plans for masters?' etc.
I was asked whether I had any questions for the interviewer and I proceeded to inquire about the different
tools and tech stacks used, the training program for freshers and about the internship. It's good to ask these
questions since it shows your enthusiasm and curiosity about the role while also clearing your own doubts in
the process.
Finally, 3 students including me received the offer :)

1. One thing I realized during the entire placement process is that the companies are focusing more on

projects and core subjects and not just DSA. I would suggest you have 2-3 good and unique projects
that can highlight your skills.

2. Make sure all your projects are working and include everything you mention in the resume as some

interviewers may ask you to show a working demo of it.

3. Be through and honest with your resume and tailor it according to company requirements.

4. Do not neglect aptitude as it is as important as DSA. Most of the companies have an aptitude section

in their OA and it can be a game changer. (My biggest mistake was to neglect aptitude and focus
more on DSA skills).

5. For DSA I would recommend solving any sheet to get your basics clear. Later you can practice on

any platform like leetcode or codechef. Personally I would recommend exploring CP although it is
not required for on-campus placements but can help you if you are applying off-campus.

6. My last advice would be that don't get upset due to rejections as they are part of the placement

process and believe me luck really matters. So even if you get rejected after giving your best don't be
disappointed and put your focus on what's to come next.
