The entire process consisted of 3 rounds :

1. Technical Test

2. Technical Interview

3. Techno HR round

1. Technical Test [138 appeared for this round]

The test consisted of technical MCQs, 1 coding question and 1 SQL query with a time limit of 90 minutes.
MCQ section consisted of 12 questions which were based on core subjects and guess the output type of
questions. For this section I would recommend going through GFG guess the output questions (language
specific). Important thing to note is that each question has different weightage so make sure you solve
questions with more weightage correctly.
The coding question was a medium difficulty question and was based on string. The question was on a
constructive side rather than requiring any kind of data structure or algorithm to be solved. I was able to pass
all test cases.
Link to Question:https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
SQL query was a very basic one and included only one table.

2. Technical Round [ 34 students appeared for this round]

Students who correctly solved the MCQ section and were at least able to solve coding question partially
were shortlisted for this round.
--- PAGE 2 ---
This was a pure technical round. The interview started with the interviewer introducing himself after
which he asked for my introduction. Make sure you have a precise and concise introduction (aleast 30
seconds and specific to the role).
The interview proceeded with the interviewer asking me for one of my favorite projects. Since I had
worked on a College Portal in my 4th semester, he asked me how I would go on restructuring the entire
project if I were to start it from scratch. He then asked me to explain and draw the architecture of the
system and how I would improve the performance of the system.
I explained that we can deploy load balancer to distribute the incoming traffic across multiple servers
and create a cluster of databases to increase reliability. However he did not seem satisfied with my
answer and said that this won't improve the performance of the system in terms of response time. I later
provided him with a caching and message broker solution which he approved and we discussed it for
about 20 minutes.
Later he asked me how I would decide on the tech stack for this project. Since I had developed this
project using MERN he asked to choose different tech stack and reason for choosing specific technology.
After deciding the tech stack he asked how and which design principles I would use in my project.
Since I wasn't completely aware about all the design principles, I explained about which I was familiar
with. The interview ended with him asking me if I had any questions. I asked him about his role and how
would he utilize my skills if I were to work in his team. Make sure you ask questions at the end of
interview as it shows your interest in the company and the role.
The interview lasted for around 1hr 15 minutes.

3. Techno HR round [22 students appeared for this round]

For some students this was a technical+HR round and for some just HR round.
The interview started with the interviewer asking for my introduction. After which he asked me if I had
worked on any project that was used in real-life. Since I was part of IPL auction (Oculus) tech team I
explained to him about the application which was used on the day of the event. He asked to list 5-6
limitations of our applications and the solutions to overcome them. We talked about this for about 30
minutes. Later he asked me some scenario based questions like for example if my team leader asked me
to work on the latest requirement by the client without providing any concrete information, how would I
deal with the situation. Later he added that if the work was humanly impossible to do within a given time
how would I deal with this situation. I told him that in this case I would be honest with the client and tell
them what he/she should expect till the deadline. Through this I was able to highlight one of the barclays
core value which is Integrity. Make sure when answering such question you try to incorporate the core
values of the company. He kept on asking me scenario based questions for the next 25-30 minutes. The
interview ended with him asking me if I had any questions. I asked him about Barclays cloud platform
and why they prefer their own cloud platform and not any other public cloud service like AWS.

4. PRANK round

All the interviews for round 2 finished around 5:30 pm and all were eagerly waiting for the final
results. Later we came to know that there would be another round and were asked to assemble in the
conference room. They said that it would take another 2 hours for the entire process to conclude as they had
decided to take another round and asked us if we were comfortable with staying in college till late night.
--- PAGE 3 ---
They started calling out our name one by one after which they said that we all have been selected and there
won't be any further rounds. Everyone in the room was relieved and happy .
Total 19 grads were selected for full time role.

Placement process consisted of 3 rounds. Online test (Test was to be taken from college only)  and  2 Interview
Rounds .

1. Online Test  :  [ No of candidates who appeared for this round  were 138 ]

The Online test was of 1hr 30 minutes .  It consisted of cs fundamentals mcq (variable marks), a 10 marks
sql query and a 50 marks coding question .The coding question was about string generation similar to this:
https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
SQL was basic group by and order by  query where we had to group by according to a month . Make sure to
practice SQL of date and months questions.
I was able to solve 10 / 10 test cases ,  SQL and MCQS.

2. [Round 2 : Tech ] [ 34 students got shortlisted ]

Before the interview rounds, a Pre-Placement Talk was conducted .
The average duration of round 2 was 40-45 minutes.
My interviewer was Assistant Vice President ( Java Developer ) .
My interview started with a fun question: "Tell me something cool about yourself." After that, the interviewer
asked about my core strengths. Following this, they inquired about my Computer Science minor course, the
subjects it covered .
( All this are Trick questions so answer honestly and give proper reasoning for your answer  . )
Next, he asked me to explain my first two projects in depth and my specific role in them, especially if they
were group projects. I had worked on projects using both the MERN stack and Spring Boot, so he asked why
I chose two different tech stacks and which one I would prefer if given a choice, along with my reasoning.
We then shifted to Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA). First, he asked me about pointers and gave me a
task to write a code that adds two numbers using pointers. He also inquired why Java doesn't support pointers.
Afterward, he asked which data structure I like the most, and I answered "stacks and queues." He then asked
me to explain both data structures and give real -life examples where they are used. Finally, he asked if there
was any data structure or algorithm I didn't particularly like. I replied that while I don't dislike any, if I had to
prioritize, sorting algorithms would rank the lowest  . Following this, he asked me to write the code for the
Insertion Sort algorithm, explain it with a test case, and discuss its time and space complexity. We then moved
on to discussing other algorithms, their respective time and space complexities, and the scenarios where each
algorithm is most appropriate to use .
Later, he posed a thought-provoking question: " With AI/ML advancements today, why is there still a need for
software development engineers like us?" I answered  , and he seemed impressed with my response, even
appreciating how I presented it .
He then asked why I chose Electronics and Telecommunications (EXTC) as my major when I was clearly
interested in Computer Science. He further asked why I didn't opt for Computer Science (CS) directly.
He then asked me about my extracurricular activities, such as hackathons, case study competitions, and my
hobbies.
Towards the end , he asked the common interview question: "Why should I hire you over others?" Afterward,
he gave me the chance to ask him any questions. I made sure to ask questions that would genuinely interest
him and avoid questions like one my friend had asked about the Barclays logo and what it signifies, to which
they had no answer. So, I would advise avoiding such questions.

3. [Round 3 : HR] [ No of candidates who appeared for this round were 21 ]

Round 3 lasted for 20 minutes.
The interview began with the usual "Introduce yourself" question. After that, she presented me with a
situational question: "Let's say you are part of a team, and your manager consistently makes wrong
decisions for the team. What would you do?" I responded with multiple approaches, but she kept adding
new aspects to the scenario, testing whether I aligned with their company's values (RISES).
The second question was about smart work versus hard work. She asked, "If given the choice between
doing smart work and hard work, which would you choose and why?" I explained my reasoning for both.
The third question was a bit more personal--she asked me to convince her that I hadn't chosen Computer
Science for the high-paying jobs, but rather out of genuine interest and passion for the field.
With that, my interview concluded.
(Some of my friends were also asked technical questions, so it really depends on your panel and your
performance in previous rounds.)

4. Round 3 (PRANK round)

We all interns + grads were told to sit in the conference room except few. Then we were told that now
they will be calling out a few names who will not be selected for further process and have to leave the
conference room immediately. Everyone was very tensed. Then they told this was a PRANK and all of
you have been selected !!!!!

A total of 19 grads were selected!!

journey.howSecured:
Barclays came on campus (7 CGPA and above) after hiring candidates from Hackathon and Cyber -
Shaala on 11th September, for the Online Assessment.
The process was : Online Assessment, Technical Round, Technical + HR round, PRANK Round
NOTE: PPT was held for the OA shortlists, the interviewers introduced themselves before the
interviews. If anything like this happens do note the interviewer's names and any crucial info as this
proved to be a massive help for me in round 2!
NOTE 2: Barclays and its RISES principles, these both go really hand in hand, try to relate your
work, your projects, your values to HR questions in a way that shows that you have integrated the
RISES principles without being way too obvious

1. [Online Assessment] [ 138 candidates appeared for this round ] - 11th September

This is a very crucial round as the majority of the elimination happened in this round. But the
questions were relatively doable. The section consisted of 12 MCQ's (40 -60 mks), 1 SQL EASY

(20mks) question and a Leetcode medium - Hard difficulty coding question (50 mks). The MCQ's

were allotted a GOOD chunk of marks some were, so be wary of that as well. They consisted of
mainly
6-7 output based questions (Pseudocode, Java code, CPP codes)
2-3 DBMS based questions (joins, DML, DDL operation types and SQL query related) Couple of
DSA based MCQ's
You need to have a strong hold on Java (basic knowledge of syntax and some concepts will also do),
DBMS, SQL and DSA to clear this round
The SQL query question was where we were supposed to simply use where clause and basic logic
used in EASY questions to get the required output
The coding question was on String Generation where
Given a string St of length L1 consisting of Latin uppercase alphabets only and a string 52 of length
12 consisting of characters 7 and F's only.
Generate a lexicographically smallest string S of length (L1+L2-1) such that a substring of length
L1 in string S starting Index (0 <i< L2) is equal to ST if and only if i element of 52 is 'T (without
quotes) else not.
Find the lexicographically smallest string S which satisfies the given condition.
I passed all the testcases of this question. What helped in my case is I completed my MCQ's in very
less time so I could give more time on coding, keep note of this. Also as mentioned the MCQ's
weighed a lot, so take care of that as well as many people were able to clear this round by just passing
5-8 cases as well by performing good with the MCQ's

2. [Technical Round 1] [ 34 candidates who appeared for this round ] - 12th September

(After round 1, I was hopeful for round 2 as the coding q was not completely passed by many people
so I got a head start for preparing for my interviews, many people who got shortlisted in the end didn't
think they would be, so don't do that mistake, any preparation you do will be useful somewhere or the
other.)
This Interview spanned about 40-45 minutes.
Don't be nervous as that could be your downfall. Students were divided into 9 panels and the interview
process started at 11:30. My interview was 3rd in my panel so I made sure to keep myself mentally
prepared and focused as well as talking to my classmate s which made me much less anxious. I got to
know my interviewer's name quite a while before my interview so I was prepared for the same.
Interview started with some slow paced Yes/No questions on my resume which was done to test my
patience and to control the pace of the interview (at such times just keep your cool and try to be
elaborative with your answers irrespective of them being Yes/No).
Then came intership's experience based questions in which basic things like overview of the work and
accomplishments were being asked.
Then the interviewer asked about my branch and why I still want to pursue a field in IT/SDE and why
not core (You need to prepare this answer beforehand or at least be mentally prepared as to how to
tackle this question. You can use real life examples or situations which swayed you in this field. Don't
give a really generic answer to this question as they have been interviewing for quite awhile and your
impression would really sink in this case).
Next he came to projects, he liked the premise of one of my projects so jumped into the details of it,
he asked about the projects in a little unconventional way which threw me off a bit, so beware of such
stuff. Then he inquired about my hackathons and some more skills mentioned in my resume. Then he
jumped to code-languages. He asked have I used C++ in any project and not just as a programming
language as I had mentioned it was the language I was proficient at. Then he asked if I was experienced
with Java along with C++ and Python (Most MNC's prefer Java so even if you're a CPP coder like me
or Python, try to learn Core Java concepts through Youtube -I referred to Kunal Kushwaha and
InterviewBit). I mentioned I know some concepts and am keen to learn more (They mainly want people
who are keen to learn and fast learners, so keep note of that). He seemed satisfied with my answer and
moved on to the next question as a follow up on previous ones. Asked me about my knowledge of
pointers in CPP and told me to impl ement a Linked List using pointers and then asked some more
questions about my work in hackathon and 1 basic HR question and that was it.
Then he asked if I had any questions to ask him. I asked a couple of them and the interview ended.
Few really good questions we must ask which will sway the interviewer's interest in our way but more
importantly, the interviewer could remember you by the questions you asked as well.

3. [Technical + HR round] [ Around 22 candidates who appeared for this round ]

During the interview process, I found it helpful to take note of the interviewers' names, as they were
introduced during the PPT. This knowledge proved advantageous in the second round, particularly
when many candidates struggled to recall their interviewers' names, I had insight into my interviewer's
area of expertise, which aided my responses.
The interview lasted approximately 25 to 30 minutes. While most candidates experienced a
combination of technical and HR questions, some faced additional technical inquiries, especially
related to testing. It's essential to remain adaptable and open-minded throughout the process.
My interview commenced with the classic "Tell me about yourself" question. This is a crucial aspect
of the interview, as it sets the tone and allows you to steer the conversation. I provided a clear and
concise response regarding my academic background, wh ich seemed to resonate positively with the
interviewer.
The discussion then shifted to my internships and projects. I took the opportunity to explain my projects
while subtly integrating the RISES principles where applicable.
Following this, the interviewer posed an SQL query question that was straightforward but included
certain restrictions. I was able to answer it effectively and move on to the next question.
Next came an HR scenario: "If you were assigned a job that you truly disliked, how would you approach
this situation?" I crafted a detailed and thoughtful response, anticipating potential follow-up questions,
which ultimately led the interviewer to refrain from asking any further inquiries.
The interview concluded with a few questions from me directed at the interviewer, allowing for a well-
rounded exchange.
[ 19 students were offered the job ]

4. Prank Round

I was done with both my interviews at around 4:50 pm and was anxiously waiting for the results. There were
rumors that they are going to conduct one more round. At around 6.15 pm all except 2 or 3 of the candidates
shortlisted for the second round were called inside room 105. They first announced that they were keeping 1
more interview round and asked everyone if there was any problem. Then they said that they will be calling
out a few names who will not be selected for further process and have to leave the room immediately. Then
they revealed that this was a PRANK and all of you have been selected!

A helpful tip to keep in mind is that if you believe in your skills and know you're deserving,
avoid going into interviews with high expectations. Expectations can add unnecessary
pressure and may lead to disappointment if things don't go as planned. Instead, approach
the interview as a productive conversation between you and the interviewer. Stay confident,
focus on showcasing your strengths, and give it your best effort.
A general tip:- Most of the companies that visited our campus required JAVA. So if possible be
aware with the concepts of core JAVA(basic syntax is enough). It was not the case with barclays
though.
Other tips:

• Be transparent during the interview - If you don't know an answer, be honest and say,

"I'm not aware of this concept, sir/ma'am."

• Know the RISES values of Barclays - Be familiar with these values and be prepared to

explain each one with a real-life example.

• Be truthful on your resume - Only include skills and experiences you are confident

about and can discuss in detail.

• Have a strong grasp of CS fundamentals - Make sure you are well-versed in core areas

like DBMS, OOP, and DSA, as these showcase your problem-solving abilities.

• Understand SQL and transaction concepts - Since Barclays is a bank, you should be

thorough with SQL concepts, especially transaction control queries (TCL) and ACID
properties.

journey.howSecured:
Placement process consisted of 3 rounds:

1. Online assessment (was to be taken from college)

2. Technical interview

3. Techno-HR round

A minimum CGPA of 7 or above was mandatory to apply for this job.

1. [Online Assessment] [11/09/24 ]

The Online test was of 1hr 30 minutes duration. It consisted of CS fundamentals mcq(guess the
output(Java based), DBMS, OOPS), a 20 marks sql query and a 50 marks coding question. The
coding question was similar to: String generation
The SQL question was straightforward, with no questions involving joins or subqueries. Make
sure to practice questions involving date as a column (extracting the day, month, and year from a
date column), as this was required in the question.
I believe I answered most of the MCQs correctly, solved the SQL question accurately, and passed
5 out of 10 test cases in the coding question.
35 students were shortlisted for the next round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. [Technical Interview] [ 12/09/24 ]

There were 9 panelists, each with 3 or 4 students assigned to them. In my panel, there were 4
students, including me, and I was interviewed last. My interview took place after the lunch
break, so don't worry if your interview starts late.
The interview didn't begin with the typical 'introduce yourself' question. Instead, the interviewer
asked, 'What do you think is unique about Barclays that makes you want to join?' I gave three
answers (always try to include the RISES values of Barclays in such questions), but after each
one, he said, 'Every tech company has that or does that.' I think he was testing my ability to stay
confident. Even though I mentioned some of the tech stack that Barclays uses, like Java, he still
asked, 'You don't have experience with the company's tech stack, so why are you applying for
this job?' Don't panic at such questions. Answer confidently-- they're just testing how well
you handle pressure and stand by your reasonsạẠại
After that, he moved on to the 'Introduce yourself' question. Then, he asked about my first
project, where I had built an ARIMA model (a time series prediction model) and he asked me to
explain it. He also asked about all the keywords I had mentioned in that project.
I had also listed a data analytics project involving SQL and PowerBI, so he asked if I was
proficient in SQL. I said yes, and he then asked if I knew about triggers and views in SQL. While
I understood the concepts, I wasn't familiar with the exact syntax, so I explained the concepts
and also mentioned stored procedures. He then asked me to write a stored procedure that takes
three parameters and returns a result, which I was able to do. Next, he handed me a blank sheet
of paper and asked me to write everything I knew in SQL (primarily syntax) and explain it to
him. I somehow forgot about joins at that moment. He then asked, 'Do you know about joins?' I
said yes, and he asked me to explain the ones I was familiar with, so I described inner, right, left,
and full outer joins.
Next, he asked about OOP concepts and told me to write a skeleton structure on paper explaining
the four pillars of OOP. I explained each pillar with examples by writing code. He allowed me to
choose any programming language.
Then, he asked basic DSA questions, starting with the selection sort algorithm and then merge
sort. He asked me to explain both algorithms and write pseudocode for each. After that, he
moved on to a project I had mentioned that involved ReactS. He asked me some questions about
ReactJS concepts. I didn't know some of the terms he mentioned, so I confidently told him I
wasn't familiar with them. Then he asked me to differentiate between props and state(a standard
question of react), which I had prepared for in advance.
Finally, he asked about my major project (a hardware project) and told me to explain what we
were doing in it. After I explained, he confirmed for clarification and said, 'Okay, you're doing
--- PAGE 3 ---
this in your project, great.' He then said, 'I'm done with your interview, do you have any
questions for me?' (Make sure to prepare two good questions for the interviewer, as it shows your
interest in the company.)
After this round o total of 22 students were selected for the 2nd round.

3. [HR round] [ 12/09/24 ]

This round was a mix of technical and HR questions. It began with my introduction, followed by
questions about my project, such as where I got the dataset and why I chose to do the project.
Then, he asked why Python is mostly used for data analytics over other languages. Since I had
mentioned pandas in my project, he asked how to join two dataframes using pandas, and what a
numpy array is.
Next, he indirectly asked about normalization by giving an example of a table with student id,
student name, course_id, and course_name. He asked if we could add a course without any
student opting for it. I said no, explaining that it would cause an insertion anomaly, so we would
need to decompose the table. I suggested creating two tables- one for students and one for
coursesso we could add courses independently. When he asked how to access both tables
together, I explained that we would join the tables and use a primary key and foreign key to
reference between them. He seemed satisfied with my answer.
Then, he asked a situational question: 'If your team lead proposes an idea, but you have a better
one, how would you suggest it without offending the team lead?' He asked another similar
question. Finally, he noticed I had mentioned GitHub on my resume and asked, 'What is
GitHub?' which I answered.
At the end, he said, 'I'm done with my questions, do you have any questions for me?' (Make sure
to have two questions prepared, which don't necessarily need to be technical, to show your
interest in the company.)
A total of 19 grads were selected for the job.

journey.prep:
• Always be honest with your answers: The interviewers are highly experienced, and they can easily

tell whether you are being honest or not. If you don't know the answer, politely tell them that you
don't know or are not able to recall it. Don't beat around the bush.

• Be thorough with RISES: Either you will be asked about it in the interview, or you will be judged

based on your answers. If asked in an interview, try to explain how you have followed it during your
projects or hackathons.

• Drive the Interview: Sometimes, you have the opportunity to guide the interview in the

direction you want. Use this to your advantage.

• Resume: Be honest with your resume and know it very well. Prepare for every word in it and

every technology used by you.

salary (this was solved using a subquery). After asking for a hint, I was able to solve it.

3 Rounds were conducted in total, 1 Online Test and 2 Interviews

1. Online Test [138 candidates]

The test was of 1 hour 30 minutes, it consisted of CS fundamental MCQS (variable marks), a DSA question
(50 marks) and an SQL query (10 marks).
The DSA question was similar to this:
https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
The SQL question was a basic aggregate query.
I was able to solve 5/10 test cases for DSA, SQL and MCQs.

2. Tech Interview [34 candidates]

The interviews were scheduled for the next day, after the ppt. Be attentive during the ppt as it will be helpful
in answering certain questions in the interviews.
My first interviewer was a Vice President at Barclays. He did not ask for an introduction and started
discussing my first project for a few minutes.
After that I was asked about OOPs concepts (Polymorphism and Inheritance in Java). The questions on
polymorphism were about differentiating between overriding and overloading and whether function return
type should be different for overloading. Next, I was asked to give an example of inheritance, then he asked
if there are 2 classes, SUV and Truck, what relation would be among them (siblings, as they will be derived
from a parent class Vehicle as inheritance is an IS-A relationship).
Next I was asked an SQL query where I had to find the second largest value in a column (offset).
Then I was asked 'Why Barclays?', to which I responded that I had an interest in the fintech domain. He
followed with asking about topics on finance (which I did not have as much knowledge on and mentioned
it). I was given a question where I had to calculate the compound interest, given 1000R as principal, rate of
10% and duration of 3 years. I could not recall the formula for it so he said that I could use the formula for
--- PAGE 2 ---
simple interest. Using that, I calculated the final amount compounding it annually. Then he asked me to
derive the formula for compound interest using the obtained series.
Next I was asked a puzzle similar to this:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-the-burning-candles/
In the end he was open to questions so I asked about general projects that Barclays does and projects that he
has done as a part of Barclays.

3. Tech+HR Interview [21 candidates]

Generally these interviews were HR only, but for me it was a mix of tech and HR. The interviewer first
asked me for an introduction (tech stack, hobbies and family background). Then he asked how my day had
gone so far, and how my first interview went and an overview of it (I gave a brief recollection of it,
remember the name of your interviewers as it creates a good impression). He asked when I had started
preparing for Barclays and what achievements did Barclays have that made me interested in it (paying
attention to the ppt helped out a lot here) and when had I become interested in the CS domain.
After that he moved on to asking why I chose web development and my tech stack (MERN), more details on
my project and that if I was selected, which role would suit me best (again it was important to have had paid
attention to ppt as six roles were mentioned for which they were hiring). Then he asked me whether I knew
what accessibility features were (in regards to UI/UX).
Next was a scenario based question where data was classified as secret, internal, external and unrestricted
and that I had to classify it. First was data from a customer who had submitted it to the company (I answered
internal, as the customer had trusted the company with their private information), next if I was a manager
what type of data would be my employee's salary (I answered secret).
Next I was asked situational questions. First, if I were part of a team whose project is to be launched the next
day and I encountered a bug the night prior, what would be my response? Next, a meeting is called with the
developers and testers, how would I relay information about the bug in that meeting? Eventually he asked a
question on unit testing and I said that I was not familiar with it, so he moved on to the next scenario, which
was more related to ML models.
In the end he asked me for any questions to which I asked what was his favorite part of working at Barclays.
In the end 19 candidates got selected (following a prank round 3 :))

Barclays had hired students prior to this via Hack-O-Hire and the CyberShala course, and it came pretty late
for the on-campus hiring. It was a two-day process consisting of:

1. Online Assessment (OA)

2. Technical Interview Round

3. Techno-HR Interview Round

4. A prank, yes you read that right, a prank (disguised as a 3rd Interview Round)

An in-depth description of everything is given below:

1. Online Assessment [138 students appeared for this round]

The OA was scheduled on 11" September at 8 am, and only those students who had a CGPA above 7 were
allowed to sit for the same. The test was conducted on HackerEarth, consisting of 12 MCQS, 1 coding and 1
SQL question.
A crucial point to note, make sure that you have a fighting CGPA, for reasons I'll explain below.
Now, a fun fact about this test, it was 1 hr 30 mins long and IT WAS THE SAME TEST AS THE ONE I
HAD GIVEN FOR THE BARCLAYS SUMMER INTERNSHIP ROLE!
--- PAGE 2 ---
The 12 MCQs were on CS fundamentals, code snippets for which you had to mark the correct output, SQL
fundamentals and queries, all-in-all consisting of 40 marks. I'll add my resources for the same towards the
end. Do not take these lightly as they contribute a good chunk to your score.
The SQL question was worth 10 marks, where you were given a table and you had to figure out the
compensation a person would get. Just read the question properly and you can easily solve it using a
WHERE clause and a bunch of AND operations.
Now comes the fun part, the coding question on strings, which could be categorized as a Leetcode medium
but the edge cases make it seem much harder. The question states:
You are given 2 strings S1 and S2, S1 will consist of a string of characters and S2 will consist of just two
characters 'T' and 'F' in any order, such that the order of 'T'/F' will map to the answer string you return in
such a way that if a character in S2 at some index is 'T', the answer string should consist of characters from
S1 starting from that index, and if it is 'F' at least one character from the substring of length S1 starting from
that index shouldn't match. And your objective is to return the lexicographically smallest such answer
string.
For example, consider S1 = "ABCA" and S2 = "TFFF", whose answer string is "ABCAAAA".
Now you may very well start off with the same thought process I had, that is to consider an answer string of
length S1 + S2 - 1 consisting of all A's and then just copying the string characters of S1 from the index of
'T' till length of S1. Yes, that will do the job for 5 of the test cases, for the next part you had to ensure the
string was lexicographically smallest, that meant changing the substring starting at 'F', now this will get you
to 8 test cases. Now, for the infuriating part, to completely pass all the test cases, you simply had to run a
loop to check the validity of the string (which I missed).
The bottom line being, your logic for the code may be correct but the test cases may not be so kind, so
bear that in mind.
Now as I mentioned before, to have a fighting CGPA, that may come in handy for you as some students just
managed to pass 2 test cases but their CGPA came in clutch and pulled them through, for others it was the
MCQS which was their saving grace, so do the MCQs diligently. The results were announced in the evening
and 34 students were shortlisted for the interviews.

2. Technical Interview Round [34 students appeared for this round]

The interviews were scheduled for the next day, 12ạiSeptember, and prior to this, a PPT was organized
They were going to start at 10 am but all the members hadn't arrived so it was a long wait, so a good night's
sleep is a must before the interviews. A tip here, keep yourself busy during this span, have a chat with your
friends, go eat something, anything to keep yourself fresh.
The interviews began at 11:30 am. There were 9 panels for the Grads and 6 panels for the Summer Interns
which were taking place simultaneously. I was the first in my panel. As I sat waiting in the TPO lobby, my
interviewer Mr. Rahul Garware himself came to call me into the cabin to begin the interview. Side note
about him, he is an alumnus of our college, which I learned during the PPT.
He created a very comfortable environment before commencing the interview, asked me about my day, to
which I responded and asked him about his. He told me to have a seat, while he himself stood for a few
--- PAGE 3 ---
minutes, examining my resume before seating. My entire interview revolved around one project in my
resume - my major project for a Multimodal Depression System and we conversed the entirety of 30
minutes on it. He asked me to explain it, and was particularly interested in its practical application in a
company like Barclays. He switched to BERT (which I had used in my project) and asked me to find a use
case where it could be used to find typos in trade data, to which I responded I hadn't heard of BERT being
used for numeric data evaluation, but I did manage to explain my thought process to him. After that, he gave
me an 'assignment' to be done at home, regarding the same, and said he was done and whether I had any
questions for him. I asked him what prerequisites we are required to have before joining - to which he said
whatever you have learned throughout your curriculum, is enough and that most of the learning process
happens on the job. He also asked me whether I had any feedback for how the interview was conducted, to
which I responded this seemed more like a discussion than an interview, to which he laughingly said, that
was the point.
A word of advice here, remain confident and maintain a positive attitude, one of the main things to keep in
mind while answering questions for Barclays is their RISES principles - Respect, Integrity, Services,
Excellence, and Stewardship. If you feel you do not know the answer, just say it, try to mention something
which you do recall around the same question, like I said about BERT not being used for numeric data and I
mentioned how BERT works, they are just testing how much you know, so just tell them what you know.
This was how my interview went, but a few of my friends were asked questions on OS, OOPs, SQL along
with projects in their resume. Know your resume inside-out, be prepared for any curveballs on the
same.
Post-lunch, around 3 pm, a list of 17 students were called out to go for the next round, while some students
still had their first ones left. Five more were shortlisted for the next round, while my next round was going
on.

3. Techno-HR Round [22 students appeared for this round]

Like the round before, I was the first one in my panel. For some students it was a techno-HR round, but for
me it was purely HR, though I didn't know it at the time. The interview started off with questions on my
resume and as I was about to explain the flow of one of my projects, the interviewer cut me off saying that
won't be necessary, this isn't a technical round anyway.
So, right then and there, I switched gears into HR mode. I was asked situation-based questions - what would
you do if you're in a conflict with one of your colleagues, what would you do if your colleagues are in a
conflict, what would your process for pitching a new idea be, what would you do if you found your
colleague doing something unethical.
I replied keeping the RISES principles in mind, and also, I was asked to reiterate my responses given a new
problem, so answer all of these without fail, even if you take some time to think about the same.
At the end, when asked if I had any questions for him, I asked the same question I asked in the previous
round and another one - how can one change departments? Funnily enough, he asked me you're asking all
of these questions like you know you've already been selected, who told you this, there is still an asterisk
after your name. I apologized saying that this wasn't mentioned in the PPT so I was curious and he smiled
and said it's standard for almost all companies but I'll tell you since you asked me this. So yeah, that
happened :)
--- PAGE 4 ---
This round lasted approximately 30 minutes, though it's hard to keep track of time during the interview.

4. The Supposed 3 Round

My interviews were done by 4 pm and then came the brutal waiting game. To kill time, I sat and chatted
with my friends, had a snack in the canteen, and went for a walk. In the middle of my walk, I was informed
that there may be another round. Now bear in mind it was 6:30 pm, I was mentally drained, just wishing for
the day to be over, so I got a bit worried that I wouldn't be able to perform well. We waited till 7 pm, and
then 19 out of the 22 students were called into room 105, for the next round.
It was a grim environment designed to fool us all. We were asked whether we would be comfortable staying
late, as it will take some time, given Mumbai traffic and Ganpati on top of that, to which we grudgingly said
yes. Then our names were read one by one, and it was declared that these names..., are all selected! That
was quite possibly the tensest 10 minutes of my life, then turned into the best minute of my life. We were
then given general feedback and called below for a photo shoot.
19 grads and 13 interns were selected finally.

journey.prep:
1. CGPA: I recommend maintaining a high CGPA if possible. Some startups that visit the campus

perform an internal shortlisting and set a criterion of 8.5 or higher. However, if your CGPA is low,
don't worry-most companies don't have strict requirements.

2. The harsh reality of placements is that most of it is based on sheer luck. From my experience, I can

tell that it may happen that your interview went very well and you were not selected or your panel
was extremely strict and was asking very difficult questions. It may also happen that during online
assessment you got a more difficult DSA ques because in OA what matters is how many test cases
you passed, they don't care whether your ques was easy, medium or difficult.
But remember at the end you need to be lucky just once.

3. Learn to handle rejections, as they are part of the process. Personally, I gave interviews in 11

companies and in 3 of them I got rejected in the last(HR) round. Getting rejected at the last stage can
be really disheartening, and it takes a lot of resilience to pick yourself up and start preparing for the
next company from scratch.

4. Do show the interviewers that you are eager to learn new technologies and adapt to different

challenges. Highlight your curiosity and openness to growth, as many companies value candidates
who are proactive about upskilling and staying updated with industry trends. Demonstrating this
mindset can set you apart from others.

5. Even if Java is not your primary language, it's beneficial to learn the basic concepts and practice a

few programs on the online GDB. Many companies visiting campus tend to prefer Java, so having a
solid grasp of it can significantly improve your chances during interviews.
I am not attaching any links for DSA, OOPS, Java etc. Most of my peers have done that so do refer to their
docs.
Feel free to contact me for any doubts -: linkedin
Finally all the best and remember "What is meant for you will find its way to you." So don't give up.

https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4006812/String-Generation-OA-Question
The SQL query was really simple, I don't remember it exactly but I could solve it easily with a simple
'WHERE' clause.
--- PAGE 2 ---
I was able to solve most of the MCQS, SQL and passed 8/10 test cases of the DSA ques.
Try to solve DSA ques first as it has the most marks and can solely decide whether you get selected for the
next round or not. First, try to pass as many test cases as possible using a brute force approach, and then
focus on optimizing the solution.
After this, the shortlist was announced on the same day at 5pm. 34 students were shortlisted for the PPT and
interview rounds which were scheduled the next day.
PPT
The pre-placement talk (PPT) was scheduled for 12/9/24. The shortlisted candidates were asked to report
to Room 105 at 9:00 AM, but the PPT actually began at 10:40 AM. Make sure to pay attention during
the PPT, as they covered important details about Barclays' history, locations, roles, and values. The
interviewer may ask questions like, "What do you know about Barclays?" or "What was your favorite
part of the PPT?"

3. Technical Interview [ 34 students appeared for this round]

Duration -: 1 hr 15 mins
Immediately after the PPT the interviews were scheduled. There were a total of 9 panels taking
interviews simultaneously. I was last in my panel. When I was called for the interview it was announced
that it was lunch time and my interview will be conducted after lunch. But until then they released a
preliminary shortlist for the second round for those who were done with their interviews.
So my round actually happened at 3pm. I was first asked to introduce myself and explain my projects.
Make sure to have a good introduction and when discussing your projects, start by explaining the
problem statement, followed by the team size, your role and contributions, the technology stack used,
and finally, the use cases of the project. If the project was a part of a hackathon do mention that.
The project discussion lasted approximately 25-30 minutes. Since my projects were primarily focused on
machine learning and deep learning, I was asked to explain some of the algorithms I used, how I collect
and ensure the quality of the data, and how my projects would function in real-time scenarios.
After that, the interviewer asked if I was familiar with OOPS and requested explanations of inheritance
and polymorphism. I was then asked to write code demonstrating method overriding and method
overloading. Since I mentioned that my preferred language was Java, I was asked about multiple
inheritance and the diamond problem in Java and how to resolve it. I explained that it can be solved
using interfaces, leading to further questions on that topic. The interviewer also asked about the
@override keyword in Java and what would happen if it was not used. I was grilled a lot on method
overriding and was given multiple scenarios to determine the outcomes.
Then he moved on to DSA. The interviewer first asked me about the data structures I knew. I answered
Stacks, Queues, Linked-List, Hashset and Hashmap. I did not mention trees and graphs because I had not
revised them recently. Then he asked me to write a code to implement Linked List, Stack and Queue
--- PAGE 3 ---
from scratch on a piece of paper. After that he gave me a scenario where in a class is given and an array
is given inside the class and I was supposed to write 2 functions one for stack and another for queue such
that whenever the respective function is called the array would behave according to the stack or queue
operations.
The questions were not very difficult but the interviewer grilled me a lot on every point of the interview.
However, they were very considerate and guided me if I made any mistakes or went off track.
At the end of the interview, I was asked if I had any questions. I inquired about what a typical day would
look like if I were working at Barclays and how the technology team collaborates with other teams, such
as risk management.
It may happen that you are still not done with your first interview and you have some people who are
already done with their HR rounds. Try to stay calm in these situations.

4. Techno - HR interview [ 21 students appeared for this round]

Duration -: 30 mins
Different people had different experiences in this round. For some, it was a direct HR interview, while
for others, it was a combined tech and HR interview. In my case, it was entirely resume-based.
After 2 mins of completing my first interview, I was called for the second round. The interviewer started
by saying you have had a long wait for the first round and now immediately you have been called for the
second round so I won't be asking you much. So again the interviewer asked me to introduce myself.
In the HR round, do mention hobbies in your introduction. I mentioned traveling and exploring different
places as one of my hobbies. So the interviewer asked about the places I visited recently.
After this the interviewer gave their formal introduction and explained to me the values of Barclays.
I mentioned in my introduction that my CGPA was above 9. The interviewer then asked how I managed
to maintain such a high CGPA, especially given my background in EXTC while studying predominantly
computer science subjects. They then asked me whether I would prefer a job in core or software. For
people belonging to EXTC background this question will be always asked directly or indirectly in the
interviews.
Then they moved on to my resume and asked me about my projects which I had worked on. Again as
most of my projects were related to ML they asked me to explain the model building process right from
collection of data to deploying the model. Then they asked if I had any knowledge of DevOps. I shared
my understanding of the concept.
Finally they asked whether I would be willing to work on a tech stack I have never used before. This is a
very common question. Do answer this question with utmost positivity and give examples for the same.
At the end of the interview, I was asked if I had any questions. I asked about the training program at
Barclays.
For this round particularly do read about the values of Barclays 'RISES" from their website.
--- PAGE 4 ---

5. Prank Round

I was done with both my interviews at around 5 pm and was anxiously waiting for the results. There
were rumors that they are going to conduct one more round. At around 6.15 pm all except 2 or 3 of the
candidates shortlisted for the second round were called inside room 105. They first announced that they
were keeping 1 more interview round and asked everyone if there was any problem. Then they said that
they will be calling out a few names who will not be selected for further process and have to leave the
room immediately. Then they revealed that this was a PRANK and all of you have been selected!
A total of 19 students received the FTE offer.

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
1. CGPA: I recommend maintaining a high CGPA if possible. Some startups that visit the campus

perform an internal shortlisting and set a criterion of 8.5 or higher. However, if your CGPA is low,
don't worry-most companies don't have strict requirements.

2. The harsh reality of placements is that most of it is based on sheer luck. From my experience, I can

tell that it may happen that your interview went very well and you were not selected or your panel
was extremely strict and was asking very difficult questions. It may also happen that during online
assessment you got a more difficult DSA ques because in OA what matters is how many test cases
you passed, they don't care whether your ques was easy, medium or difficult.
But remember at the end you need to be lucky just once.

3. Learn to handle rejections, as they are part of the process. Personally, I gave interviews in 11

companies and in 3 of them I got rejected in the last(HR) round. Getting rejected at the last stage can
be really disheartening, and it takes a lot of resilience to pick yourself up and start preparing for the
next company from scratch.

4. Do show the interviewers that you are eager to learn new technologies and adapt to different

challenges. Highlight your curiosity and openness to growth, as many companies value candidates
who are proactive about upskilling and staying updated with industry trends. Demonstrating this
mindset can set you apart from others.

5. Even if Java is not your primary language, it's beneficial to learn the basic concepts and practice a

few programs on the online GDB. Many companies visiting campus tend to prefer Java, so having a
solid grasp of it can significantly improve your chances during interviews.
I am not attaching any links for DSA, OOPS, Java etc. Most of my peers have done that so do refer to their
docs.
Feel free to contact me for any doubts -: linkedin
Finally all the best and remember "What is meant for you will find its way to you." So don't give up.

journey.howSecured:
Barclays organized an industrial-academia hackathon called Hack-O-Hire, which I had the opportunity to
participate in and win. The details of this experience are also mentioned in my LinkedIn post. Initially, there
were around 1,200 teams participating, and out of these, 28 teams were selected (5 from our college) for the
final hackathon, which was conducted at the Barclays Pune campus. Some of the candidates from these
shortlisted teams were given the opportunity to proceed directly to the interview stage, skipping the online
assessment round.

1. Technical Round [ 9 Candidates participated in this round - 3 Hackathon / 6 Cybershala]

My first round of interviews at Barclays was conducted online via Microsoft Teams by the Assistant
Director, and it lasted for about 45 minutes. The interview began with a brief introduction, during which I
highlighted my experience winning a hackathon on a cybersecurity problem statement. This led the
interviewer to ask some cybersecurity-related questions, such as What does a hacker typically do after
gaining access to a victim's system? and What are trojans, backdoors, and worms? He also followed up with
a specific question about how backdoors work.
Next, he asked me to open Notepad and discuss the components of the backend. He then instructed me to:

• Write code for a login page for both frontend and backend.

• Connect the login page to a database.

• Write JavaScript for the password field.

Following that, I was asked several questions on APIs:

• What is REST?

• Perform an API call using Postman.

• Explain the body, headers, and keys of a URL.

• Write API routing code.

• What is regex? He then asked me to write a regex expression for the password field.

He also inquired about the design aspects of an application, asking If you were creating an application, what
would your component roadmap look like? Later to write code to connect a database (any) to your web
application.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The interview concluded with some DSA-related questions:

• Write optimal code to calculate factorial.

• Given an unsorted array with 100 elements, add the 101st element in the correct position. This was

for a dynamic array, where the array has no fixed size, and each new number needs to be inserted in
the appropriate position.

2. Techno-HR Round [7 Candidates participated in this round - 3 Hackathon / 4 Cybershala]

My second round interview at Barclays began about 1-2 hours after the first round and lasted for about 1.15
hours. The interviewer was quite relaxed and even encouraged me to not be nervous before we started. He
opened the interview by asking me for a brief introduction, and then transitioned into several situational
questions.
One of the key questions was: You're working on a project with a deadline tomorrow, and you discover that
your selected model is showing a 25% risk. What approach would you take?
The majority of the interview involved situational questions like this. Afterward, he moved on to some
technical topics and basics of OOPS, DBMS such as:

• What is method overriding and function overloading?

• Why do we use OOP, what are the advantages of OOP, and can you provide real-life examples of

OOP?

• What is better between an array and a list?

The conversation then shifted to typical HR questions, such as:

• Provide an example where you did something extraordinary.

• Give an example where you and your colleagues had different opinions, and explain how you

handled the situation.

• Can you share an example where you realized you had made a mistake, and how did you deal with

it?

• Tell me something in your academic journey that you're really proud of.

• What are your plans regarding a master's degree?

• Do you have a dream company?

7 students were offered the role and I was one of them !!!.

15 Technical MCQS: Focus on Java, DBMS, OOP, and SQL, DSA

During the online test, allocate the first 20 minutes to tackling the DSA question and try to develop a
solution. After that, move on to the MCQS, which should take no more than 30-35 minutes. Once you have
completed the MCQS, revisit the DSA question with a fresh perspective.

2. Technical Interview (1st August)

Introduce yourself: keep it short and crisp, practice it a few times.
If you are an EXTC student you would be asked this in all interviews and hr rounds:
Why do you want to pursue a career in tech instead of core?

- Prepare a strong answer for this beforehand.

- My answer: Engineering develops your logical reasoning, critical thinking and

problem-solving. Which can be used to write esp32 code or a web application.

- You could also say that during my first year of engineering, I excelled in C and C++.

This developed a passion for programming and problem-solving and I pursued this
interest further while balancing my core branch studies and projects.

- Do mention if you are enrolled in cs minor.

Java and OOP questions.

- Know the functionality of JDK, JRE, JVM, and JIT. How is Java different from other

languages. Advantages and disadvantages.
Projects:

- Have at least 1 unique project which they might not have seen before.

- Prepare a brief intro for each project, and prepare questions, and follow-ups that could be

asked about the project.

- The follow-up questions are asked from your answers. Be careful about what you say.

- Prepare answers on your tech stack and why you chose that tech stack. How is it different

from others?
DBMS and skills:

- What are rollbacks and transactions. Their significance.

- standard questions on Spring Boot and JavaScript.

Puzzle:

- Find out the 1 heavier ball from the other 7 of equal weight using a balance only twice.

- Resource: GeeksforGeeks link.

While answering questions try to maintain eye contact with the interviewer. If you don't know the
answer, give it a try then say I don't know.
Question for the interviewer:

- you can use this to showcase your excitement for the company.

- I asked: What is your favorite part of working at UBS? What are some skills I can learn

before joining?

- You could also ask about the role and tech stack but this is usually answered in the ppt so

asking it again implies you didn't attend the ppt.

- Do attend the pre-placement talk and learn about their principles, and values.

--- PAGE 3 ---
While answering questions, even if you know the answer, start from scratch and build up your
response. This showcases your thought process to the interviewer and allows them to provide hints if
you are heading in the wrong direction.

These are some specific things I would like to share. You can find all the resources below.

1. Try to build your project from the ground-up, if you have the time. If not, know every part of

your project extremely well. Prepare some common questions beforehand for every project.

2. Practice timed DSA questions. Start giving contests as early as possible.

3. Sometimes while focusing o n the advance d concepts, we tend to forget /neglect the

fundamentals. So, revise them thoroughly to build a strong base.

4. For interview rounds,  rather than searching for top interview questions and answers, learn

everything about and around the topics.

5. I know its easier said than done, but do not overthink and overprepare in your head for different

interview scenarios. Most of the times, it's a very natural discussion during interviews.

6. Try not to make any company 'the ultimate'. It just adds more pressure  and stress during the

process.

3 rounds were conducted.

1. Online Assessment  - (Aptitude + CS Fundamentals + 1 DSA question)

2. Technical Round

3. HR Round

1.     Online Assessment  [Around 200 students appeared for this round ]

This was a 90-minute HackerRank Test that was to be given from college. It had three sections.

1. 15 questions on CS Fundamentals majorly focusing on OOPS, SQL and Java/C.

The questions were conceptual, testing fundamental knowledge of these subjects.

2. 15 Aptitude questions - Probability, Speed of Trains, Boats and Streams, Ratio and Proportion etc

Refer to IndiaBix for practicing such questions.

3. 1 DSA question:

severLoad = [3,4,5]
serverCapacity = [6,2,7]

Return a combination of the serverLoad array where sumOf(serverLoad[i]*serverCapacity[i]) is
minimum. If multiple combinations are possible, then return the lexicographically smallest array.

Base Idea:  Assign the smallest available serverLoad element to the largest available
serverCapacity element to get the minimum value for sumOf(serverLoad[i]*serverCapacity[i])

My Approach:

1. Create a min heap for storing serverLoad elements and maxheap to store serverCapacity

elements.

2. Create a hashmap to store the key->value as elementOfServerCapacity->indexOfServerCapacity

from the serverCapacity array.

3. As there can be same valued elements at multiple different indices, you can make the hashmap

of type (Integer,List) so that if the key is repeated, you can add the indices in the list.

4. Create a new answer array.

5. Remove minheap element, this is the element you want to place at a particular index in the

answer array.

6. Remove maxheap element, and search in the map for the key and you will get the list of indices

where you can add the minheap element

7. From this list of indices choose the last index in the list because you want the lexicographically

smallest possible combination.

8. Add the minheap element to that index, remove the last element from the list and add the list

back to the hashmap.

9. Do this until all elements of the heap are removed.

10. Return the answer array.

The interviewer asked  me to introduce myself . After a brief 2 -minute introduction, ranging from my
academic projects to extra-curriculars, the interview pivoted to the projects I mentioned and their
explanations. Many of the candidate's interviews revolved around their projects/experience.

They asked me questions related to the scope of the project, the changes to be made in the future and how
I would make them. They were curious to know about how I contributed to the project and collaboratively
built and managed the work on my projects. Some basic questions were asked about the tech stacks used.

Moving on to the fundamental CS subjects such as DBMS, OOPS, Java, API etc. They presented a scenario
and asked me which type of database would be more useful and why. Difference between SQL and NoSQL
and its advantages over another. Different HTTP requests and their use cases. Questions on polymorphism,
its types and some cross questioning. They asked me about File Handling in Java . As I was unaware of
the concept, I said that I have used file handling in one of my projects using Java Script but I have yet to
explore the concept in Java. Difference between ArrayList and HashMap in Java and how can they be used
interchangeably. Can HashMap have objects as keys and other similar questions were asked.

Two Problem Solving questions.

1. Water Jug Problem

2. If 7 balls of the same weight and 1 heavier ball were present in a basket, just by using a weighing scale,

how would you find the weight of the heavier ball in minimum operations? O(1)

Lastly, the interview ended with me asking a question about the use of cloud computing at UBS.

journey.prep:
The most important thing about placement season you need to understand is that there is a large
amount of luck involved here. You can increase your chances by practicing as much as possible but in
the end you really need good luck (only once ;)).
I did not get through 5 companies before landing this offer. All that went wrong was pure bad luck. My
resume was not shortlisted for Work India even though I prepared a lot for it and I verified it from one of the
senior employees itself, it was purely random. Same thing happened with JPMC and there was nothing I
could do about it. So be ready that even though your resume is great and according to the JD it could not be
shortlisted.
When I finally landed my first interview for MSCI, it went horribly wrong as the interviewer was very
difficult to impress and was asking the toughest of questions, it was least likely to qualify for the further
rounds though him (hardly anyone could). Same thing repeated for IDFC too!. Be ready that you might get
a tough interviewer and your interview might go completely different from others and in a bad way.
Then I was not selected after the HR round of InCred even though everything went as perfect as they
could've just because the seats were limited. So be ready for rejections even if you have answered
everything perfectly well.
These are mentally tough times to process as it takes a lot of effort from some to achieve it while it happens
in the first for some. What is important is to not give up and embrace the process instead of stressing about
it. Have trust in yourself, and it will work out, just keep grinding consistently till it happens and it will
happen !!

There were 3 rounds for this process all within the span of two days. Make sure you are prepared beforehand
as you will be notified a day prior to the OA Test and the Interviews of shortlisted candidates is on the next
day itself.

1. Round 1: Online Aptitude Test [ 208 students appeared and it was conducted in college]

There were 30 MCQS: 15 Technical - Java, SQL, DBMS and 15 Aptitude.
There was 1 coding question and it was important to solve it fully to get through.
My Question was after simplification of the word problem into a basic question, it would look something
like this : Given an input string consisting of characters 'a', 'b', and 'c', determine the minimum number of
insertions required to transform the string into a sequence of "abc" repeated multiple times, without
changing the order of existing characters.

2. Round 2: Technical Interview [36 Students appeared in College the next day]

The Round started with Introduction (By this time I had mentioned this already in 4 interviews and I was
well versed in it). Make sure to keep your introduction simple yet elegant, mention those things and
achievements in which you are confident if questions are asked about. The interview started with the
Interviewer going through my Resume and asking me about the mentioned Projects. There was in depth
discussion on the projects
Tip 1: Now you need to understand that asking about your projects is a blessing in
disguise because it is your playground to play with as anything can be asked in core
subjects or DSA but Projects is what you have done and accomplished, so make sure you
know everything about your projects. (Be ready with questions like why you did it? What
problem did you solve? Try to include such projects which are solving real world
problems. Then make sure you have an idea of the tech stacks used and the alternatives
to them and why you chose what is implemented in the Project. Some may even ask to
write code of a particular function)
--- PAGE 2 ---
Then they proceeded to ask about the database schema for my project. They gave me tricky situations
and how I would handle the database. They were satisfied with my application of concepts.
Tip 2: The answers to these questions lied in basic applications of concepts of
Normalization, Candidate Keys, using Relational Database. So make sure when you
study core subjects you understand the concept rather than the theory so as to
understand where they are applicable and what kind of problems they resolve.
Then they asked me to explain about types of Joins in SQL. Now the answer to this question is simple,
but I made sure that I was explaining each type with clarity by communicating and simultaneously
drawing a diagram on the page. So they are satisfied with the answer enough to change the topic.
Then the interviewer asked me about OOPs concepts, what is overriding and give a real life example of
when would you implement it. They expected Java, however I said that my primary language is C++. I
was able to convince them that I possess fundamental conceptual clarity and can easily switch to Java if
necessary. They were very pleased with my answers.
Tip 3: All the Banks majorly use Java so it's a plus if you are already familiar with
it. Make sure to know all the concepts OOPs including real life examples of
applications of each pillar and subtypes. And if you use C++, make sure you know
the difference between them.
Then they asked me about the different types of databases, are you familiar with mongo db? What are
key value pairs? Which is suitable for your project?
Then they asked about my ML project and they wanted to know what was done after the results were
achieved. I explained the purpose of the project and whatever lies beyond the results is out of scope of
the problem.
Tip 4: Here I could've given a simple no as an answer that nothing is done after the
Data Analysis and Model building, but I made sure that the interviewers don't get
disappointed by the limited scope of the project by explaining the procedures I
followed and learning them was the main purpose. This way the interviewers
understand that you have a learning attitude and you learnt something valuable from
the project implementation.
Then they asked me to explain Data Structure and Algorithms in layman terms to someone who doesn't
know anything about it. Then I gave them a detailed explanation using easy to understand terms and
basic understanding of why Data Structures are used and what are they used for and then what is
Algorithms and what are they used for
Tip 5: These types of questions can be answered only when you study concepts with
conceptual clarity. So a tip would be to make sure whenever you are learning
something to constantly ask why? Why is something used, what is the need for it?
Then they asked me a medium- hard DSA question on how will you reach a root node from a leaf node
given that it is a directed acyclic graph pointing from parent to children. This is a tricky question, so
give it a thought !
Then they asked me about my leadership position as Head of Finance and how I manage finances and
did I automate the process.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Then they asked me if I had any questions for them. I asked them two questions. The first one was if
there is a Role in Research and Analytics working on AI/ML engines of the company? They explained
that first you have to work for 18 months before switching to a role and then depending upon the
requirements. Then I asked what if someone faces an unfamiliar technology while working on the
project what are the opportunities provided for upskilling the employee at UBS?

3. Round 3: HR Round Around 20 students appeared for this round

I was called within 15-20 minutes of my first round for HR. This was a very short round which hardly
lasted for 5-10 minutes. Make sure you are well prepared for the generic HR questions on Strengths,
Passion, Future Plans, Family Background. Work preference. Attending ppt is a must and making notes.
Tip 5: HR rounds may seem easy but you have to play safe here, as this is also the
round where you have a lot to lose if something goes wrong as you have worked
hard enough and the luck was in your favor to have qualified till here. So don't take
it lightly, be well prepared with your answers, create an impression. Don't ask for
feedback (never), don't talk about negatives or anything. The atmosphere at all
times should be positive.
12 students were offered the role and I was one of them !!!.

--- PAGE 2 ---

1.     Online Assessment [209 candidates appeared for this round]

OA for UBS had a duration of around 85 minutes. It was conducted on HackerRank platform and we had
to give it from our college (offline mode).

1. Comprised of 15 technical questions, 15 - 20 aptitude questions and lastly 1 dsa problem.

2. The problem statement for DSA question was ,

Given 2 arrays named as serverLoad & serverCapacity, the goal is to minimise total cost of the server.
For Example,
serverLoad = [7, 2, 7, 3], serverCapacity = [4, 1, 5, 6],
The total cost of server is calculated as -  7 * 4 + 2 * 1 + 7 * 5 + 3 * 6 = 83 (dot product of 2 initial arrays)
In order to minimise the cost of server , the problem statement mentioned that you can swap the position of
elements in serverCapacity only. The objective is to find the sequence of serverCapacity that results in the
minimum total cost. In case multiple sequences result in the same minimum total cost, return the sequence
that is lexicographically smallest.
In the above example, elements of serverCapacity can be arranged in a order [4, 6, 1, 5], and the dot product
with the serverLoad (elements of serverLoad are not altered)  - 7 * 4 + 2 * 6 + 7 * 1 + 3 * 5  = 62 (total cost).
But note that there is also 1 possible sequence which could minimize total cost which is [1, 6, 4, 5].
(7 * 1 + 2 * 6 + 7 * 4 + 3 * 5  = 62).
Now for sequence s1 [4, 6, 1, 5] and s2 [1, 6, 4, 5], s2[0] < s1[0]
So the output would be sequence - [1, 6, 4, 5]
Approach that came to my mind - Greedily, dot product of 2 arrays will be minimized if larger numbers
from one array are multiplied with smaller numbers from the other array and vice versa. . So I sorted
serverCapacity array and mapped the maximum value with minimum value of serverLoad.
Elements of serverLoad mapped with serverCapacity -
7 -> [4, 1]
3 -> [5]
2 -> [6]
Now for each key, I sorted the list in ascending order.
7 -> [1, 4]

3 -> [5]
2 -> [6]
After that I created an array of size serverLoad and assigned each value by iterating over the map.
I thought this would give me TLE, because for each key I was performing sort on the corresponding values,
but to my surprise it passed all the test cases.

Technical mcqs were straightforward, which contained questions on -

1. 4 - 5 questions on MySQL queries, normalization.

2. 4 - 5 questions on guess the output of the given code, output of bitwise operation ( &, | ), type casting

(all ques were based on C++).

3. 2 - 3 questions based on Data structure. (3-Ary Tree, map interface, dynamic list)

4. Questions on Java classes, package and synchronized keyword.

Aptitude mcqs were bit tricky and time consuming. It contained questions on -

1. 4 - 5 questions on probability, PnC, sets, intervals.

2. 3 - 4 questions on complete the series / find element in the series.

For Example -

1. ABC, ABC2,  AB2C2, A2B2C2, ? (guess the next element)

2. A10, A12, B18, B42, __, C882 (fill the blank)

3. 1234, 1024, 78, 1556, ?

3. 2 - 3 questions on Letter and Symbol series.

4. 3 - 4 questions on Diagramatic reasoning.

5. 1 question on mirror image of given sequence.

Tip -
In my opinion, when weightage is not assigned to each component, it is best to start with the coding questions
first, followed by the technical mcqs, and finally the aptitude questions.
Also even if you are not able to think the optimal approach, just code a brute force soln and submit it, because
some of them were shortlisted  for interviews based on aptitude and technical mcqs  even if they didn't clear
all the test cases of the problem.

3. Offline Technical Round - 1 [36 candidates appeared for this round]

I had 2 interviewers on my panelist which were very friendly and chill. At the start, they were just having fun
with me, although I was nervous (don't know why) but they made me comfortable. They began the interview
by asking me to tell them about myself . Based on my introduction, they started to ask me why I only knew
JavaScript only and not TypeScript (TS), as I had mentioned JS as one of my primary language s. To this, I
answered that I have use TS in my projects, but I am not as proficient in it as I am in JS. Then they asked why
one should use TS over JS. I responded that TS is more stricter version of JS, most of the github repo I looked
upto where in TS, and the community support of TS is excellent.
After that, they asked me if I knew React, to which I replied yes, but they didn't ask any further questions on
it.
In my resume, I had mentioned about implementing virtual stock market  (vsm) using Paytm Websocket, so
they asked me why WebSocket and not traditional HTTP request - response can be used for vsm. I broke the
question into 2 parts by explaining what WebSocket is and how does it work and same for HTTP. I explained
that if HTTP is used in place of ws then the client needs to request each second to server because the share

price of any stock keeps on fluctuating in seconds. They then asked how do you call an api from the frontend.
I explained them that I can use fetch method which return s a promise. Then they immediately asked what is
promise, promise status - pending, fullfilled / resolved  or rejected. Then I was asked to write the code for
same.
fetch(api).then((res) => { // logic }).catch((err) => { // log error })
Then they asked me about HTTP status code that I have used in my projects , and what do you mean by the
error 'resource not available'. Then they moved on to explain left join, right join, inner join, outer join, self
join in MySQL. They indirectly asked about normalization by inquiring why should one create multiple tables,
why not to keep data in one table only. To which I replied by giving an example and told that 3 anomalies
would arise - insertion, deletion and updation. Then they asked me to tell one use case where developer should
not normalize the table / relation !. I replied that if a table is decompose into more tables, then the query would
take more time to process as it would required join operations to retrieve data. Then they asked me to name
sorting algos, and which one I would prefer all the time. I replied that I would use Merge sort over other
because the worst case TC of it is O(n * log(n)).
Then they asked me some typical HR questions about my strengths, weakness, role model, why I joined SPIT,
why did I chose CE department.
The entire round took duration of around 30 - 40 mins.

4. Offline HR Round [around 20 candidates appeared for this round]

Like the technical round, the HR round was also relaxed and informal. I was asked about my family
background, where I see myself in two years, my interests outside of academics, whether I plan to pursue
higher studies, how many interviews I had before UBS and why I want to join UBS. At the end, I asked her a
few questions about idea sharing and internal hackathons.
The entire round took duration of around 15 - 20 mins.
At the end of the day, a total of 12 candidates received job offers.

assessments. Interviews involve a bit of luck and depend significantly on the panel you get.

1. Pre Placement Talk (31-07-2024)
