same. The interview started on the similar lines with me providing my introduction to the
panelist. Then he introduced himself and gave some information about the overall process for
this round. Then we started with the DSA questions.

1. Given a grid of size mxn, suppose a person is standing at the top of the grid and he needs to

reach the last row of the grid. An array of indexes (i, j) A is given where on the kth A[k] cell of
the grid is filled with water and blocked. Return the maximum number of days after which the
person is still able to reach the last row of the grid
Approach:
--- PAGE 4 ---
i. Initially I was a bit confused with the problem statement and spent some time clearing
my doubts regarding the same. After which I instantly provided the brute force solution of filling
one block at a time and then performing dfs to check the possibility of reaching the goal.
ii. The panelist told me to improve the same and after that I discussed different
approaches but they provided no significant improvement. After a hint from the panelist I was
able to arrive at the binary search based maximization + dfs based approach.
ili. I was told to write the complete code in my preferred language and the time and space
complexity for the same.

2. Given a graph with R, G, B colored edges where Alice can walk on R colored edges, Bob can

walk on G colored edges and both of them can walk on B colored edges. Return the number of
edges that can be removed from the graph such that Alice and Bob can still reach all the nodes.
Approach:
i. As it was needed to reduce the number of edges I approached this problem using a
Minimum Spanning Tree. The panelist told me that I was in the right direction.
ii. After some discussion I arrived at a modified Prim's algorithm solution where two
different visited arrays would be used to mark the arrival at a particular node.
ili. I was told to write the pseudocode for the same as the remaining time left was less.
Finally after the interview I got to ask the panelist what all tasks were normally a part of his role.
The interview lasted for around 1 hr 25 min. 9 students were shortlisted for the last round.

4. Hiring Manager Round (9 students appeared for this round)

So I was overall confident about this around as having read all the interview experiences of the
seniors I had a lot to talk about in my resume. As I had been actively participating in hackathons
, I had work experience as well as experience of working in a committee.
The interview started at 5pm. The interviewer was the Head of Engineering and led around 17
teams. I gave my introduction to him after which he started asking me questions based on my
resume.
Initially, he started by asking about my internship experience. So I have been working at the
same startup for 1 year. He was curious to know what was the reason behind the same. I
explained each and every project which I had developed and the overall growth that I
experienced in using different tech stacks.
--- PAGE 5 ---
After which he asked me about my experience with hackathons as I had mentioned my
achievements regarding the same. I explained some of my projects which I had made during the
hackathons.
Then he asked me about my experience as the Technical Head of CSI where I explained about
my role and responsibilities. The overall experience is about the same.
He asked me about my favorite application, which I told as Instagram and then he asked me how
the stories feature is implemented in the same. I explained about the priority based sorting which
he verified himself by checking the app on his phone.
He asked me some situational questions about resolving conflicts, working in a team. The criteria
that I used for shortlisting people for the hackathon. A tech based startup I would like to build if I
was provided funding and time for the same.
He also asked me about a feature I would want PhonePe to have. Here the conversation with the
second panelist helped me understand how the PhonePe SDK was still under development for
TypeScript. I discussed the same and how I would have used it instead of other options.
Finally, he asked me about my weaknesses to which I answered based on the facts that were
quite evident from my resume. I asked him what all tasks were a part of his role.
Finally 6 students were offered the I + FTE role and I was one of them.

0. [Coding Round (OA)] [291 shortlisted (*Everyone who applied)]

Platform: DoSelect || Questions: 4 || Time: 1hr 30mins

Tips:

1. You don't need to solve all questions to get shortlisted (it's points-based with each question having

100 points, with partial marking based on the number of questions)

2. Read all questions properly and then focus on the ones which you are sure you can do.

3. Try your brute force approach (or whatever approach that comes to your mind first), there's a high

chance that most test cases or all will be accepted.

4. You should be aware of how to take i/p in your specific language, especially for space-separated lists

as input.
Questions:

1. Subarray XOR question with divisibility check

Given: An array of length n, find the (sum of lengths/count [not sure which]) of subarrays whose
XOR (^) has an even number of divisors
Approach: Bruteforce passed all test cases → O(n')

• Using 2 loops get all subarrays → O(n?)

• Perform xor of each of those arrays → O(n)

Find the number of divisors for the XOR'ed value and if the number number of
divisors is even, then add it to the ans (it was either to return the number of such
subarrays or to add up the lengths of such subarrays) → O(sqrt(x)) [here x is the max
value of xor operation that might be possible i.e. INT_MAX]

2. XOR-based Sorting

Given: An array of length n, make it as sorted as possible (and print it) i.e. lexicographically ordered
with a constraint that you can swap any two values only if their XOR is less than 4
Approach: Bruteforce passed 9/10 test cases → O(n?)
--- PAGE 2 ---

• Using two nested loops i and j, check if arr[i] > arr[j] and (arr[i])XOR(arr[j]) < 4 then

perform a swap

3. Unique String with sub-string sort queries

Given: A binary string of length n consisting of O's and 1's and k queries consisting of a pair (Ir),
sort the substring(between 1 and r) in the original string and return the number of unique strings after
performing the operations k times.
Approach: Bruteforce passed 2/8 test cases → O(k*nlogn)

• For each operation, create a new string with the sorted substring from index 1 to r, 1 and r

were one indexed

• Add the new string to a set and after all queries return the length of the set

• Optimization, instead of sorting, we can perform a counting sort. This is because of the nature

of the string containing only O's and 1's, so instead of the Onlogn) due to sorting we can
reduce that part to O(n) making the overall time complexity as O(k*n)

4. Dependency question

Given: N number of initial edges (transitive dependencies) of a directed Graph, Perform three types
of operations given k operations
Approach: 9/9 test cases passed
Create an initial graph (adj list or instead of a list in the hashmap, you can have a set making
the delete operation more efficient),
Types of operations, Given k operations,
Type 1: Insert a new dependency i.e. add a new edge u,v to the pre-existing graph → O(1)
Type 2: Delete a dependency i.e. edge u,v (not necessary that it already exists) → O(1)
Type 3: Given u,v check if a path exists between them (apply DFS), the exact wording wasn't
to check if a path exists but after giving it some thought and dry running the example test
case it was easy to understand → O(V + E)
[Technical Round 11[30 Shortlisted]
This interview happened the very next day of the OA so there was little to no time for any last-minute prep.
The interview began with my introduction followed by my interviewer's introduction. It is important to be
attentive to their intro. Asking questions at the end of the interview aligning to their role makes a difference.
In my case, the interviewer was a backend developer managing customer experiences (such as the chatbot in
the app). I was curious about the fact that they had 100+ microservices, something that was highlighted
during the PPT. Also, I was curious about their reliance on cloud providers (if any, SPOILER alert, they
don't use any cloud providers, everything is on-premise). I asked these 2 questions at the end of the
interview and we had quite a discussion on them. Also, my interviewer was quite impressed with my
introduction as he found it to be quite relevant, especially my work experience and the cloud part that I had
worked on.
I was asked 2 DSA questions, the second one was common for all panels occurring concurrently.

1. Given an array of messaging queues, each element in the array houses the number of messages in

each queue. At time H minutes, all the messages in the queues get cleared out. You have a
single-threaded process that can consume K messages/minute. Find the minimum k value such that
you can consume all messages present in each queue before the reset operation happens after H
minutes. The consuming process can't move to the next queue until all messages have been
--- PAGE 3 ---
consumed. Also if you have say 30 messages in queue 0 and your K is say 32, that means you'd have
cleared 30 messages and you could still clear 2 more messages of the next queue but that isn't
allowed, you have to wait and then move to the next queue.
Before proceeding with the question I was asked whether I knew what async messaging queues were
and I had previously used Apache Kafka for my final year major project which left a good
impression at the very beginning of the interview.
Approach:

• Over the top of my head, I said that the max value of the array should be the K value, but that

was wrong because there is also the I value that you need to consider. Also at this point, I
clarified with the interviewer that the value of H should necessarily be greater than or equal
to the length of the Queue to which the interviewer agreed.

• The interviewer then gave me the correct answer for the initial test case which made me

realise that it could be any value between the minimum and maximum value of the array.
After which it dawned on me that this is pretty much a binary search with a check function
that verifies whether or not the selected value (mid) works within the H value constraint

• To solidify my approach, I asked for another test case and performed a dry run explaining

each step to the interviewer. He agreed that this was the correct and optimal approach.

2. Given an array of pairs of start and end time (s,e) indicating when a flower is visible in a garden

where s and e are inclusive. Find the number of flowers that are visible to the i person given we
have the time at which the person visits the garden:
Approach:

1. (Brute force) Simply go through the people, with a nested loop and go through the pairs of

start and end time and you can find the number of visible flowers. This approach but the TC
would be ON*M), where N is the number of people and M is the number of flowers.

2. I was asked to optimise and after talking about the complexity of the previous solution, All I

could think of was binary search. I just straight up asked the interviewer what the expected
TC would be of the optimal solution and they said if they told me that I would know exactly
what to do. So I asked for one more test case and tried my binary search approach by sorting
the pairs based on start time. It was correct for person[0] but not for person[1]. When I did
this dry run, the interviewer told me that I was on the right path and asked me to maybe think
of using two binary searches as my approach was failing for a specific edge case.

3. I then made a sorted copy of the pairs, sorted based on the end times and tried my same

approach, I performed 2 binary searches, the first one returned the index up to which all
flowers had been sown using the check that the start_time <= target (ith persons visit time).
This consisted of flowers that died as they no longer were visible.

4. This is where the second Binary search comes into play, you find the number of flowers that

have died (i.e not visible) before the target time i.e check if end time < target.

5. The number of flowers visible is the absolute difference between the two indexes returned

from each of the Binary Searches
I was asked my preferred language to code and then I was asked to write the code for both problems and a
brief description of the Time and Space complexity of the solutions.

Tips:

--- PAGE 4 ---

1. A wrong approach won't reduce your chances of getting selected, the interviewer will immediately

correct you. All you have to do is understand why your approach is wrong and then patch your
approach or move to a new approach.

2. Ask for test cases and do dry runs on them whilst explaining your approach. You can ask for hints

but don't ask for optimal time complexity hints.

3. Time and Space complexity is a must.

After asking my questions, I was sent for my 3i round immediately, instead of the 2"d round
2.
[Technical Round 21[14 Shortlisted]
In my case, this round happened after round 3. I had 2 interviewers in my panel and was again asked 2 DSA
questions. Similar to the previous round I was first asked my introduction but I purposefully cut short on it,
because I was informed that this Round would have 2 questions that had to be solved within 50 minutes
with the last 5 minutes for Questions from my end.

1. Given a N*M matrix initially set to O's, where 0 indicates land and 1 indicates water. Each day at

some i, j the land will turn into water, this is the provided input, with the number of rows and cols.
We have to find the max day on which we could still reach the last row from the top row.
Approach:

1. Started with explaining the brute force approach, performing dfs from each element of the top

row (if it is O) and if we reach the bottom then we return true. Followed by which we will fill
the grid based on the input one by one and trying the dfs operation again. This approach was
agreed to be correct but an optimization was needed.

2. I struggled a bit here for a few mins, I did optimize it slightly but that would reduce the

amortized complexity rather than the asymptomatic complexity and is much more reliant on
the Test case.

3. I asked for a hint on what exactly from my approach should I optimise because I was clear

that there is no other way better way than DFS to know if I can reach the bottom. The
interviewer agreed and said that I needed to reduce the number of DFS calls that I was
making. That's when it struck me that I have to perform a binary search on the input array
(indicating positions) fill up to the mid of each iteration of the binary search and then perform
DFS. This approach was accepted by both interviewers followed by being asked to write and
explain the code and a time complexity discussion.

2. LC 1579. Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable

This question was quite tricky, I knew this question and the name of the algorithm (Union-Find) that
is required to solve this question as it was part of this year's LC Daily questions. I had forgotten how
the algorithm worked, so I proceeded to solve it with a completely open mind.
I gave them a backtracking approach but at the same time I acknowledged that the Time Complexity
of such a solution would be exponential. After this the interviewer gave me a hint regarding how I
should treat Alice and Bob as 2 different graph components. This is exactly what I had done while
solving this question on LC but without knowing how the algo worked completely, I was again stuck
I took a few test cases to try and get to the answer of that test case. Using the previous hint, I created
the two components and then told the interviewer that the superimposition of both graphs would
result in the graph consisting of the minimum edges. They agreed but by that time I had run out of
time. I was quite nervous that maybe I had flunked this round but the interviewer told me that I
--- PAGE 5 ---
should look up the Union-Find Algorithm and also that I was pretty close to the solution which gave
me some hope.
I asked a few questions based on their role, they both were in the same team working as Sr. Backend
Developers in the Billings team (the section of recharges, bill payments, etc in the app)

3. [Tech+HR Round (Hiring Manager Round)| [9 Shortlisted]

I was interviewed by the App Dev Manager at PhonePe who led around 20 teams at PhonePe. This was not
exactly an HR round because the people interviewing had technical knowledge. Now that I'm writing about
this experience, one thing that I feel helped seal the deal with my manager was that I was quite considerate
about my behaviour, For example: I had to take the stairs to reach the lab where my interview would take
place and as soon as I got in along with the interviewer, he asked me about the 1s work exp on my resume.
As soon as I started my breath got heavy because I came in a hurry and took the stairs, the interviewer told
me that at one point he was also on the other side and that it was alright if I needed a break for a few
minutes. I asked whether I could have some water and also asked him If he wanted some water.
After I was back in a minute or two, the interviewer asked a few questions such as where I live and a bit
about my family members, their background, etc. These are standard questions that are asked to calm a
candidate down.
Tip: You can always ask for a few minutes before the interview especially if you need water or something
specific.
After these standard questions, we came back to the initial questions, about my work exp. There was a
detailed discussion on how I was able to get that opportunity (it was a freelance gig). A bit about how it
works, the system design, etc. The reason for the opportunity was because of my contribution in building
TechRace which then made the interviewer a bit more interested in it. We then discussed in length about
TechRace. This also got my interviewer curious about how and why I had learned Flutter.
After that, we moved to another project which was built at a hackathon. After I told him that I used to
actively participate in a hackathon before the placement season, He asked me a few situational questions
such as what would you do if your team member wasn't delivering things on time, how would you tell a
person that they are not fit for the task, have you ever had a conflict with any team member or teacher.
After this, I was asked about a feature that I'm impressed with; in any app or website and also a feature that
I'd like to see in some app. I was also asked my favourite app in context to these questions. I spoke about
Spotify and how they put the lyrics feature behind a hard paywall i.e. you need premium to view them. He
then asked me what would I do differently in this case as also the company needs to earn money as well. So
I gave him an example of a soft paywall, similar to the analyze complexity button on leetcode as it allows
2-3 free tries each day and Spotify could do the same. The interviewer liked this approach.
For the feature that I found impressive, I spoke about the Tap to Pay feature, present in apps like Gpay,
Paytm and PhonePe(I said I was not sure it is present in PhonePe). After that, I explained how I tried a
hacky way of trying to get it to work with the Mumbai Metro Card using an NFC reader app that can clone
and read data from an NFC card i.e. tap to pay cards. I told him that on inspection I found an encrypted
string. But when I tried to use it on the Metro terminal that didn't work. After this, the interviewer asked me
how the entire process works in reality. I spoke about tokenization and how some data is added as a payload
--- PAGE 6 ---
such as user_id and encrypted using some asymmetric hashing algorithm with the metro servers having the
public key that can decrypt the payload and then check in the DB if I have enough money to travel and
based on that the metro gate is opened.
I was asked about what domain I would build my startup in, given I was provided with the required capital. I
told him about an Idea that I had which I had implemented as my Semester long Mini Project.
I was also asked if I'd like to join the App team or Backend team at PhonePe and also questions such as
whether I would choose Cross-platform (Flutter, React native) or Native (Kotlin, Swift) for building a
production app. I chose Native and explained why as well.
I was asked a few basic HR questions like strengths that make me different from other candidates my
weaknesses and how I've grown away from them.
At the end, I asked them about why they were not relying on any cloud providers (as stated in the previous
round but I forgot to ask the reason at that time). I asked a few more questions which led to a deep
discussion on how PhonePe used React Native to integrate components from their Partners like Ixigo for
flight booking within the App (built with Kotlin for Androd and Swif for iOS). Also when we left, I opened
the door for him and I thought that he had left while I was turning off all the lights and fans, but he waited
whilst holding the door for me and may have noted that down as well. These basic etiquette also play some
role so be on your A-game.
6 candidates received the offer. This year all of us received I+FTE offers.

• The interviewers are very friendly, even if you start with a wrong approach, or aren't able to reach a

thinking and how you are reaching a solution.

3. [Technical Round 21 [ 13 candidates were shortlisted]

The interview started at around 2pm. Again this round was solely DSA based.
Initially the interviewer asked me for my introduction and then a jist about my resume and then the DSA
question started.
The 1 st question was:
https://leetcode.com/problems/remove-max-number-of-edges-to-keep-graph-fully-traversable/descriptio
This question was quite tricky, I knew this question and the name of the algorithm (Union-Find) that
is required to solve this question as it was part of this year's LC Daily questions.
So I was easily able to provide the solution to this question. The interviewer then asked me about the time
complexity and told me to write the pseudo code of the solution.
The 2nd Question:
Given N*M grid initially with all 1's in it. We can start from 1st row and can move in any direction. The
goal is to reach the last Column. Each day a coordinate will be provided, and a blocker will be added to
the given coordinate. The question was to find the day from which we no longer will be able to reach the
last column.
I started with the brute force approach of using dfs for each case and then finding the answer. Later i tried to
optimize it but the interviewer was looking for a much better solution. After thinking a lot i was still not
able to reach a solution.
The interviewer then told me that we could binary solution for this question.
Hater understood the reason and then the interviewer asked me to write the pseudo code for it. Which i did.
The 3rd Question:
This question was a medium leetcode question: https://leetcode.com/problems/decode-ways/description/
I quickly gave the recursion solution for it and then optimized it by giving the memoization solution and
then the tabulation solution for it.
Then I wrote the pseudo code and explained the time complexity for the same.
The interviewer then asked if i had any questions for him, I asked about the technical challenges the
company was facing. We had a discussion about it and the round ended.

Tips:

• Don't lose your confidence if you aren't able to answer, keep trying but once you know you wont be

able to reach the solution let the interviewer know, don't beat around and try to fool the interviewer.
--- PAGE 4 ---

• Know about the time complexity and how it works, because after each question you will be asked to

explain their time complexity and space complexity.

3. Hiring Manager Round [9 students]

This round lasted over an hour, and the interviewer was an Engineering Manager at PhonePe.
The interviewer was very chill and it mostly was a discussion round, Initially he started with my
introduction and then he asked me about my preparation for the placements.
Then he asked me about how I developed skills and balanced academics along with it. Later he asked me
questions on one of the projects on my resume which he liked and we had a little discussion about it.
He then moved on to ask me questions about my hackathon experiences and how do I go about forming
a team about the same. This discussion was followed by a question as to what would be my approach to
learning if I joined Phone Pe as a full time engineer. He then asked me a feature I would like to
implement on any of the UPI apps.
He was quite impressed with the answer I gave. Lastly he asked me about any conflicts i have faced while
working in teams, and how i resolved them and also a few questions on my committee experiences.
In the end I asked him about his experience after joining Phone Pe.
6 students received the offer (Intership+FTE).

Tips:

• Keep your calm while giving your interviews. The interviewers are there to help you, keep

conveying your thoughts and approaches to them, do not stop talking.

• The interviewer is looking for how much you are willing to learn and not how much you

already know.

• Try and relate your answers to real life experiences, those give you an edge and shows the

interviewer your skills to learn from your environment.
All the best for your placements!

moving from top to bottom and then bottom to top again, we collect fruits and then they replaced by a 0. We
need to collect the maximum fruits.
I started with a dp solution and a traversal technique, but wasn't able to reach the correct answer, however
after the help of the interviewer, i was able to reach to a solution.

The interviewer was happy with solution and the round ended.

complexity and told me to write the pseudo code of the solution.

last column.
I started with the brute force approach of using dfs for each case and then finding the answer. Later i tried to

learning if I joined Phone Pe as a full time engineer. He then asked me a feature I would like to
implement on any of the UPI apps.
He was quite impressed with the answer I gave. Lastly he asked me about any conflicts i have faced while

In the end I asked him about his experience after joining Phone Pe.

conveying your thoughts and approaches to them, do not stop talking.

• The interviewer is looking for how much you are willing to learn and not how much you

already know.

interviewer your skills to learn from your environment.

There were a total of 3 rounds conducted for the role of data analyst. All of these rounds were in the form of
interviews. 46 people had been shortlisted by resume to appear for the first round.

1. SOL Round [46 candidates ]

The first round took around half an hour. The interviewer introduced herself and then asked me to introduce
myself as well. In all three rounds my introduction was very basic and only included my name, branch, and
my interests in the aspect of data analysis which led me to apply for this position. After that we began the
SQL evaluation. I was provided with an excel sheet which had two tables and there were 7 questions based
on the data provided in those tables, for which I was asked to write queries. Most of these questions
involved joins, some involved the group by - having clause and one involved using a window function. Then
I was asked to explain the logic behind the queries, and modify them according to certain conditions. I did
make a mistake in one question, but then I was given a hint and I was able to correct it. I only completed 6
out of the 7 queries because of a bit of network delay which took up a lot of time, so we skipped the last
question. Then I was asked if I had any questions, and then we were done with this round.
I had prepared for this round by only doing two things - watching a comprehensive video of SQL from
basics to advanced, paying special attention to joins, group by - having, and window functions; and then
searching for difficult sql questions asked in interviews and practicing them. I feel that if you get the essence
of how these clauses and functions work, you will be good to go.

2. Problem-Solving Round [24 candidates ]

In this round the panel had two interviewers. They introduced themselves and asked me to do the same.
After that the first question I was asked was on guesstimates: - estimate the number of cars in Mumbai. I
took some random estimates about the number of people who would be able to afford a car and then
mentioned multiple factors which would affect the same, this led me to an estimate about the number of
privately owned cars. I thought my answer would end here, but then the panel hinted on the fact that I had
missed something out, and I realized I had to estimate the number of taxis as well. Here too I took a very
--- PAGE 2 ---
wild guess as to the number of people who work as taxi drivers and made my calculations based on that, and
my approach seemed to satisfy the panel.
The second question was slightly on the mathematical logic side, as it was based on averages. The essence
of the question was as follows: -
Let there be 4 values x, a, y and b.
We have a value R = (xa + yb)/(xty)
If both a and b increase, is there any situation where R can decrease?
Here I gave an incorrect answer. I immediately said no as the value of R is directly proportional to both a
and b. But I was asked to take a minute to think and re-evaluate my answer. This was a pretty obvious sign
that my answer was incorrect. Even so, I was very unsure that such a situation was possible. Still I kept
talking and shared my reasoning so as to why I believed this situation was not possible. But then I was given
a hint about breaking down the equation and from there I realized how this question could be answered, and
I then explained what I understood and gave the solution, and the panel seemed satisfied. Again I was asked
if I had any questions, and then we were done with this round.
To practice for this round, I had searched up common guesstimate questions and puzzle-type questions asked
in interviews and gone through the common approaches for the same.

3. HR Round [10 candidates ]

The HR round was the only interview round conducted in-person. It was taken by Ranaq Sen sir who is the
Head of People at WI.
This round was very unlike typical HR interviews, none of the questions that were asked was something I
had a prepared answer for. I was first asked to introduce myself, there I had mentioned certain strengths and
interests which sir discussed a bit in detail. Then I was asked about my opinions on the field of data science.
I was also asked about my hobbies, which led to a bit of a relaxed environment as we discussed novels I had
read. Then I was asked what direction I would want my career to take in the future, or more simply, what I
would like to be doing for the next year or two. Here I emphasized the fact that I had a genuine interest in
the role of a data analyst, and for the future part I gave a pretty non-traditional answer and included the fact
that I was considering higher studies in the future along with other job prospects. I felt it was not correct to
do so at first, but at the end of the interview when I asked sir for feedback/advice, he complimented my
honesty on the topic and added how that is one of the core values of the company. I got a bit more general
advice from sir and here my interview ended.
A total of 5 students had been selected for the role of Data Analyst in the end.

Process had a total of 3 rounds, before that there was a resume-based shortlisting.

1. Round 1 : SQL Round [46 candidates appeared for this round]

The round was conducted in offline mode but on a gmeet with 1 interviewer in the panel. This was based
purely on SQL for me and went for about 30 mins. Firstly, the interviewer introduced herself and than
asked for mine. Keep it short, not more than 45 secs.  An Excel sheet containing two tables (customers
and orders) and their schemas was shared with me. I was asked to solve 7 queries, ranging from easy to
medium LeetCode questions. After solving each question, I explained my logic and approach, during
which the interviewer either cross-questioned or asked for modifications. The questions primarily involved
joins, aggregates, and subqueries. Do practice and understand MySQL functions (datetime, string, math),
CTEs and window functions (lag, lead, row number, rank, dense rank, etc) and make sure you know the
differences between them (also get a small example ready with you to explain the differences just in case
if required).
Initially, some of us faced internet issues, so keep your laptops connected to given WiFi and even if things
like these happen do not stress out, just let your interviewer know about the same.
Additionally, got to know that some of the interviewers in other panels were asking resume-based
questions as well as tableau if mentioned so be prepared with that as well.

2. Round 2 : Problem Solving Round [Around 24 candidates appeared for this round]

The panel had two interviewers, each with 5-6 years of experience. The round started with some SQL
questions, but this time, I only needed to provide the logic rather than the complete query. Some
questions required MySQL datetime functions and it was more of real life questions.
In some panels, they conducted guesstimates, but in my case, it was a root cause analysis based on
Swiggy. Specifically, the question was: "The ratio of the number of orders placed to the number of
active users is decreasing every month (i.e., the order rate is declining monthly). What could be the
possible reasons for this?" They let me brainstorm and asked me to open the app if needed. After each
reason I gave, they acknowledged but asked for another reason. This happened about 3-4 times.

Eventually, I couldn't come up with more reasons at the moment so I let them know about the same, so
they switched the question and asked, "If the discounts given on Swiggy are reduced, what type of users
will be most affected?" (This was a sort of follow-up question since I mentioned greater discounts on
competitors like Zomato as one reason. The answer involved age groups and income levels.)
The last segment of the round was puzzles. I was asked 3-4 questions (resources mentioned below). I
got the correct answers for some on the first attempt. For the others, I was initially wrong, but they asked
me to reconsider and provided hints, which helped me arrive at the correct solutions.
Overall, this round lasted about 45-50 minutes.

3. Round 3 : Culture Round [10 candidates appeared for this round]

This round was supposed to begin at 6 pm, but since I was scheduled first in every panel and had already
completed the first two interviews by 3 pm, my turn came around 5:15 pm. The interviewer started by
introducing himself but paused midway to ask if I had attended the pre-placement talk. He then asked
for my introduction and went through my resume, focusing on one of my data-related projects. I
provided an overall brief of the project, and discussed a new project I was considering that was similar
and related to one of my achievements listed in my resume, thus highlighting the same.
Next, he asked whether I was more interested in the business or product side. We then discussed my
hobbies and whether I am still pursuing them. He also inquired about where I live, why I would prefer to
move to Bangalore, and what I like about Mumbai.
Finally, he asked why I wanted to join WorkIndia, what specific and unique qualities I liked about the
company, and how my values aligned with theirs. Overall, it was not a typical HR round but more of a
discussion to understand my personal opinions. However, remember not to get too carried away, as
they are evaluating you from the moment you enter the room. The round lasted about 30-35 minutes.
Total 5 candidates were shortlisted including me for the role.

Pro Tip #1: Make sure your introduction is not more than 30-40 seconds long, if the
interviewer still wants to ask something he/she will. Do not over answer.

round were based on the additional tables.
The queries ranged from leetcode easy to leetcode hard level problems. The first one was a simple join
query, the second one was a bit tricky and also involved calculations on date. The third was a complex
query involving subqueries, the interviewer was pretty chill and helped me by providing hints for the third
one. (Although he asked me to drop the question because he wanted me to ask another theory question)
--- PAGE 2 ---
Pro Tip #2: Whenever you are solving the question, make sure you first discuss the
approach with the interviewer. Keep explaining as you continue to write the solution.
The final question was a theory question on the different types of window functions and the difference
between them. The round lasted for about 50 minutes.

same have been provided at the end). The first part of this question was to find the number of ACs in
households while the second part involved public places.
Pro Tip #3: Ask questions related to the problem statement. For example, do we also
need to consider ACs in the buses and metros?

and Rb for the two verticals of Swiggy (Two verticals are food delivery and instamart). The two questions

gaussian distribution. (Both were pretty easy if you have basic knowledge on probability and statistics).

using the inbuilt function, I was not able to recollect the approach, but was provided with a hint from the

The first round of my interview, conducted online via Google Meet, started with a brief introduction of
myself and lasted about 30 minutes, focusing on SQL. A single interviewer asked me questions ranging
from very easy to hard Leetcode SQL queries, with the difficulty level increasing after each correct answer.
I tackled five questions in total: a simple WHERE query, a straightforward JOIN query, a more complex
query covering aggregate functions, joins, the GROUP BY clause, and window functions, and finally, a
question about the difference between DENSE_RANK() and RANK().  I was able to provide correct
answers to all the queries.

2. Round 2: Problem Solving [24 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

The second round of my interview lasted about 45  minutes. After introducing myself again, I was asked
to solve two guesstimates. The first question was to estimate the number of Maggi packets sold in India
in a day. Although I initially got stuck and confused in my approach, the interviewer guided me to solve
it using a different method. The second question was quite unique: I had  to estimate the number of liters
of alcohol required at a middle-class Punjabi wedding. I asked preliminary questions to gather necessary
details and estimated the number of guests to be 500. I categorized the guests into kids, adults, and senior
citizens, further dividing adults and senior citizens into low, medium, and high drinking capacities. After
receiving the values in milliliters for each category from the interviewer, I performed the calculations and
provided an answer. The interviewer appreciated my approach and showed interest in my response. It
is crucial to ask preliminary questions to ensure your assumptions are correct and to communicate your
thought process to the interviewer throughout the problem -solving. He then asked if I have any
questions for them.

Also, my panel did not ask me puzzles and some advance SQL, but students from other panels were asked
so make sure you prepare that too . Some students were also asked about root cause analysis of a certain
company.

3. Round 3: Culture Fit [10 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

The final round of my interview began at 7:30 pm and lasted approximately 45 to 50 minutes. The interviewer
started by introducing himself, and when it was my turn, he interrupted my prepared introduction, advising
me to avoid a rehearsed response. As our conversation progressed, it maintained a relaxed and informal tone.
The interviewer asked about the places I have visited in India and requested that I highlight the most underrated
one. He also inquired about my extracurricular activities and my ac hievements, the committees I was
involved in, and the Position of Responsibility for the college fest mentioned on my resume. He asked about
my learnings from that role and why I chose to be part of it for three years.
The interviewer then asked about my plans for further education, specifically whether I intended to pursue an
MBA or a Master's degree, suggesting that a Master's degree would enhance my profile. He wanted to know
why I believed I was a suitable fit for the role  and what unique qualities I brought to the table .
Additionally, he asked about my knowledge of WorkIndia and which of their mission values resonated with
me. Although the interviewer maintained a casual tone, it was clear that the evaluation began from the outset
of the interview.
Towards the end of the session, I had the opportunity to ask questions. Just as I did in the previous round, I
used this chance to pose well-researched and unique questions  about the company. This final interaction
was crucial for creating a lasting impression and demonstrating a genuine interest in the organization.
Total 5 students including me, were selected, and offered the I + P offer from Work India for the Data
Analyst role

1. Keep engaging with your interviewer by thinking out loud and explaining your logic when given a

question. Do not just solve the problem; the interviewer wants to understand your approach. Take a
moment to think before you start answering to avoid giving a rushed impression. If you do not know
the answer, be honest about it. If you know the approach but cannot reach the final answer, explain
your thought process.

2. It is essential to have a strong understanding of all SQL concepts. Use resources like w3schools to

reinforce your knowledge and challenge yourself by solving 50 SQL questions on platforms like
LeetCode. These problems will test your problem -solving skills and deepen your understanding of
SQL.

3. Enhance your learning by working on real -world projects related to data analysis or data science.

Applying SQL in practical scenarios will improve your logical thinking and show you how SQL fits
into larger data-driven processes.

4. Develop your critical thinking and puzzle-solving skills by engaging with challenges on platforms like

GeeksforGeeks and Brainstellar. These exercises will sharpen your problem-solving abilities.

5. Boost your confidence and refine your communication skills, as these are crucial for effective

interaction during interviews.

6. If you still have any questions or need guidance, feel free to contact me on LinkedIn

Round 1: SOL Round [ 46 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

The round was conducted in offline mode but on Gmeet with 1 interviewer in the panel. However some
panels had 2 interviewers. This round was entirely based on SQL for me and went on for about 20-25 mins.
Firstly, the interviewer asked me to introduce myself. Keep the introduction short, upto 40 sec. The
schemas for the questions were shared to me on the Gmeet chat along with the required questions one by
one. I was asked to copy these on the Notepad and write queries for the same. I was asked to solve 6 queries
ranging from leetcode easy to medium. The queries included topics like JOINS, AGGREGATE
FUNCTIONS, WILDCARDS, SUBQUERIES. Make sure you discuss the details about the schema with
the interviewer like the datatypes of the column, Primary Keys, etc. During my interview, even the columns
which consisted of numbers entirely were in the string format so pay attention to such details. Also, discuss
your approach with the interviewer and make sure to explain why you are using the necessary functions
while writing the query. I was also asked the difference between WHERE and HAVING and their use
cases. For a few of the queries the interviewer had asked me to give multiple approaches so be prepared for
that and if you are not able to give any just say so to the interviewer, they don't expect you to know
everything.
Some of us faced some connectivity issues during the start of the interview, so keep your laptops connected
to the WiFi and do not panic even if things like this happen just let the interviewer know about the same.
I was told that in some of the panels along with the SQL queries, the interviewer had also asked questions
about their projects based on the resume, so be prepared for that as well.
--- PAGE 2 ---

Round 2: Problem Solving Round [24 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

This round had a panel of two interviewers. The round started with a brief introduction of myself. This
round could be divided into two parts:

1) Guesstimates 2)Puzzles

I had a web- development project on my resume so the interviewer asked me "Why didn't I apply for the
SDE roleại Try to answer this question in a way that will support your decision of applying for the Data
Analytics role. Then I was asked to give a brief overview of the same project. The interviewer followed this
up with a guesstimate "What are the number of daily active visits on your website". I asked some
preliminary questions to clear the details about what I had to find. While solving the guesstimates and
taking approximations, always explain the reasons to the interviewer for the same. Next, I had mentioned
basketball on my resume which interested the interviewer. He asked me about my favorite team and then
asked a guesstimate to calculate the number of tickets sold by the team. However, after some initial
calculations he changed the question to calculate the total seating revenue generated by the team in a
single season. Again this was a guesstimate question so I asked some preliminary questions and confirmed
my approximations with the interviewer.
The next part of the interview was based on Puzzles and SQL. Firstly I was asked to write a SQL query. I
was unable to write the query but I explained my approach to the interviewer which was partially correct
and she seemed satisfied with it. Next she gave me the "3 ANTS AND TRIANGLE" puzzle which I was
able to solve with a hint from the interviewer. Make sure to explain your thought process to the
interviewer while thinking about the solution. The chances are that your approach is correct and just
missing a small point.
After this the interviewer asked me if I had any questions. I asked them a question related to my
web-development project which was somewhat similar to WorkIndia.
Overall, this round lasted for about 1 hr.

Round 3: Culture Fit Round [9 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

My interview was at 10pm since I was the last candidate to be interviewed. This was a complete offline
round with a face to face interview. The interview began with my introduction and asked me how I
developed interest in Data Analytics. Then he went through my resume and asked about a case study
competition that I had participated in. I gave a brief overview of the case study that we did after which he
enquired about my team. One of my team members had been interviewed just a couple of interviews ago so
he asked a couple of questions about the case study(The interviewer was probably verifying what I was
saying and if that matched with what he had said about the case study). Then he asked me whether I read
books or not. Try to be honest while giving answers to such questions like in my case I said I am more
interested in visual media rather than books.
Next, he asked me whether I was interested in the product or the business side. We then discussed my
hobbies and whether I was still pursuing them. He inquired about where I live, my family and what is their
opinion about me moving to Bangalore. He also asked me why I was not interested in going for higher
studies.
Finally he asked me why I did web-development when I wanted to work in the Data Analytics field and
then we discussed my projects. Overall, this was not a typical HR interview but more of a discussion to
--- PAGE 3 ---
understand my personality and if my values align with theirs. Answer the questions with a mix of your
own ideas and keeping the job profile in mind. The interview lasted for about 30-35 minutes.
A total of 5 students were finally offered the job including me.

For the placement process, three rounds were conducted. There was a resume shortlisting round before any
of the actual rounds happened. 182 students were shortlisted after the resume round.

1. [Case Study Round] [20 students were shortlisted to appear for this round]

About : The Case Study Round started at 8am sharp and we were given a time of 2 hrs for making PPTs for
the cases. Students were provided with a case study each based on product designing, and were supposed to
study the challenges associated, suggest new features and define success metrics for each feature. My
case-study was regarding GooglePay, others got Healtifyme and Olx. From this round, 15 people were
shortlisted ahead together for APgM/APM/AGM roles.
How I prepared for this round: I started participating in business-case competitions (mostly organized by
IITs/NITs/IIMs) almost a year before placements (5th Semester). My experience helped me a lot in this
round, because I knew the template of how case-studies work . It was all about understanding the problems
associated with the product and providing solutions.
Suggestions:
a) Try and make your resume strong in terms of internships and competitions, because skill set is all
that matters.
b) Always mention numbers in your resume to show the impact you caused by the positions you were a
part of. For eg, during my tenure as a social media & marketing intern at ABC company, our
engagement shot up by 60%.

2. Interview Round 1:1 [15 students shortlisted for APgM/APM/AGM)]

About: In this round, each of the 15 shortlisted candidates had a one-on-one interview with the industry
experts of the domains. My interview lasted for around 1 hr 30 mins. I was asked about my case study, 1
guesstimate question, 1 RCA question and why I wanted to go into Product Management. Lastly I was
asked if I had any questions for the interviewers. I think one mistake that everyone should avoid in this
--- PAGE 2 ---
round is not listening to the interviewer. Always keep communicating, keep asking the interviewers if
your approach is correct, if the values and assumptions are correct etc.
How I Prepared : Guesstimates & RCA - https://www.youtube.com/@technomanagers/playlists

3. ¡HR Round] [ 6 candidates were shortlisted for APgM/APM/AGM]

About : In this round, the interviewer asked me to introduce myself followed by questions like why I wanted
to do product management, Proud moments in my experience, About my plans for masters etc. The
round ended with me asking the interviewer a few questions.
How I Prepared: What I did was first get an idea about questions that can be asked in the HR round. You
can easily find videos on Youtube about the same, or just ChatGPT the questions for your role. Once I
had the questionnaire ready, I started building answers about them based on my interests and role applied
for.
Suggestions: My technique for answering the questions in HR round is as follows:
First, tell the interviewer about the number of points you are going to talk about.
b) For each point, use a key-word and then explain each point in brief.
For eg: Why should we hire you?
Ans. - I think you should hire me mainly because of these three reasons. Firstly, I have a proven track
record, as in I have experience in this domain.......(Brief explanation). Secondly, I have a
customer-centric approach, which means that....(Brief Explanation). And lastly, I am really
adaptable, that is I understand.... (Brief Explanation)
c) Your Introduction in the HR round should be brief, try mentioning your experience more than talking
about your technical skills and always end the introduction with telling the interviewer why you are a
good fit for the role.

The Placement process consists of 4 rounds. 1st round is resume shortlisting followed by Case
Study Round followed by the Problem Solving Interview and the last round is the Culture Fit
Interview.
For the role of APM/AGM/APGM: 45 Students were shortlisted post resume screening for the
case study round. 15 were selected for the problem solving interview and 6 were shortlisted for
the Culture Fit Interview.
It was an offline process with some interviews being held over G-Meet.

1. Resume Shortlisting Round]

Make sure your resume is of 1 page and proper formatting is maintained. Include and highlight
relevant internship experiences and courses which you have undertaken. I had made my resume
on MS Word.
[Case Study Round] [45 students appeared for this round]
The Case Study Round started at 8am sharp and we were given a time of 2 hrs for making PPTs
for the cases. Students were provided with one of 3 different case studies each based on product
design, user retention, and solutions for betterment of the product, and were also supposed to
define success metrics for each feature. My case study was regarding HealthifyMe, and
following was the problem statement:
--- PAGE 2 ---
"Healthifyme aims to increase user retention and encourage long-term usage for its users.
Despite a high number of downloads, the app struggles with retaining users beyond the first
month"
You have to be innovative and practical while suggesting the solution,it will help to stand out
amongst the rest. Allot sufficient time in understanding the problem statement,the app and the
solution which you are proposing. The content is more important than the aesthetics. There was
not a strict slide limit but try to keep it as concise as possible.
I have participated in various case study competitions and marketing competitions since the
onset of my second year which helped me a lot to understand what was expected in the solution.

3. [Problem Solving Interview Round] [ 15 candidates appeared for this round]

My interview was taken by the VP of Growth. I had prepared for this round by practicing
guesstimates and root cause analysis questions which are generally asked in this round to
check how can you solve a problem in a structured manner. To my surprise,my interview did
not consist a single question on guesstimate or RCA.The interviewer asked me questions
regarding my case study solution. Questions revolved around what problems are existing in
the app currently and as the PM how would I solve it? What features would I implement to
tackle it? The entire interview was heavily product focused and I was put in the shoes of PM
to solve situation based problems. The interview questions were very close to the real world
scenarios..It checked my problem solving skills and how differently does one think. I was
given situational based questions on Spotify and G-Meet as well. Whatever feature I
suggested as the solution, the interviewer asked few follow up questions to it. My interview
lasted for 45 minutes
Few tips:

• It is okay to ask the interviewer to give you 30-90 seconds to think about the answer.

• Make sure you have 2-3 supporting reasons for the feature you are suggesting to be

implemented

• Give mock interviews, this helps a lot.

• Expect the unexpected.

4. [Cultural Fit Interview Round] [ 6 candidates appeared for this round]

--- PAGE 3 ---
My Interview was taken by the CTO of the company. He asked me how could they improve
on their recruiting process,post which I was asked about my biggest achievement and the
lowest point in my life. Don't try to pretend to be someone which you are not. The interviewer
shall recognise it immediately. All the questions asked to me were very behavioral and
specific in nature. I could answer them easily as I responded by first thinking what would
have been my natural response if I was put in such a situation. I tried not giving an ideal
answer but an answer which resonated the most to me. I was also asked questions on the
concept of greater good and what would I do if I had 100 cr. Most of the interview revolved
around my life experiences and my actions in certain hypothetical situations. This interview
went on for an hour.
Few tips:

• Be yourself and confidently tell the values which you believe in.

• In this round the interviewer genuinely wants to know about you,so do share your

life experiences which have moulded you.

• You might be asked about company specific questions,researching about the

company would be beneficial.
Resources that helped me:
1)I referred to the casebooks by IIM A,B,C for my preparation on guesstimates along with
the videos on the Exponent Youtube Channel.
2)The course by Google on Project Management aligns significantly with this role.
3)The Product Management Books by the Product clubs of HIM A and HIM B helped me to
understand about PM in general.
LASTLY,
"BELIEVE IN YOURSELF BECAUSE IF YOU DON'T, THEN WHO WILL!"

WI campus Drive lasted for a day and consisted of 4 Rounds. The day before, we had a PPT in which we
were briefed about their values and work culture. Following that we had to submit our resumes for
shortlisting. We could only apply for only one of the 5 roles. 92 students were shortlisted after the resume
round.

1. API/Frontend Round (92 candidates appeared for this round)

We had two choices for this round in which we had to code out any one option. They were:

1. Front-end round: Create a website frontend in 2 hours. They had given a Figma mock design which

we had to replicate in any frontend framework. We were provided with APIs to load data to our page
and were evaluated based on the quality of code and the quality of UI and UX.
OR

2. API dev round: This was the one that I chose. I had to create APIs for a car rental platform

(ZoomCar) in 3 hours. They had given a problem statement and the details of 6 API endpoints we

needed to create. The details for each API included the type of request, the request data, query
parameters, the expected output, and access type (user/admin access).
After submission, I was asked to demonstrate the endpoints. Then they asked me questions about my
database schema, code structure, how I would perform some changes in the code and some theoretical
questions based on jwt/encryption. This interview lasted for 1 hour.
25 Students were shortlisted for the next round.
Tips for this round:

1. Prepare on topics like jwt and hashing since these are required almost every time. Also have some

experience in role based access.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. It is compulsory to use SQL as the database. So have some practice so that you can build the schema

and prepare APIs within the time constraint.

3. You are allowed to use google. But using Al tools and copying an existing project is not allowed.

4. Use different folders for routes, controllers and middleware. Ensure that you are following proper

coding conventions.

5. Have the postman or curl requests ready so that you can quickly demonstrate it to the interviewers.

2. Technical Round 1[18 students appeared for this round]

This round primarily focused on DSA. I was asked 2 DSA questions. The first question was a
straightforward question in which I had to find the 3 least performing Engineers in the current year. I
initially suggested a brute force approach by sorting and then I gave him the optimized approach using max
heap. The second question was to partition the array into k parts so that the max sum of the partitions is
minimum.
This question was same as :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/split-the-given-array-into-k-sub-arrays-such-that-maximum-sum-of-all-sub-a
rrays-is-minimum/
Initially I gave him the brute force approach, but he was not satisfied. After some thinking, I realized it was
a binary search problem. I was required to share my screen and write the pseudo-code. The interviewer also
asked me to perform a dry run and tell him about the time and space complexity of each solution.
This round lasted for around 1 hour.
Tips for this round:

1. Be as interactive as possible with the interviewer, and let him know what you are thinking.

2. If you want any clarifications, be sure to ask since the interviewer expects and welcomes it.

3. Ensure you communicate the meaning of your pseudo-code properly along with the reasons for your

decisions.

3. Technical Round 2[10 students appeared for this round]

This round primarily focused on SQL. I was asked to prepare a schema for an e-commerce website. The
interviewer was really helpful and I ran all my ideas through him while building the schema. In case I was
going in the wrong direction the interviewer nudged me to the right path. I was also asked some standard
questions like differences/advantages/disadvantages of NoSQL over SQL databases. Then I was asked to
perform database queries on my schema which was easy to medium level questions on leetcode.
This round also lasted for around 1 hour.
Tips for this round:

1. Prepare for SQL questions using platforms like leetcode, w3 schools, etc. Ensure you complete at

least one of the SQL sheets: (the one that I did was https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/).

2. Do prepare for concepts like schema normalization, types of relationships and other standard

concepts as they will surely ask about it.
--- PAGE 3 ---

3. HR/Culture Round [ About 6 students appeared for this round]

I was interviewed by a former SPIT student and core team member of WI. He began by asking me to
introduce myself. He asked me about my college experience, and we had a brief chat on how it was different
from his time there. He proceeded to ask me about my internships and projects that I had built. Then he
asked personal questions like:

1. What's the most valuable thing for you that you currently have?

2. What's the most valuable thing for you that you are yet to receive?

3. What was the lowest point & the highest point of your life and how did you learn/improve from it?

4. What would you do if you had infinite resources (100 crs)?

5. What mistakes did you make in your college years and how did you improve on them?

6. You had the privilege to study at the prestigious SPIT. What did you do with this opportunity?

7. Why did you choose this career path?

8. Why did you choose to work in a startup like WorkIndia?

9. Would you prefer a stable work environment or environment with lots of highs and lows?

There were some more questions of the similar sort.
I was given time to think on how to answer these questions. The interviewer was really chill and encouraged
me to be honest and candid. At the end,the interviewer asked me if I had some questions for him. I asked
him about the features his team was working on as well as some questions about the business model and
advertising strategy. This round lasted for around 45 minutes.
Tips for this round:

1. Be honest. Answers that are insincere or contradict at any point will be caught by the interviewer.

2. Do take some time to think before you answer. Also add some information/evidence to support your

answer.

3. Learn about the values and goals of the company beforehand.

4. At the end, prepare a well thought out question that genuinely interests you.

Three students were offered the opportunity at WorkIndia for the role of SDE.

1. API/ Frontend Development Round

2. Technical Round 1 (DSA)

3. Technical Round 2 (Relational database schema design and queries)

4. Culture Fit Round

1.     API / Frontend Round + Explanation [ 92 candidates shortlisted for this round based on resume]

First round was an API / Frontend Development R ound. You ca n choose to w ork on either the API
development (3 hours) or the frontend  (2 hours). I had chosen API development. A detailed document
describing all use cases, endpoints and sample inputs and outputs will be shared through mail  on the day
of interview. Some problem statements I have come across are: Library management system (admin can
post a boo k, users can borrow a book if it is not already borrow ed, browse different books using title
search), InShorts-like platform (admin can post shorts, users can search and filter shorts, view all shorts in
a sorted order).
Common requirements are of the form: allowing user to signup, login (auth using JWTs), allowing admin
to create a resource using an API key, allowing all users (unauthenticated as well) to browse all resources,
allowing authenticated users to book/borrow a resource or use advanced search and filters.  5-6 endpoints
had to b e developed. We were allowed to use any language and backend framework of our ch oice like
Node/Express, Python/Django or Java /Spring Boot, but the database must be compulsorily MySQL or
PostgreSQL.
After the development is done, there will be an evaluation o f your solution. I was asked to walk through
the database schema (tables and attributes) and then the entire code for the API, explaining in brief what
each file does and implementation of each endpoint. This was followed by demo o f the API, where the
panelists tested quite a few possible edge cases (invalid request body, un authorized acc ess, different
search, and filter queries). I had used ThunderClient extension for VSCode as REST API client.
Few things to remember for API round and some tips:

• Even if an error pops up during the demo or some edge cases do not pass, do not panic. Panelists will

ask you to fix the error there and will ask you to explain your approach/mistake. Even if your API fails

multiple edge cases, if you can fix those during the demo, there is a high chance you might get selected
for the next round.

• They might ask you to explain any line of your code during the walkthrough . So do not copy code

blindly without understanding what it does and have a basic understanding of all the libraries you have
used. I had mistakenly included cookie-parser middleware of Express in my code, and I was a sked
about it because there was no need of cookies in this project. Be honest in your answers.

• Make sure to push your final code on GitHub before the deadline . They might disqualify you if

your final push is after the deadline.

• Practice authentication, authorization using JWTS, CRUD operations, search, and filters beforehand

in the framework of your choice. Implementing the solution in 3 hours can be quite challenging if you
are out of practice or unfamiliar with these concepts. Keep a template ready for your project.

• Use enough dummy data to test all use cases of the API. I used Mockaroo to generate dummy data.

• Keep the API and schema as simple as possible. Make sure all the requirements in the document are

covered (including basic implicit ones such as password encryption and basic input validation), but do
not waste time adding extra features or implementing extremely complex use cases before completing
the requirements given in the document.

2. Technical Round 1 [18 candidates appeared]

This was a primarily DSA round. The round began with my introduction. Most students were only asked
DSA questions, but my pa nelists also asked a few other questions. A Google doc was shared and I was
asked to write pseudo code and any thoughts or answers on the doc. Following questions were asked:

1. Given a natural number n, find a natural number x (< n) such that sum of natural numbers before x is

equal to the s um of numbers after x up to n : I first showed the brute force solution with linear time
complexity, then optimized it to use constant time using the sum of first n natural numbers formula
(sum of first x - 1 numbers = sum of x + 1 to n → sum of first n numbers - x - sum of first x - 1
numbers).

2. House Robber and then House Robber II :  I started with the recursive solution, explained its time and

space complexity, then optimized it using dynamic programming . Then I was asked the variation of
the problem in which first and last houses are connected.

3. Square root of an integer : Gave both brute force and binary search solutions

4. You have a table in a database which contains data about app i nstalls (date of install, location, OS,

etc.). This table contains 10 mi llion records. You need to visualize this data ( number of installs in
different periods) but since it has a huge number of records and no index on date of install column , a
simple query cannot be used. How will you proceed?
I started by writing a simple COUNT(*)....GROUP BY query to get the number of monthly installs,
but was interrupted by interviewer saying that running this query will take a lot of time and resources
because of the huge volume of data. I answered that one way could be to break down the data into
chunks of rows,  run this query o n the chunks in parallel and aggregate t he results. Interviewer then
asked the term for this concept, which I could not answer. He later said that my idea was correct, and
the term he was looking for was database partitioning. I then spoke a bit about Hadoop and HDFS,
since I felt that these concepts were a bit similar

5. There is a backend application which has a POST endpoint which accepts a phone number in its request

body, and sends an O TP to the phone number through SMS. An attacker is hitting the endpoints
repeatedly which is causing a large financial loss t o the company. How can the com pany solve th is
without removing the endpoint?

Frankly I did not know the exact answer to this question. I talked about a similar problem I had solved
in a project of mine u sing cookies  to avoid mischievous use of a feature , but that was a different
scenario. I talked about IP blacklisting and rate limiting, but interviewers did not seem satisfied with
my answers. I do not know what the expected answer was.
Some of my peers were asked easy  and medium questions on sliding window (longest substring without
repeating characters, sliding window maximum), implementation of a hash map , a question on finding
missing number and duplicates using cyclic sort (similar to these questions)

3.    Technical Round 2 [10 candidates appeared]

I was asked to design a database schema for an e-commerce platform. I had to consider schema for users,
products, orders and reviews, relationships between these entities and different attributes involved.
Major focus was on the relationships, and the interviewer was asking about types of relationships between
different entities, various scenarios in which the schema might not work, and how I can modify the schema
to incorporate new requirements given by the interviewer (e.g. different products in a single order, different
variants of a single product, reviews being related to variant or product? etc.). I was also asked to normalize
the schema.
I was then asked a query on the schema I had created (top 10 products sold by volume in Mumbai). Since
the schema was highly normalized, it required a lot of joins.

4. Culture Fit round [7 candidates appeared]

This was a HR round. I was asked about my experience of the entire process, any feedbacks for the process,
my ambitions, my lowest point and how was I able to overcome, latest trends in technology I am interested
in, etc. I answered very honestly in this round as I had not prepared much for it.
3 STUDENTS WERE SELECTED FOR THE SDE ROLE

Following are the four rounds that occured after resume shortlisting:

1) API Round

2) Technical Round 1

3) Technical Round 2

4) Hr Round

1. API Round [ 92 students appeared for this round]

In this round, you will be given 3 hours to create an API for a problem statement. You can use any web
server of your choice, but the database should be MySQL or PostgreSQL. At the end, you need to fill out a
Google Form and submit the GitHub link for the API.
I got the problem statement of creating an API of dining reservation system for Zomato, where I had to
implement the following requirements:

1. Register a User

2. Login User

3. Add a New Dining Place

4. Search Dining Place by Name

5. Get Dining Place Availability

6. Make a booking

After submission, you will explain your API to the panel, where they may ask you to write code for a
different functionality in front of them. They asked me to write code to search for a dining place by address
and to delete the dining place.
Tips for this round:

1. Practice creating 1-2 APIs beforehand

2. Have a template ready where the server is connected to the database, and the login and register

functions are working with JWT Authentication.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Decide the libraries you will be using beforehand to avoid wasting any time during the round.

4. Have clear understanding of how Authentication using JWT works

5. Your first priority should be to complete all the functionalities; once implemented, you can improve

them and adjust the output format as required.

6. Ensure that all backend code is not in the same file.

7. Keep your explanation short and effective, as the panel may be short on time.

8. If possible, prepare a few extra points to distinguish yourself from other candidates. For instance, I

described how my API is secure against various types of attacks and can be scaled.

9. If the Google Form requires you to submit the GitHub link, do not wait until the last moment. Push

whatever code you have written and ensure your last commit is before the deadline.

2. Technical Round 1[18 students appeared for this round]

In this round, the panel asked me to share my screen and open a Google Docs document, where they had
pasted a DSA question. They explained the question to me and asked how I would approach it. I initially
shared a brute force approach and discussed its time complexity. They then requested optimization, which I
explained within 30 seconds due to my familiarity with the question. Subsequently, I was asked to code the
solution in the document.
The interviewer then remarked, 'Now that you're warmed up, let's increase the difficulty,' and presented me
with a LeetCode medium-level question. I explained the brute force approach, then within the next 30
seconds, I formulated a DP approach and discussed its time complexity. Thinking the solution couldn't be
further optimized, the interviewer provided hints that led me to realize the question could be solved using
binary search. I proceeded to write the code accordingly.
The exact questions that i was asked are:

1) Find the Engineer who has kth lowest score this year

Productivity : [5, 6, 7,7, 8, 8, 9]
Engineers: 7
Quarter wise performance
Q1: [1, 5,6 ,8, 8, 8,9]
Q2: [4,6,7,3,8,9,1],
Q3: [6,8,1,6,5,4,4]
SCORE: productivity * performance

2) partition tasks into X parts such that the maximum sum out of all partitions is minimum

Sprint - eg: 14 days - n days
X engineers team
t tasks
I just know about t tasks and i know for every task how much time will it take as x y z tasks
Tasks -> [2, 1, 5, 6, 2, 3] 6 tasks
X = 2 engineers
--- PAGE 3 ---
N - sprint days
Sprint = 11 days
Constraint

• You can't divide/break tasks

You have assign tasks sync to same engineer

• Order of tasks can't be changed

Tips for this round:

1. If you don't understand the question, ask the interviewer to explain it again.

2. Before diving into the solution, clarify the question's constraints with the interviewer

3. Test your approach with an example to validate its correctness

4. Always begin with the brute force approach, stating its time complexity, and iteratively optimize the

solution

5. Vocalize your thought process so the interviewer can guide you effectively and save time

6. If you feel stuck, don't hesitate to ask for hints; they can be very beneficial

7. Reviewing standard questions thoroughly is usually sufficient to succeed in this round

3. Technical Round 2 [ About 10 students appeared for this round]

This was my first round where I had to answer the common question 'Introduce yourself.' I had prepared a
response to keep the interviewer interested. I mentioned that I'm in the top 5% of global coders and shared
how I reduced task completion time by 75% during an internship, saving over 200 hours each year. After
that, I explained the task in detail and we discussed how the project's architecture works with the database.
Next, I was given the task to design a database for an Instagram-like platform. I asked questions to fully
understand the requirements and avoid making assumptions. I discussed my thought process out loud,
explaining why I chose certain solutions and considering potential problems that might come up as the
database gets used more.
During the database design, I suggested several solutions and asked for feedback on whether they were
practical for an SQL database. Whenever I got stuck, I asked for hints to help me move forward. After
finishing the database design, I was tested on writing SQL queries using aggregate functions and joins. I
managed to answer all the questions and even suggested improvements for the last query.
The interview ended with me asking a question and having a short chat with the interviewer.
Tips for this round:

1. Emphasize the reasons behind your solution choices. They want insight into your thought process.

2. Learn from my mistake: Prepare by considering how you would design databases for common apps

like Instagram, Twitter, WhatsApp, YouTube, and blogging platforms beforehand.

3. Practice sql questions before the interview

4. HR Round [ About 7 students appeared for this round]

The interview started at 11 PM and lasted about 30 minutes with the co-founder. He asked me to introduce
myself within 30 seconds, so I focused on highlighting important achievements and kept my introduction
--- PAGE 4 ---
concise, about 3-4 sentences. It's advisable to prepare multiple versions of your introduction for such
situations.
We then briefly discussed my internship experience, particularly focusing on the quantifiable results I
achieved. Since I mentioned leading a team, I was asked about delivering negative news to team members
and how I would handle various leadership situations.
This round primarily aimed to understand my thought process and assess whether I would be a good fit for
the company culture. I was asked personal questions such as the lowest point in my life in the last 3-4 years,
why it happened, what might have occurred if things had gone differently, and what I learned from the
experience. They also inquired about any regrets I might have.
Additionally, we discussed what global issue I would choose to solve if given the opportunity, and why. I
was also asked what I had learned if I didn't secure the internship today.
The interview concluded with me asking several questions about the company's core values
Tips for this round:

1. Take your time to consider your answers. Speaking impulsively can lead to difficulties when

discussions delve deeper into the topic

2. Frame your life experiences as a narrative. Be prepared to explain why things happened as they did

and what lessons you've drawn from them

3. Approach this round as a conversation rather than a formal interview. Use it as an opportunity to

discuss your life and experiences
