1. Digital Interview - HireVue

This was the first round of the placement process, it was a 15-minute interview on Hire Vue, with 6 basic HR
questions about my background. Those not familiar with HIreVue, it's basically a virtual interview, the
question will be displayed on screen and you will be given 40 seconds to prepare and then 3 mins to record
your answer. The 6 questions were same for everyone:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Don't use chat gpt, make your own answers and speak, do not read off any material, look at the camera and
speak. The max limit is 3 minutes per question doesn't mean you have to answer for that long you can stop
the recording whenever you feel like.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Technical Test - Online (120 Candidates)

Platform: Microsoft forms (No proctoring)
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, OS, SQL, Aptitude, Java and Python
The test was mcq based so not that hard, do java/python guess-output questions beforehand as they are
asked, don't get stuck on a question, time management is key.

3. Group Discussion - Online (80 Candidates)

The group discussion was held online on Microsoft Teams, we had 2 choices either give the GD from home
and reach college in-case of selection or go to college early and sit there and give the GD (depends how far
you stay from the college), choose accordingly, The Actual GD for me was a bit scuffed, time is less overall
only 30 mins, of which 2 mins are given after topic reveal to prepare a bit. Remember basic guidelines for
GD - pay attention when others talk, its not a debate so dont fight, introduction should be done only if 100%
confident in the topic. Conclusion should be as inclusive as possible in short amount of time.
Some topics:

1. Challenges/Opportunities for India in the Indian Subcontinent (Political)

1.     Digital Interview - HireVue

This was the first round of the placement process, it was a 15-minute interview on HireVue, with 6 basic HR
questions about my background. Those not familiar with HireVue, it's basically a virtual interview, the
question will be displayed on screen and you will be given 30 seconds to prepare and then 3 mins to record
your answer. The 6 questions were same for everyone:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Don't rely on scripted responses or read from any material. Just speak naturally, looking directly at the camera.
Although the maximum time limit is 3 minutes per question, you don't need to use the full time --stop the
recording whenever you feel you've answered thoroughly.

2. Technical Test - Online (120 Candidates)

Platform: Microsoft forms (No proctoring)
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, OS, SQL, Aptitude, Java and Python

The test was MCQ based so not that hard, do java/python/os/ccn guess-output questions beforehand as
they are asked, don't get stuck on a question, time management is key.

3. Group Discussion - Online (80 Candidates)

The group discussion was held online on Microsoft Teams, we had 2 choices either give the GD from
home and reach college in-case of selection or go to college early and sit there and give the GD (depends
how far you stay from the college), choose accordingly . The Actual GD didn't, time is less overall only
30 mins, of which 2 mins are given after topic reveal to prepare a bit.

Remember basic guidelines for GD -

1. Listen Carefully: Pay attention when others speak to understand their points.

2. Avoid Arguments: Remember, it's a discussion, not a debate--don't fight or interrupt.

3. Introduction: Only introduce the topic if you're 100% confident in your understanding.

4. Conclusion: Aim to make the conclusion as inclusive as possible within the limited time.

Some topics:

1. Challenges/Opportunities for India in the Indian Subcontinent (Political)

2. Digital Twins (Technical)

3. Gen AI / Chatgpt (Technical)

4. Future of EVs (Hardware, Economical)

5. Complete Cashless Society

Tips: While in 2-min prep time, try to make your own points, don't search here and there, write down what

you can think of, they will come to know if you have searched online. A night before sit down and go through
current affairs in all the most common domains.  If you don't understand the topic well, listen properly
what others are speaking based on that, try to find out some valuable points.

4. Technical Interview (30 Candidates)

The Technical Interview was conducted by a panel of two senior developers, and they focused heavily on
my resume projects. It was essential to be completely confident about each project, including the
technology used, the reasons for choosing it, and the implementation details.
When I entered the interview room, we exchanged greetings, and one of the interviewers complimented
the quality of my resume, noting that it was a color copy. After introducing myself, the interviewers began
their in-depth questions about my projects.
One of my projects was a client facing project so that went on in detail about each and everything. They
asked why I built the project and what made it unique compar ed to similar ones. They were interested in

the challenges I encountered during implementation and how I overcame them. Additionally, they wanted
to know whether it was a team or personal project and what my specific contributions were.
Next, they moved on to a project where I used Oauth 2.0. They inquired about some advance terms such
as SAML etc. which I was not aware about so I honestly told them about having no knowledge about them.
Being honest is better than saying anything irrelevant.
Later they moved to docker and went on in depth about docker its working and commands. Later they
moved to Ubuntu as it was mentioned in m y resume. They a sked about chmod and other commands in
depth
After discussing my projects, the interviewers shifted to topics related to computer networks and operating
systems. They began by asking about the OSI model. They wanted to know what it is, its layers, and the
function of each layer. They also inquired about the differences between the OSI model and the TCP/IP
model.
They then asked about TCP and UDP --what they are, their uses, and their differences. They wanted to
know which one is better and asked for real-world examples of where each might be used.
They then asked me a basic Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) question:

1. reverse a string - first I explained brute force approach using stack and then moved to optimal one by

swapping characters

2. how to find the middle node of a linked list. I explained the solution using the slow and fast pointer

technique.
They also asked me the internal representation and working of hash map and how it is different from stack.
Later they moved on to java, multithreading, thread synchronization, pass by value and pass by reference
concept.

At last, they asked me what Baker Hughes do and If I had any questions for them. I asked them about the
most fascinating project they have worked on till date at Baker Hughes.
I tried to answer nearly all of their questions, and they seemed satisfied with my responses.

5. Leadership Interview - Techno HR (15 Candidates)

The final round was a mix of technical and HR questions. The interviewer  started by asking me to introduce
myself. Then, she asked about my weaknesses and how I plan to overcome them.

She also asked some managerial questions, like what I would do if I were in a team with three people and two
of them weren't working properly.  Another question was about what I would do if a project deadline was
approaching and the project wasn't completed yet.

Next, she asked about the app I spend the most time on my phone. She wanted to know why I like that app,
what the best thing about it is, and what I would change if I could.
She also gave me a situation where they are going to reduce time size of 5 to  team size of 2  because of AI
takeover and why should she keep me in top 2 employees and what is it that I can do and AI cannot. She also
asked me my favorite food delivery app from swiggy and zomato and the tech issues of both.
Then, the conversation shifted to why I want to join Baker Hughes. She also asked if I had gone through
previous interview rounds, and when I said yes, she followed up by asking why the other company didn't hire
me.
Finally, she asked if I had any questions for her.
(TIP: Stay calm and answer confidently during the interview. Remember, your body language, facial
expressions, and speaking skills will all be closely observed.)

After a long wait, the results finally came in, 7 students were selected, and I was one of them 😊

Process Date: 30 August 2024

1. OA Round - DSA Computer fundamentals and Aptitude (Criteria min 7 CGPA)

There were 3 sections - Problem Solving 1  problem, Technical MCQ -20 Q and General Aptitude and
Communication MCQ-15 Q
I got a substrings dynamic programming problem which was very much easy as it was similar to the ones I
had practiced.
Technical MCQs were on code snippets, OOPS, CCN, OS and DBMS.
General Aptitude was of the Indiabix level.
So total 36 questions in 2 hrs.

2. Preplacement Talk

3. Technical Interview (40 students appeared for this round.)

The interviewer began by asking how many interviews I had previously attended, ensuring I was comfortable
with the interview process. The first question was an introduction. Then, he inquired about my proficiency in
Java. When asked if I had experience with backend development in Java, I honestly mentioned that I didn't
have direct experience but explained the general flow of how backend development is typically done in Java,
which I had prepared for a prior Java-based role. He then asked about Spring Boot, and I admitted that I wasn't
familiar with it. However, I assured him that if it was required for the role, I would make it a priority to learn.
The conversation moved on to OOP concepts, where he tested my understanding of the basics.
Next, he asked me to write a basic "Hello World" program in Java, expecting me to explain each part of the
code as I wrote it. After that, we discussed exception handling in Java, focusing on the try, catch, and finally
blocks, and the Throwable interface. He posed a tricky question about the execution order when multiple catch
blocks are present, essentially testing my understanding of the exception hierarchy. The interview then shifted
to SQL, where I was asked to write a basic query, which was straightforward. He also asked me to explain
different types of joins, which I did using Venn diagrams, similar to those found on GeeksforGeeks.

We then moved on to system design and various design patterns. Although I couldn't recall all the patterns, I
mentioned the ones I knew. I chose to explain the Singleton pattern in detail. When I struggled to articulate it,
I asked if I could demonstrate with code, which I did, and he seemed satisfied with my explanation.
Finally, he asked some CSS-related questions, including what typically goes into a CSS file (classes containing
key-value pairs) and about Tailwind CSS.  He also asked me about basics of Machine Learning . There were
no DSA questions in this round.
This round lasted for around 35 -40 minutes . Throughout this interview, it's crucial to provide thorough
explanations for your answers, using examples , codes, diagrams, and detailed concept explanations. This
approach helps avoid tricky follow -up questions that could potentially lower your confidence.  If you don't
know a concept, politely admit it, and emphasize your willingness to learn.

3. HR Interview (25 approx students were appeared for this round.)

This interview also began with introduce myself. Following that, the interviewer inquired about my internship,
focusing on the platform's users, my role, the current status of the website, the tech stack we chose, and the
challenges I faced during development.
He then asked me to explain a recent project, so I chose to discuss a blockchain project I had worked on. He
mentioned recent news about data breaches in blockchains and asked why these occur. I didn't have any idea
of data breaching in blockchain, I didn't have an immediate answer, I asked which specific blockchain he was
referring to and guessed it might be Hyperledger. I then explained how Hyperledger works and guessed and
identified potential vulnerabilities that might not be fully explored during smart contract development. I also
described a vulnerability that had occurred in a smart contract I developed earlier. He then asked how these
vulnerabilities could be identified  beforehand. I responded by sharing a past scenario where I had handled
similar work.
The conversation then shifted to the software development lifecycle (SDLC). He asked about various models,
specifically the Agile model, and inquired about the scaling factors used to measure development progress.
Since I had mentioned software testing on my resume, he delved into that as well, asking about different
testing levels, including black box and white box testing, as well as static and dynamic testing. I was well -
prepared for these questions and provided detailed answers . He then asked my about Data migration about
which I didn't know anything but I did have basic understanding what it was and explained in layman terms.
He then asked about the process which goes behind that,  And I politely replied that I didn't have knowledge
about it. He then asked about jdk, jre why is Java a plateform independent language.
Finally, he asked about the most challenging project I had worked on and why it was difficult, which I had
also prepared for. Since I mentioned my leadership role on my resume, he asked in -depth questions about it,
including the marketing deals I managed a nd how I balanced those responsibilities with my studies.  Finally
he asked if had any question.  I asked him about how a role shift process occurs at Oracle and about Oracle
institute.

This too lasted for around 40 minutes. Overall, this round focused heavily on the experiences and skills I had
mentioned in my resume. Confidence in your answers, maintaining a positive attitude, and good posture are
key to succeeding in this round. This is a round where in you should be ready to answer the questions which
you haven't prepared. If you don't know a term completely then polite tell or if you know it a bit try to guess
or explain it with your similar past experience examples.

You have two lines of students, Line A and Line B, each with N students. The students
face each other, and you need to make the height of every student in Line A equal to the
height of the student directly opposite in Line B. You can swap any student from Line A
with any student from Line B, and each swap costs the minimum height of the two
students being swapped. Determine the minimal cost to achieve this alignment.

Mostly were based on Verbal and Quants -

• https://www.indiabix.com/database/questions-and-answers/

• https://prepinsta.com/learn-aptitude/

2. Technical Round 1 [ Around 45 students were shortlisted for this round]

The interview started around 9:30 in the morning. It started with the introduction: Tell me about
yourself (Be confident, maintain positive body language, and keep a good eye contact). Then the
interviewer went through my resume and asked me to give a detailed overview of an event I
attended at NIT Trichy. He asked me about the various activities conducted there, what all
things I learned, and my overall experience.
Next, he asked me to explain the projects listed on my resume. There were few
counter-questions regarding how I implemented specific functionalities, and he asked why I
chose Flutter, in one of my project. After a brief discussion, he asked me which programming
language I was comfortable with, to which I responded, Java (Oracle focuses on Java).
He then asked me some technical questions related to polymorphism, early binding, late
binding, encapsulation and the main pillars of OOPs (Try to answer every question with an
example). What is Multithreading? He also asked if I was familiar with file operations in Java
and whether I had used them in any of my projects.
Next, I was asked to write a program on paper to find duplicate values in an array of string
values, such as I'"aa", "bc", "cd"
', "aa", " de" ], without using HashMap. I was also
asked to find the minimum and maximum values in a linked list, and to check if the given string
is palindrome or not (I gave a recursive solution), reverse a string without using any built-in
method. I was able to write all the programs.
Then, a few situation-based questions like - Suppose you're working on a project with a
colleague from the mechanical department who lacks technical expertise. How would you
effectively collaborate with him to ensure the project's success, while addressing any technical
challenges that arise?
Suppose you are managing both your tech team and a client, explain the key steps involved
from project initiation to delivery. How will you handle both of them? As I answered, to which he
said you are missing out on something, after a hint i said feasibility study which was correct.
--- PAGE 3 ---
For scenario-based questions, they want to understand your thought process. Analyze the
situation properly and make sure your answer reflects key skills like teamwork, time
management, and leadership that aligns with the role. Overall, the first technical round went
very well, and I was able to answer all the questions confidently.

3. Technical Round 2 + HR [ Around students students were shortlisted for this round]

The second round started around 2:30 pm after the lunch break. It started with the panelist
introducing himself, he was a Senior Lead with expertise in software development and product
implementation at Oracle. He then reviewed my resume and asked me to introduce myself.
Following this, he asked me to explain one of the project listed on my resume. (Only include
those projects you're 100% confident about, as they may ask in-depth questions).
Then he asked me about MVC architecture and whether I used it in my project to which I
replied Yes! and I explained it, then the following question was how does mvc works in your
project. I explained the complete flow of the project. Then next was where do we write Business
logic? So I explained that the Model handles the application's data and business logic, while the
controller manages how user input from the View interacts with the Model. He then asked me to
explain client-server architecture, what is REST API?, and why is an API considered
RESTful? I was able to answer these questions confidently.
Next question was If I was familiar with microservices, to which I said I'm not much aware of
the concept, he responded, "Okay, no problem." He then asked me about multithreading and
told me to write a query to find the highest salary for each department. I did that part.
Then I was asked to write on paper how to hash a string by replacing each character with a
letter which is 5 letters ahead alphabetically.
Since I had mentioned various sports achievements, he asked situation-based questions about
my strategy and planning, particularly focusing on how I would manage my team. One of the
situation based question was: Suppose you are leading a team on a critical project with a
short deadline, but one team member is underperforming. How would you help them
improve, keep the project on track, and keep the team motivated?
He also asked me about the certifications listed on my resume. At times even if you don't know
the exact answer it's okay, try to explain your approach. They want to see your ability to tackle
problems, how confident you are,and how eager you are to learn. They don't expect you to
know every answer so be calm and answer wisely.
Finally, he asked if I had any questions. I asked a few questions, including: What is the work
culture of Oracle?, What specific skills and attributes are essential for success in this role at
Oracle?. Overall, it was a really long interview, but I had a great experience.

customSections.content:
For Round 1:
Keep practicing Basic quants and aptitude questions every week.
You'll get a lot of resources on the internet.
For the Interview:
Refer to GFG for a basic overview of all the generic questions asked to freshers
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/java-interview-questions/

https://www.interviewbit.com/
Javatpoint is another great resource if there's anything you want to relearn in the last week
https://www.javatpoint.com/
For  video  explanations,  there  are  a  lot  of  references  on  youtube  but  I've  personally  used  BRO  CODE  's
videos for the last moment basic doubts.
Overall:
Maintain your confidence throughout, don't let anyone know you're tensed even if you are.
COMMUNICATION IS THE KEY!!!
Sit back and relax!
Keep communicating with the interviewer , talk to him and clear your doubts .
Don't make any assumptions  when you are asked any question.
Also, SMILE! It shows you're not tensed and also lightens up the environment.
That's a huge factor that I don't want you guys to neglect (please!)
Furthermore,  don't try to fit in the interview mode before you go.
BE YOU  because that's what they admire.
You do you!
Wishing you lots and lots of luck for the interview.
If you have any queries, feel free to connect with me on linkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/in/mrunal-jadhav-05a230228/
All the best for your preparations :)

The interview was scheduled for August 30th, 2024, with a reporting time of 9:00 am, and
interviews were set to start around 9:30 am. However, due to some delays, they began at
approximately 10:30 am. The TPC members called the first few students according to their
assigned panels, with a total of 8-9 panels conducting interviews. As time passed, most
students completed their first round, and some even started their second, but my name wasn't
called until around 2:30 pm, by which time about 10-15 students had already finished their
second round. In such situations, it's important to stay calm and not get anxious. If you do feel
nervous, take a walk near the TPO office and drink some water. During long waits, avoid
studying anything new instead, focus on revising key concepts and reviewing your projects.
Around 2:30 pm, I was called in for my interview. It began with the interviewer introducing
themselves, followed by a request for me to introduce myself. It's essential to be thoroughly
prepared with your introduction. After I introduced myself, the interviewer reviewed my
--- PAGE 3 ---
resume and noticed a project I had mentioned, which was based on Java and MySQL. This led
the discussion to focus heavily on that project, with various situational and technical
questions being asked, including a request to write the database connection code. Following the
in-depth discussion about the project, the interviewer moved on to questions about Core Java,
covering all OOP concepts, syntax, debugging, and output-based questions. Additionally,
there were questions related to DSA(easy to medium level), OS, DBMS, and SQL queries
This round lasted for around 45 min - 1hr The questions were as follows:

1. Explain Encapsulation and Abstraction.

2. Define Polymorphism and its types.

3. Differentiate between runtime and compile time polymorphism.

4. Write down the code showing inheritance.

5. Implement custom Exceptions in Java.

6. DSA 1 - Reverse a number followed up by Reverse a string

7. DSA 2 - Check if Binary Tree is a Binary Search Tree

8. DSA 3 - Search in Rotated Sorted Array

9. DSA 4 - Merge Intervals

10. What is a Process? What is Deadlock and how can we avoid it?

11. Sir(Interviewer) gave me 2-3 schemas (tables), basically it was an employee dataset

consisting of columns such as salary, department, employee id and other tables had
columns like department id and department. Then he asked me to write queries on

• Find details of employees having max salary. (Aggregate Functions)

• Find details of employees having 2nd and 3rd max salary. (Aggregate Functions)

• Output all the unique salaries and count them. (Group By and Count Function)

• Find top 3 salaries from the table (Table contained duplicate salaries too).

• Find the top 2 salaries of each department and details of those employees

("dense_rankO" window function to solve the query).

12. What is the difference between primary key and unique constraint?

13. Can there there be multiple primary keys?

14. What is Foreign key? What happens when a primary key which is referred to as foreign

key in another table is deleted?

15. Why do we need indexing and what are types of indexing?

16. What is the CAP theorem?

17. Also be ready with 2-3 questions (For eg: regarding job profile or company to ask at the

end

As soon as my first technical interview ended, I was immediately called in for the Technical +
HR round. This round lasted for around 1-1.5 hrs. When I entered the interview room, the
interviewer offered me a handshake. It's important to ensure your handshake is firm and
confident, as it reflects your level of self-assurance or nervousness. Additionally, maintain
positive body language and wear a pleasant smile. Avoid shaking your legs or leaning on the
table during the interview. If the interviewer hasn't invited you to sit, always ask, "May I have a
seat, sirạbefore sitting down.
The interviewer reviewed my resume again and noticed a project I had mentioned, which was
based on Java and MySQL. This shifted the focus of our discussion heavily towards that
project. He asked me to explain the overall flow and architecture of the project and whether it
was a solo or group effort. Next, he inquired about the database connectivity, including the
libraries or dependencies I had used. He also presented some technical situational questions
related to the project, asking how I would handle specific cases. Finally, he asked how I would
approach making the project scalable, including the adjustments to the tech stack and the
step-by-step process I would follow to meet this requirement.
I also mentioned a MERN stack project where I had used JWT tokens and Socket.io. The
interviewer asked me to explain the reasoning behind using JWT tokens and the role of
Socket.io in the project, as well as the challenges I faced during implementation. He then
asked for my opinion on whether I would prefer using an external library or an external API
in a project. In response to such questions, it's important to focus on the positive aspects of
both options, highlighting how they differ and how they can be used according to the project's
needs. Additionally, consider the security implications of each option and explain which one
would be better in that context. After this the interview concluded with some HR questions and
then he asked me if I had any questions for him. As I had said earlier, be ready with 2-3
questions to ask the interviewer during the overall interview process. The HR questions were as
follows.

1. Tell me about a challenging scenario faced while working on a group project and what all

steps you took to handle the situation

2. If you were the team leader and one of your teammates was working on their task, what

would you do in that situation?

3. Why are you interested in Oracle and the role of Associate Consultant?

Prepare for commonly asked HR questions, including top and frequently asked ones, use
the storytelling method for your responses. This approach involves structuring your
answers as a narrative. Refer to this site for various HR questions: HR Questions.
Additionally, research the company to understand its activities, principles, and values. This will
help you tailor your responses and demonstrate alignment with the company's goals and culture.

1.     Online Assessment Test  (All those who applied for OFSS were allowed to give the test)

The test was conducted on Hackerrank platform and there were 36 questions divided into 3 sections
(1 coding+20 core subjects MCQ+15 Aptitude MCQ) which were to be solved in 2 hours time. You
were allowed to switch between sections.

a. Coding Section:
Only one coding was asked and everybody had received different coding questions.

Question: Determine whether a triangle formed by three points (x1,y1),(x2,y2) and (x3,y3) is non-
degenerate. Also two more points A(ax,ay) and B(bx,by) were given and we had to tell whether
the lie inside or outside the triangle together or individually. We had to return a number based on
the various possible which could happen (A inside triangle and B outside, both inside triangle
inside and A outside triangle or both outside the triangle).

Reference to what I did in the question:
i. Check whether triangle is valid or not if three points are given:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/check-whether-triangle-is-valid-or-not-if-three-points-
are-given/
ii. Check whether a given point lies inside a triangle or not
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/check-whether-a-given-point-lies-inside-a-triangle-
or-not/

b. Aptitude questions:
There were  15 M.C.Qs which were easy and majorly comprised of basic verbal and quants
questions
I used IndiaBix to practice aptitude questions : https://www.indiabix.com/

c. MCQS on Core Subjects: This section had 20 M.C.Qs on core subjects and JAVA.

I gave mcq mock tests for various core subjects in the website below:
https://www.codehelp.in/mock-tests

After this round 40 people were shortlisted.

2. Technical Interview (40 people were shortlisted for this round)

Before this round there was a Pre Placement Talk in which they explained about the company. This ppt
was in online mode.
So the round started with the interviewer asking me to "Introduce yourself" question. Then he asked me
about my hobbies and how was my day until now. He then also asked me how many interviews I have
given till now and how was that experience. I told him that this is my second interview and also about the
experience of the previous interview.
Then he came to my resume. He asked me to explain the first project mentioned in my resume which was
my major project. I explained it to him in detail. He was convinced.
Then he asked me whether I was comfortable in JAVA or not to which I replied that all the oops concept
was taught to me in JAVA and apart from that the Dsa problems were solved by me in python.  Then he
asked me what are all the things I knew in oops. I replied to him by telling the 4 pillars and then he asked
to explain all the pillars. Then he told me to write a code on a paper showcasing inheritance concept. I
was able to do that easily.  Then he told me to modify the same code to showcase the overloading and
overriding concepts.
Then he asked me about JVM. I explained it to him and drew the entire JVM architecture on sheet and
explained each component properly (fyi he did not ask me draw the architecture but since I was aware
about it, I drew and explained it to him properly). He was quite satisfied with my answer.
Then he asked me what if the heap is running out of memory then what you will do? So I told him that I
would use the concept of garbage collection. I elaborated on garbage collection and also wrote a code
explaining garbage collection concept on paper (again fyi he did not asked me to do so but since I knew I
did it anyways). The interviewer was quite impressed with the answer.
He also asked me about threads in JAVA which I explained him by talking about the 2 ways you can
implement threads and also wrote a code for both ways. The interviewer asked me a tricky question on
try catch blocks in the code written which I was able to solve  (What if multiple catch blacks are there in
code, then which catch and how many block/blocks will run).
Then he asked me what are design patterns in JAVA. Luckily one of my friends who had the same panel
as mine went before me and told me about this question asked. So in the meantime I prepped for this
question if asked which the interviewer did eventually. I explained him about one of the design pattern out
of five which is the singleton pattern which is a design patterns type  and wrote the code implementing
singleton class. I told the interviewer that I am not aware of any other pattern.
Then he asked questions on SQL like triggers which I said to him that I am not aware of it .Then he asked
me about views which I explained to him. Then he asked me about left outer join  and all other joins

which I explained to him by drawing a Venn diagram for each of them. He also gave me a basic SQL
query on left join and inner join.
Then he asked me about the git commands  I have used till now. I told him about command like
push,clone,commit and explained them.
Then he asked me about SDLC(Software Development Life Cycle)  where I named a few models like
agile,waterfall and devops but was able to explain only two of them(waterfall and devops) .
He also asked me I have worked on react or not(it was mentioned in my resume),to which I replied that I
have worked on few solo projects on react but since the re were some  better presentable projects that's
why I haven't  showcased them in my resume.
After that the interview concluded and I asked him one question.
The question was regarding what was expected from us in the associate consultant role. What would we
work on?

Advice: If there's any concept which you are 100% confident of, go beyond what's expected by the

interviewer and elaborate much more on it. You can do it by drawing/writing on a sheet to showcase
your deep understanding of the concept to impress the interviewer.

Advice: If there is any concept which you are not aware of, don't get nervous. Always have a smile

on your face.

After a few minutes I was told that I have been selected for the next round and was told to have lunch and be
ready for next round by exactly 2 pm.

3. Techno-HR interview

I was the first one to be called after the break. The interviewer went through my  resume first. Then
asked me to introduce myself. He then asked me whether I had lunch or not to which I replied honestly
that I did not because I was very nervous and didn't feel like eating. He chuckled a bit.
Then he asked me about my hackathon project which was a chrome extension for visually disabled
people. I explained him what it exactly did and what's the purpose of it and how it can benefit people
with vision disabilities.
He then came to the other projects mentioned in my resume and asked me about them one by one.
I explained him my first project without going too deep into it. Then he asked about the second project
which was lab inventory web application project. He asked me to explain about it and gave me a piece
of paper and told me to write a piece of code describing an html file and something related to loading
a csv file in JAVA or c. Here I was unable to understand what he actually expected from me and I
became a bit nervous. However what I did was I diverted his question by asking him whether he wants
to know what I have done in inventory project(about which I knew A-Z). The interviewer paused for a
second and said to me to proceed with writing the code about the project. The project was based on

flask so I wrote one of the GET methods in my project and explained it to him. Then he told me to
write the same code in JAVA or c to which I took some time to think about and eventually said that I
don't know. Then he told me to parse a csv file having 100 records and 10 columns in JAVA or C.
I again told him that I am not sure how to do it in these languages but I can do it in python to which
he agreed and I wrote the entire code. He then asked me to read a file in JAVA or C. I knew how to
read a file in JAVA as I had done it in one of my projects. Then he went inquired a bit more about it
to which I had no answers.
He then asked me the difference between c and JAVA to which I was not able to tell much about.
Then I asked him with a smile whether he could asked me between any language other than C. He too
chuckled with me and asked me difference between JAVA and C++.I gave him minimum 5 points
of difference. He was satisfied with the answer.
Till now I understood that the interviewer was looking for some JAVA or c skilled guy so I went on a
5-minute talk explaining the chain of events leading to why I don't code more frequently in JAVA and
c anymore and prefer to code in python.

Advice: Read the room. Try to understand the demands of the interviewer. If you are somehow

not able to answer a chain of question related to a particular concept/language/subject. Try to
come up with a genuine answer explaining how and why you feel you are not confident in it and
also suggest the alternatives to the particular concept/language/subject  on which you are
confident about.
My aim was to assure him that I can answer his questions but the language expectation is problem
here. He heard me out my problem here and nodded with a smile on his face.
He then asked me "Where do u see yourself in 5 years" followed by "What was the lowest point in
your life".
He then told me that we are done with the interviews and I asked him for how long has he been with
oracle, his experience in oracle and what has he been currently working on. He talked about it briefly
and shook my hand as I was stood up and was about to leave the room.
In the end 19 students were selected and I was one of them.

1) An OA was scheduled at 10:30 pm in the night.

2) Next day the shortlisted candidates were announced.

4) PPT followed by 2 rounds of interviews.

Please ensure that you have two copies of your resume, each with your photograph securely attached using
either a paper clip or a stapler. It's imperative not to overlook this detail, as they have explicitly stated that
applications without a photograph will not be considered.

1. [Online Assessment (OA)] [ No of candidates who appeared for this round => 200-300]

The round consisted of a total of 22 questions: 20 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) focusing on aptitude,
and 2 coding problems. The time duration for this round was 90 minutes. Among those shortlisted for
interviews, only 2 to 4 candidates managed to solve both coding problems. The coding section featured one
problem of medium difficulty and another that was quite challenging.
The aptitude test was of moderate complexity, though it did include 3-4 particularly difficult questions. Most
of the questions were intuitive and required a strong grasp of common sense. Additionally, there were a few
verbal reasoning questions included in the test. You can practice aptitude questions for here - Aptitude
Questions with Solutions
2.
¡Technical Round (Projects, OOP, Brain Teasers] | No of candidates who appeared for this round =>
21]
In this round, I was asked about core Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts such as Inheritance,
Polymorphism, Abstraction, and Encapsulation. I was asked to implement these concepts in Java using pen
and paper and to elucidate their practical applications. Following this, I was asked to delineate the
differences between Hash Set and Hashmap, including their implementation in Java, typical use cases, and
the time complexities associated with various operations performed on them. I was also provided with a
scenario and had to discern which data structure would be most efficacious.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Subsequently, the interviewer presented a diagram and asked me to identify the number of squares within it.
This was followed by a similar task involving the identification of triangles. Later, I was instructed to
rearrange some triangles to form the maximum possible number of squares.
The interview then shifted focus to my resume, where I was questioned about my projects. The questions
revolved around the problems I aimed to solve with these projects, the benefits to others, the most arduous
challenges encountered during development, and the solutions I devised. I was also asked about potential
optimizations, the rationale behind choosing particular technologies, and alternative technologies that could
have been employed. Finally, the interviewer inquired about REST APIs and their alternatives, and asked me
to compose two SQL queries.

fundamentals of Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA). Initially, I was asked to elucidate the structure and
representation of both singly and doubly linked lists. Following this, I was tasked with rotating a linked list
by k positions-- Link to the code. Next, I was questioned on the representation of trees using linked lists
and the distinctions between trees and graphs. The interviewer also probed into the practical applications of
trees and graphs, asking me to choose the appropriate data structure for a given scenario.
Further, I was asked which traversals are necessary to construct a unique binary tree-Link to the code. I
was also asked to print the top view of a binary tree - Link to the code. For all these questions, I was

1. Preparation Resources:

• Aptitude Questions: IndiaBix

• Guesstimates/ RCA:

→ The Consulting & Strategy Club, IIM Lucknow - YouTube: Initial understanding
→ Case Interviews Cracked - YouTube: Initial understanding

• [Case_Interviews_Cracked_Case_Interviews.pdf](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1LbGkz-cPT_lqWW3s9Op7C23bDBWwGKmS/view?usp=drive_link): To practice Case Studies (this level is

higher than that asked in interviews).

• Puzzles: Top 100 GFG

• SQL:

→ SOLBolt: Use initially to get a hang of the basics
→ GFG SOL Articles: For theory/ better understanding
→ Leetcode SOL 50: For practice (sufficient for InCred rounds)

2. Resume Shortlisting:

• Make sure to tailor your resume according to the role. If you don't have a particular role in mind or

want to try out for multiple roles, I suggest keeping 2 projects per role handy and then changing the
projects in your resume according to the role.

• Use a single-column ATS-friendly resume. (Overleaf or Resume Worded)

• Always check your Resume score using a resume checker. (Resume Worded)

• If you're using Resume Worded, a score of 65+ is great!

3. Interviews (general tips):

o In interviews, questions often arise from the conversation flow and your responses. Use this to your
advantage by steering the discussion towards your strengths and preferred topics.

• Prepare some standard HR questions before the interview.

• Research the company thoroughly and keep a few questions ready to ask after the interviews.

• If you mess up during the interview, it's completely fine and normal. Don't get nervous because of it

and try to laugh it off and correct yourself as soon as possible! Smile and try to seem relaxed.

• Always be humble. HR representatives are really good at detecting overconfidence or

underconfidence, so try to be neutral.

• Lastly, just be yourself and let your personality shine!

For any further questions, feel free to reach out to me on Linkedin
Keep at it and believe in yourself! All the best!

- Pre-Placement Talk (Online) - 24th July

- Resume Shortlisting - 25th July

- Written Assessment and Interviews - 26th July

The process consisted of a resume shortlisting, a written pen-and-paper test and 2 interview rounds. There
was no distinct HR interview. One HR representative from the company was present in each round to ask
relevant HR questions.

1. Round 1: Written Test (Offline) (124 students)

Highlights: Aptitude, SOL, Python
We had 25 minutes to solve the test. It was given on a printed paper where we had to tick correct options for
MCQs and write answers for other questions. The test included 12 Aptitude questions, 3 SQL questions, and
1 Python programming question. I solved the Aptitude section first as it was easier, then the Python
question, and finally the SQL queries.

• Aptitude (MCQ format)

This section had easy questions on topics like Profit and Loss, Time and Work, and Simple Interest.
It's important to solve these quickly since the SQL section usually needs more time. About 10-12
minutes should be enough for this part.

• SQL Questions (Write query on test paper)

We got 3 easy-to-medium SQL questions. They involved writing SELECT queries, JOINing tables,
and creating output tables for different types of JOINs. This section needs careful thinking, so I
suggest using about 10 minutes for it.

• Python Question (Write solution on test paper)

This was an easy question about summing N natural numbers. I spent about 2-3 mins on this section.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The test aims to test both speed and accuracy. To move to the interview rounds, you need to get almost
all questions right. Do not underestimate the test after looking at the difficulty of the questions! While
the questions are easy, you will need to use the allotted 25 mins wisely to clear this round.
38 students progressed after this round

2. Round 2: Interview Round 1(38 students)

Highlights: Resume-based questions, SQL, Guesstimates (Duration: 45 - 60 mins)
For this round, there were 3 interview panels, each consisting of 2-3 panellists. My panel had three
members: one HR representative and two technical experts.
Upon entering, I was first told that I had answered 15 out of 16 questions correctly in the written test and
asked to guess which one I might have gotten wrong. Next, I was asked to introduce myself. Following that,
they inquired why I chose InCred and a BA role. I shared a few personal experiences, along with my interest
in participating in case studies to support my response. Afterwards, I was asked to name one Data Analytics
project I had completed, describe it, and state the top 5 analytical conclusions I drew from the project. I
could only recall and name 3. They asked a few follow-up questions before moving on to guesstimates.
While discussing one of my case studies, we started talking about OTT platforms and their relation to my
case study topic. One of the panelists then asked me to estimate the number of Netflix subscribers in India. I
asked some preliminary questions and made a decision tree to estimate. My number was too high. In such
situations, it's crucial not to get nervous and to try to build upon your previous logic. I hadn't considered
rural/urban and age factors, so I explained this and recalculated. The interviewer wasn't fully satisfied but
decided to move on to technical questions. For the technical part, I was asked a few resume-based techstack
justifications, different types of keys in SQL and execution sequences for statements in SQL.
Finally, I was asked if I had any questions for them. I asked two questions related to the company and the
role, after which we concluded the interview.
15 students progressed after this round

4. Round 3: Interview Round 2 (15 students)

Highlights: Case Study Question (Duration: 45 - 60 mins)
My panel had two panellists. My case study question was to add a loan function to the PhonePe app. When
facing case study questions, always ask relevant preliminary questions to fully understand the problem and
requirements. I took about 10 minutes to understand the PS and asked around 8-10 questions.
After taking the interviewers' input I concluded that I had to look at 2 major points: Data analysis of the
target audience (to analyze what features we should have) and Basic UI or input parameters. I classified
people according to different parameters to understand who would be eligible to take a loan.
--- PAGE 3 ---
For most of the interview, I focused on providing a detailed analysis of the target audience. This part lasted
for about 30 minutes. It's important to keep this round as conversation-like as possible. Talk to the
interviewers, take their feedback regularly and keep them engaged. Once the interviewer was satisfied with
my analysis, he told me to move on to the UI/ Input parameters part and I drew a basic Wireframe for the UI
and listed 6 major parameters that should be taken as input from the user before considering giving a loan.
The interviewer was satisfied with my responses. Finally, I was asked if I had any questions for them. I
asked two questions related to the company and the role, after which we concluded the interview.

The placement process had 4 rounds consisting of resume shortlisting, test-based shortlisting, interview-1
and interview-2. There was no separate HR interview, but HRs from the company were present in both the
interviews and asked some HR-type questions. There was an online pre-placement talk by the company
prior to the entire process where they detailed what the company does, its growth, industry position and
values, as well as what the job role would demand and offer. It is important to pay attention here, as you can
then modify your resume/ interview answers to be better aligned with the job role and company. It is also
useful in answering HR questions.

1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (Candidates: roughly 200)

The resume shortlisting is generally done based on the company's requirements and job roles. The most
important thing here is to prepare a job-role and company specific resume. Highlighting more
development projects/skills in a data science role or vice versa will not be much helpful. It is unclear
whether CGPA was a criteria. It is always good to keep a CGPA above 8.5. I had worked on machine
learning and data science projects, which was very relevant to this role. For each project explain what the
project did, the methods it used, the technologies used, and results obtained. Do NOT lie about something
you didn't do, as you are grilled on the projects in further rounds. It is also good to have 1 extracurricular
activity showing yourself as team player/leader. I used 2 ML projects, 3 data science projects and my
experience as an HOD Creatives at Oculus in my resume. Lists of relevant skills are given at the end.
124 candidates from 200 were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Written Test (Aptitude, SOL) (Candidates:

124) Interestingly this test was conducted by pen and paper. It had 10 questions to be solved in 25 mins. There

were 6 aptitude type MCQ questions, 3 SQL questions and 1 very simple coding question. The questions
were very much doable. Because of the time constraint you had to do them fast. Almost all students could
solve most of the questions, and hence only 2-3 questions became the deciding ones. Only students who got
9/10, 10/10 were probably shortlisted. The questions covered mathematical and logical aptitude, SQL
aggregate functions, sorting and joins. The coding question was to simply sum numbers from 1 - N.
However as the papers were checked manually by the recruiting team, using the formula (N(N+1))/2 could
be an edge over recursion/loop. Only Python/ pseudocode was allowed. Keeping a calm and focused head
will easily let you pass such a test.
--- PAGE 2 ---
38 candidates from 124 were shortlisted for the next round.

3. Interview Round 1 (Candidates:

38) This round started with the recruiters asking me to introduce myself. Keep an introduction prepared

beforehand (company and role-specific of course) highlighting the relevant coursework, skills and passion
for the field. The panel consisted of 3 recruiters, one of them was an HR.
They took my resume and one by one started covering my projects. They picked up keywords/concepts
from my project descriptions and asked me to explain it/ asked me related questions. Some questions that
they asked are: difference in HAVING and GROUP BY. These are not actually differing but are keywords
that are used together. I explained how they worked and also gave an example. (HAVING lets you put
checks on aggregate results obtained by GROUP BY) They asked me to explain how window functions
worked, and list some of them. I again gave an overview of the concept and followed it with an example.
(Window functions calculate values in a running fashion over rows, assigning the values to each row while
keeping each row intact. Most aggregate functions can be used as window functions. Others are: RANK,
DENSE_RANK, NTILE, ROW_NUMBER, etc.) Mentioning OVER, PARTITION BY, and window
function aliases could be a plus. Mention only those words/ terms you can explain, as you could be
cross-questioned. This was followed by a simple Python question to explain difference in sets and lists,
and explain some of their characteristics. (Sets are like a bag, sets can't have duplicates, sets are
unordered, lists follow the order they are subjected to, etc) Next they asked what is a confusion matrix. I
explained its structure and usage as a metric for classification models. Then they asked about false positives
and what does it mean when there is a high number of false positives. (False positives are results
classified as positive class by a model when they were actually of the negative class. More false positives
indicate uneven distribution of classes in the training dataset, it could have more positive class entries
leading to biased training of the model. I should have also detailed that another reason could be using an
erroneous threshold while classifying.)
Next they asked a case study type question: What factors will I consider to decide a suitable location
for a Zudio store. Here your knowledge of current trends comes handy as it is important to know Zudio is
focused on making fashion affordable and cheap. I first highlighted that Zudio targets middle class and
lower middle class populations so those areas must be recognised. For this I first thought of collecting
incomes of residents in an area but then realized that it was personal to collect such data and the collection
will also prove to be difficult. Then I suggested collecting the housing prices and rent prices in the area to
gauge what kind of area it was. I also suggested analyzing local shops and the prices they provide, especially
clothing shops, and whether any branded/ top end entities existed. After recognising a suitable middle/lower
middle class area, I further noted that Zudio is much more popular in the youth. Hence I must find a
road/junction where there is a constant stream of young people such as near a college, mall, movie screens
etc. This will make the shop more visible to its target market. (Note: I had never prepared for such
non-tech questions before, I was focused only on SDE or data science kind of roles. I just went ahead with
what I thought was logical at the moment and kept explaining my thought process clearly.)
The recruiters seemed satistied with my answer. Lastly, the HR asked me to explain one of my hobbies. I
am very passionate about graphic designing, so I explained what I do, the tools I use, and where I have used
them. (Maybe I went a little overboard:)). The interview ended in a happy/friendly mood due to this.
15 students from 38 were shortlisted for the final round.

4. Interview Round 2 (Candidates:

15) --- PAGE 3 ---

This interview was much more serious-toned than the previous one. They only asked one case study
question: How will you diagnose delays in loan repayment in tier-2 cities and what methods could you
undertake to avoid them. I literally used the first 5-7 mins to understand what they were actually asking
me to do. The interviewers were helpful and explained how loan repayment works and that reminders are
sent via telecom centers in Mumbai to loan bearers in tier-2 cities regarding their installments. I fumbled a
bit in the start and then slowly narrowed down to various points which I noted on the pen and paper
provided. Firstly I stated that some borrowers are incurable, that is they are taking ibad loans' which cannot
be supported by their income. We should avoid such customers by analyzing their income before giving a
loan. Next I surmised that people delaying repayment are already lacking ethics, hence they can only be
made to repay by threatening them with their own loss. They should be made aware of the consequent effect
on their CIBIL score, increasing interest rates, and possible legal action. (Effect on collaterals is another
possible threat). The interviewers were satisfied, and further asked how this awareness could be created if
the current telecom system mentioned is not being effective.
One interviewer suggested thinking around a system where loan repayment reminder teams can be sent
to the borrower's homes. I suggested two approaches: I had heard about third party companies which
provide the services of collecting loan repayments using their own mechanisms. So such a company's
services can be hired. Secondly a team based system design could be made where each team is assigned
certain households to visit in a day. Upon visiting, they meet the borrower, familiarize him with his situation,
remind him about the repayment and list out the threats. They also do a OTP/QR based two-way verification
with the borrower. This will be a consent on the borrower's side that he has recognised what could be the
consequences of his delay in repayment and a confirmation from the team's side proving that the household
was visited. This verification's location could be tracked in the centers located in Mumbai. Failing to do the
verification on the customer side would result in one of the threats being implemented, and failure from the
teams' side would count against the teams' performance. This will prevent any malpractice/bribing. The
interviewers were satisfied with this.
Some of my friends were asked guesstimates. Guesstimates are absolutely essential for data science/
non-tech roles and they can't be overlooked. Most of the case studies/guesstimates asked were in a way
related to services that InCred provides. Hence skimming through the company's website and gaining
more information about their services/products is helpful.
5 candidates from the final 15 were selected for the job role.

straightforward. Using the formula instead of a loop might give an edge.

emphasizing speed and accuracy.

a solid grasp of the basics is crucial, as the questions are typically not too challenging.

recommendation part using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) with cosine similarity. They asked about the
algorithm, how it works, the dataset used, and the preprocessing steps involved.

clarified doubts with the interviewers, such as the type of bottles considered. It's important to articulate your

to organize your thoughts.

preparation, leaving a positive impression.

then asked about my native place. Since my projects had already been discussed, they moved on to case

increase the company's profitability. I suggested identifying areas where Amazon might be losing
profit, such as issues with damaged goods, and addressing these sources to reduce returns and
enhance profitability. Additionally, I proposed reducing delays in shipping and addressing higher
costs and longer delivery times for international goods.

suggested identifying the primary reasons people seek personal loans and targeting these segments
with tailored marketing and sales campaigns.

interest in the company's direction and long-term goals.

The assessment consisted of three sections: SQL, Python, and Aptitude (Quants), and it was conducted over
a duration of 25 minutes. We had to reach college by 8:45 AM, and the assessment started at 9:00 AM. A
question paper was given, and we had to tick the answers for the aptitude section like MCQS, and write
down the SQL queries and Python code.
The SQL section included 2 queries related to joins, group by, having and where clause and one was an
output based question where we had to write down the output for different types of joins. I would classify
the questions as easy to medium level. For Python, the task was to find the sum of n numbers, which was the
easiest question. The aptitude section featured easy to medium level questions, mostly logical type
questions. It tests your speed, so try to maintain a good pace.
To prepare for this round, understand how to write pseudocode, build logic for Python, and be proficient in
SQL queries. They won't ask very hard Python and SQL questions, but it's important to have a solid grasp
of the basics. Do not neglect the aptitude section. More than testing your Python and SQL skills, they want
to assess your critical thinking and your ability to think logically.

2. Round 2: Interview 1[39 students were shortlisted for this round]

There were three interview panels. My interview was scheduled after lunch, around 2 PM, and lasted
approximately 30-35 minutes. The panel consisted of three experienced interviewers. They began by asking
how my day was going and then inquired about my family background. Then they told me to introduce
myself. They also asked why I was interested in a Business Analyst role.
When answering this question, I shared some personal experiences to provide a realistic and authentic
response. It's important to be ready for such HR questions and prepare for them before the placement
process begins.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Then they asked me to rate myself out of 10 in SQL. I said 8, and they proceeded to ask SQL questions
based on this rating. They asked about the difference between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause,
the purpose of the GROUP BY function, and the execution sequence of SQL statements. I correctly
answered all their questions.
Next, they delved into my resume and asked questions related to my projects. One of my projects was
related to machine learning, so they inquired about my choice of algorithm, how it works, and any
challenges I faced during the project.
Afterward, they asked about my hobbies. Initially, I mentioned sports, but since many candidates were asked
guesstimates related to sports, they requested I share another interest. I mentioned Yoga, and they asked me
to estimate the number of people practicing Yoga in Mumbai. While answering the guesstimate, keep
explaining your approach to the interviewer, as they are often helpful and may provide hints. Even if your
estimate is much higher or lower than what they expect, it's important to stick to your answer and justify it
with examples. They might cross-question your estimate, but remain confident and provide proper
explanations.
Usually, interviewers ask if you have any questions at the end, but in this case, they didn't. I took the
initiative to ask them some questions I had prepared based on my research about Incred Finance. They were
quite impressed by this. If you have any questions, do ask them, as it shows your interest and preparation.
If you have tech projects in your resume then just make sure to justify why they should still select you for a
non tech role.
Be prepared with some guestimate and case study questions. I will list down the links at the end of the
document.

on various case studies, primarily related to lending terms. The session began with me introducing myself,

interviewers were quite impressed.

1. Aptitude and Technical Test [90 mins]:

The first round was a comprehensive test that included aptitude, technical multiple-choice questions
(MCQS), and coding. It was divided into 7 sections, and the total duration was 90 minutes. One coding
question was provided, and 30 aptitude questions had to be completed within 30 minutes. The aptitude
section was timed and non-navigable, meaning you can navigate between questions but once you exited this
section, you couldn't return to it.
The remaining sections covered subjects like Data Structures (DS), Database Management Systems
(DBMS), Computer Networks (CCN), and Object-Oriented Programming (OOPs). Unlike the aptitude
section, these technical sections were untimed and fully navigable, allowing candidates to move between
questions as needed.

• Coding: 1 coding question:

Evan needs to collect the maximum number of fruits from a garden matrix by moving up to K steps,
starting from a given position, and can move to adjacent cells only once per visit. The goal is to
return the maximum fruits collected in K steps.
Answer: Use Depth-First Search DFS) with backtracking to explore all possible paths and track the
maximum fruits collected.

• Aptitude: 30 timed questions based on logical reasoning, quantitative aptitude, and verbal ability.

• Technical Sections: MCQs on DS, DBMS, CCN, and OOPs. The questions tested fundamental

concepts in each subject.
Number of students shortlisted: After this round, 31 candidates were shortlisted.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Technical + HR Interview 30-40 mins :

This round had two panels, one panel focusing more on your resume and the other delving into Data
Structures and Algorithms (DSA). It was essential to be well-versed with your resume and to have a good
understanding of core subjects like DBMS, OOPs, and DSA.
Interview Experience:
I started by introducing myself and explaining one of my projects. The interviewers went in-depth, asking
me why I had chosen MongoDB instead of MySQL, leading to a discussion about the differences between
SQL and NoSQL databases.
They first asked me about some React related questions like What is Virtual DOM.
Since Python was my primary language, they asked me about the difference between lists and tuples.
As I had mentioned C and Java in my resume, they asked a question from C about the difference between
pointers and references.
Lastly, they presented me with a puzzle to solve, which I was unable to answer, but I asked the interviewer
to explain the approach. This shows that you are open to learning and not just there for the interview.
Next, they asked me about my family background and about a leadership role I had in one of my internship
projects, specifically how I divided the work among my teammates. They also asked how I would handle a
situation with a tight deadline, and that was it.
Overall it was an easy round. You just need to be confident when explaining your projects and concepts and
stay calm and speak your approach during the puzzle-solving portion, as they're often looking to see your
thought process.

3. HR (With VP) |10-15 mins]:

The final round was a 10-15 minute interview with the VP.
It was more of a conversation to assess your mindset and goals.
Interview Experience:
He began by asking how my day was and whether I understood how things work in a corporate
environment. He then asked about my strengths, giving me the choice between development, data science,
and cloud. I told him that while I'm open to exploring various domains, my first choice would be data
science.
He asked if I had any questions for him, and that concluded the interview.
This was the final round and 10 students including me were offered the job.
--- PAGE 3 ---

• Aptitude: Focus on practicing timed tests with a variety of problems. Indiabix can be sufficient for

preparing and answering the aptitude questions.

• Technical: Make sure you have a solid grasp of DSA, DBMS, and OOPs concepts. Practicing

common DSA problems on platforms like LeetCode and GeeksforGeeks can help.

• Resume: Mention relevant projects and technical skills clearly. Be thorough with everything you

have mentioned in your resume.

The following rounds were conducted in order:

1) Pre-placement talk

2) Online Assessment (on Hackerrank platform)

3) Interview Round 1

4) Interview Round 2

1.     Online Assessment [~240 students appeared]

The first round was the online assessment, conducted right after the pre-placement talk. Around
240 students appeared for this round, as students from both SPIT and SPCE were eligible to
apply.
The assessment was for 1 hour on Hackerrank platform and consisted of 18 questions covering
logical reasoning, aptitude, basic supply chain concepts, programming and SQL. The
programming and SQL questions were straightforward, as were the supply chain questions if
you had a basic understanding of the concepts of supply-demand, inventory, process planning,
graph interpretation etc. Having pursued a minor in management at SPJIMR, I was able to
answer all the supply chain-related questions. The programming question (1 question only) I
got was to find the sum of numbers from 1 to n using a loop. The SQL questions were simple
as well (2 questions) and could be solved using just SELECT statement with WHERE
condition.
22 students were shortlisted for the next round based on resume and the online assessment
score. (Make sure you attempt most questions accurately and submit the assessment as quick
as possible as shortlisting was also done based on speed).

2. Interview Round 1 [22 students appeared]

This was a personal interview round. There were 4 panels and each panel had 1 interviewer.
My interview lasted about 30 minutes. The interviewer first introduced himself and his position
in the company and then asked for my introduction. After the introduction, we moved to
questions.
The questions consisted of guesstimates, puzzles, basics of supply chain and some were resume
based as well. I was asked a guesstimate question to find/estimate the number of ATMs in
Andheri. I could reasonably solve the question and the interviewer was satisfied with my
approach. Next, I was asked a puzzle of 5L, 3L water containers - you have a 3L and a 5L
water container, and neither one is marked aside from the total volume. In order to measure out
exactly 4L of water, we must utilize the containers in the right way. How is this possible? I had
read this puzzle beforehand and so could answer easily.
For guesstimate questions, practice a wide range of scenarios to improve your estimation skills.
Focus on breaking down complex problems into smaller, manageable parts and making
reasonable assumptions. Familiarize yourself with common guesstimate frameworks like
market sizing, population estimates, and resource distribution. This will help you approach
these questions with confidence and structure during interviews.
For the puzzles, go through and practice Geeks for Geeks puzzles for interviews. Almost all
types of puzzles asked during the interviews of any company are from here.
Some other questions I was asked:

1) What is supply chain, who are the stakeholders in a supply chain, what are the different

stages of supply chain and what moves from one process to another in a supply chain
(answer - money, goods, information).

2) My understanding of the role

3) Describe your internship as a web development intern

4) Describe your BTech major project and how you are planning to go forward

5) One SQL question to find the count of IDs grouped by country and ordered

alphabetically in a table having columns - ID, country

6) One programming question to find and display all prime numbers between a given

range (num1 to num2)
10 students qualified for the next round.

3. Interview Round 2 [10 students appeared]

This was the final round of the process. There were 2 panels, first panel had 1 interviewer and
the second panel had 2 interviewers. My interview was taken by the second panel and lasted
about 40-45 minutes.
The questions asked in this round were similar to the ones asked in the first interview round.
There was one guesstimate question - find/estimate the number of cups of tea consumed in
Mumbai in a month and one puzzle - two people went to a cafe together and both ordered iced
tea. One person drank ten of them in 30 minutes, and the other drank just one in the same time.
The person who drank one was poisoned, while the other who drank ten was fine. But, all of
the drinks that were served turned out to contain poison. Why did the person that drank more
iced tea survive? I took a little longer than expected to reach the final solution but was able to
get hints and convince the interviewers about my approach and solution.
Keep asking clarifying questions about the guesstimate/puzzle if you are unable to recall or get
to the solution right away. The interviewers often give some important hints to guide you to the
right solution. Also keep them informed about what you are thinking and how you are
approaching the problem instead of just solving on a paper silently. This lets them know about
how you approach problems, how you think, how you apply logic, etc and they can correct you
if you go wrong in some step.
Some other questions I was asked:

1) Are you good with handling pressure and what are you doing to get better at it?

2) If given an easy task and a difficult task, which one will I do first and explain why?

3) Are you good at multi-tasking, how do you prioritize things?

4) How did you work on improving your weaknesses?

These were some basic HR questions. You can go through some general HR questions asked
in interviews that are available on the internet and prepare general answers for them
beforehand. These questions are asked in the HR rounds of almost all companies.
5 students, including me were offered the internship/placement.

1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (All students above 6 CGPA were shortlisted)

Also take care to fill the Deloitte 's form properly on their website which includes candidate basic
information and submission of resume.

2. Round 2: Online test

Test Duration: 1 Hour
Platform: HirePro (We can take the test from home.)
Test information: 3 Sections (Aptitude, Reasoning, Verbal skills, 2 Coding Questions)
Each section was having definite time (no switching between sections), MCQ's were mostly easy and
solvable.
Coding Questions:
Question 1: This question is based on the concept of input validation and string processing. It asks
to determine whether the input is an integer or a string. If the input consists only of digits, output
"integer"; otherwise, output "string".

Question 2: Write a function that takes an array of numbers and returns the sum of all positive numbers
that can be divided only by 2, 3, or 5. These numbers should reduce to 1 when divided by these primes
repeatedly.

3. Round 3: Online Interview (Technical + HR: 30 min) [35 Students]

One day before the interview, we were assigned specific time slots for our interviews, each lasting 30
minutes. My interview was scheduled from 10:30 to 11:00 AM.
My interview began with an introduction where I talked about myself, highlighting my projects, the
technology stack I used, competitions I participated in and extracurricular activities. I also mentioned
my interest in chess, which prompted the interviewer to ask me a few questions about it.

After that, the interviewer asked me about my projects, starting with my data analysis project. She
requested a detailed explanation of the project and the technology stack I used. Following that, she
inquired about group project I worked on, which was based on the MERN stack. I mentioned that my
focus within the group was specifically on JWT, WebSocket, and Zustand. She then asked me to
explain the architecture of this project and the workings of  JWT in detail, which I was able to articulate
clearly. Then the interviewer asked about the challenges I faced during the project and whether there
were any conflicts among group members while working on it.
Then the interviewer inquired about how I managed my time to work on these projects alongside my
exams and major projects. Additionally, she wanted to know about my strengths and weaknesses. She
also sought my approach to learning a new technology in detai l. Finally, she wanted to know what
recent technology I had used, which one was my favorite, and the reasons behind my choice.
The final part of the interview involved her asking if I had any questions. I took this opportunity to
inquire about the culture at Deloitte and the specifics of the job description.
I had only one interview, while some students attended two. In the evening, the results were announced,
and 15 students were selected for the opportunity, and I was one of them.

Important tips:

• Be confident.

• Familiarize yourself with your resume so you can explain your projects and every detail you've

included.

• Some candidates were asked basic DSA questions, OOPS concepts, as well as DBMS and SQL

queries.

• Practice DSA regularly.

• Participate in mock interviews to improve your skills.

ALL THE BEST!
