1. Round 1: Resume Shortlisting (All students above 6 CGPA were shortlisted)

Before Resume Shortlisting we were asked to fill the registration form on their website, make sure
you stick to any one resume format and use the same email address everywhere you apply and make
sure you fill all applicable fields.

2. Round 2: Online test

Test Duration: 1 Hour
Platform: HirePro
Test information: 3 Sections (Aptitude, Reasoning, Verbal skills, 2 Coding Questions) Each section
was having definite time (no switching between sections), MCQ's were mostly easy and solvable.
And last section was coding, coding Questions asked were so easy to solve. More weightage was on
solving aptitude reasoning and solving MCQ.

3. Round 3: Online Interview (Technical + HR: 30 min) [35 Students]

A day before the interview we were assigned specific time slots for the interview. Each slot was 30
minutes and my interview was scheduled from 10.00 to 10.30 AM.
My interview began with the interviewer introducing himself, followed by my introduction. I had
prepared an impressive introduction, which included details about my experience, projects, skills, and,
most importantly, my achievements. Preparing a strong introduction is essential because it allows you to
steer the direction of the interview. After my introduction, he asked me in detail about my internship at a
startup. This was followed by some technical questions and one HR question: "How has this internship
helped you grow?" Another question was related to my work and coordination with the founders, though
--- PAGE 2 ---
I don't remember it exactly.
He then asked me three in-depth questions about the frontend, mainly regarding React. I answered two of
them but couldn't answer the third one correctly. When he asked if I was sure about my answer to the
third question, I was honest and explained that I had been more focused on backend work and hadn't
worked on the frontend in several months. Never lie in your interview.
He also asked detailed questions about Docker. Since I had mentioned AWS in my resume, he asked
about where I had used it and my experience with it. Later, he asked if I had taken on any leadership
roles, to which I mentioned leading a team of four developers in building the Oculus event website, as
well as leading my team in the National Hackathon at Barclays.
I had also noted my activity as a problem solver on LeetCode and my strong ranking in their contests. He
asked me an HR question about how participating in contests on LeetCode helps me upskill. Then he
asked what language I prefer for contests, to which I answered C++. He followed up with questions about
different types of data structures, asking me to provide real-life examples. Afterward, he gave me three
DSA questions (focused on string manipulation, stack, and recursion) and asked me to explain my
approach, to which I provided three approaches for each. Then, he asked two SQL questions and one
query.
He also asked if I'd be comfortable working with unfamiliar technologies. I told him that I would be,
sharing how I had learned AWS, Docker, and other tools during my internship, demonstrating my
"learn-as-you-go' attitude.
Finally, he concluded by asking if I had any questions for him. Make sure to prepare plenty of specific,
interesting questions about the company-avoid generic ones. He didn't ask me about my projects,
likely because there was already so much information on my resume. I had designed my resume in a way
that ensured specific questions would come up.
I had only one interview, while some students attended two. In the evening, the results were announced,
and 15 students were selected for the opportunity-I was one of them.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Important tips:

1. Prepare an well-crafted introduction

2. Make notes during pre-placement talk

3. Solve striver's A2Z DSA sheet at least once; you don't need to be a knight on LC or a pupil on

CF to clear the interview rounds

4. Solving LC top 50 SQL sheet will give you enough ideas about different types of possible sql

questions

5. Dont panic in the interview, simply ask for help-interviewers are very helpful

6. Practice mock interview with friends

7. Thinking aloud might help you a lot

8. After every interview, prepare genuine questions and avoid generic ones. The notes you made

during the pre-placement talk might assist you here. Prefer asking follow-up questions and
engage in a conversation

9. Don't mess up with your CGPA. It will kill your chances and it hurts :)

Linking resume for reference: Resume

All the best for your placements!!!

journey.prep:
• For ppt

Make sure to attend every pre-placement talk (PPT) attentively, whether it's online or offline. Actively
engage with the company representatives and ask thoughtful questions about the company, job
description, and recruitment process. It's important to leave a positive impression on the HR team, so
ask meaningful questions that show your interest and understanding of the role.

• For Online Assessment

For aptitude preparation, practice regularly on platforms like IndiaBix. You can also refer to
YouTube channels such as Carrer rides, campus Monk, or any other channel, but it's best to
stick to one consistently instead of switching between multiple sources --most of them cover
the same topics, just with different teaching styles. Also, avoid getting stuck on aptitude
preparation for too long.
For DBMS and OS, I recommend following Love Babbar's playlist and supplementing it with
theory from GeeksforGeeks (GFG). For Computer Networks (CCN), you can find good

resources on YouTube, but I personally relied on Karia Sir's notes. If you attend CCN lectures
regularly, that should also be sufficient.
For DSA, there are numerous resources available online. Start by mastering the basics and
practicing on platforms like LeetCode, Codeforces, or Coding Ninjas. If you have enough time,
I highly recommend following Striver's A to Z DSA playlist and solving the prob lems
thoroughly. A to Z
If you're short on time, focus on Striver's SDE sheet or LeetCode's Top 75 questions for
efficient preparation.
For Java, you can refer to Kunal Kushwaha's playlist or JavaTpoint for comprehensive learning
resources. I recommend covering all the theory, especially Java and OOP concepts, from
JavaTpoint. https://www.javatpoint.com/java-tutorial

• For Interviews

For interviews, it's crucial to participate in as many mock interviews as possible, as they are very
helpful for the actual interviews. Perfect your self -introduction and ensure you know your resume
inside and out, word for word. Prepare for standard HR qu estions by researching them online, and be
honest about your experiences--never lie on your resume. Give it your best shot, and also make sure
to practice puzzles; aim to solve at least the top 100 puzzles from GeeksforGeeks. Puzzles
It's helpful to practice guesstimates with friends or solo and review situational questions in advance.
This will build your confidence and improve your approach during interviews. Always start by
explaining your approach before diving into the solution, and keep interacting with the interviewer as
you code. If you get stuck, don't hesitate to ask for hints --it shows you're open to guidance and
collaborative problem-solving!

"Confidence in your abilities is key to making a positive impression."

• General tips

The placement process can be truly challenging --Deloitte is my 30th application! Throughout this
journey, holding on to faith and patience is essential. Never give up, and always put forth your best
effort. It can feel discouraging when friends get placed b efore you, but keep believing in yourself.
Your opportunity will come too. Remember, everything happens for a reason, and while luck can play
a role, it's ultimately your hard work and smart work that can truly change your path. Keep pushing
forward, stay consistent, and trust the journey--you're closer than you think!
Remember this: in Mumbai, if you miss one local train, another one is always on the way. Just like
that, if one company doesn't work out at S.P.I.T., another will come along. So, don't feel disheartened
if one opportunity doesn't go your way--stay resilient!

Whenever it feels like you've reached your limit, remember: you're closer to your goal than you think.
Take that next step with courage and confidence--you're on the brink of something great. Believe in
yourself; you can do it!!

For any doubts you can connect with me on LinkedIn
sahil tayde

1. [Online Assessment] [100+ candidate] Aptitude + Coding

The test consisted of five sections, each with a time limit. In the aptitude section, each question required
a minimum of 45 seconds to complete. For the coding section, we were given 35 minutes to solve two
coding problems. The coding questions were relatively easy, but time management was crucial.

2. Interview [34 candidates]

After the online assessment, 34 students were shortlisted for the interview round, which was conducted online.
Though we could attend the interview from anywhere, I would suggest giving it from the TPO office for a
better setup.
My interview started at 10 AM. It began with a request to introduce myself, followed by some basic questions
on probability, such as the probability of getting heads and the probability of getting two consecutive heads.
Next, we moved on to the coding section. I was asked to solve two problems using a code editor:

1. Finding the factors of a number

2. Calculating the sum up to a given number

After coding, the interviewer shifted to Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) concepts. They asked about the
importance of OOP, had me write pseudocode to implement inheritance, and discussed the significance of
inheritance. I was then asked to write a code to find the second-highest number in an array. Initially, I provided
a solution using array sorting, but the interviewer wasn't satisfied and asked for optimization. I then offered a
solution using a set, which they accepted. They also advised me to ask clarifying questions before jumping to
a solution.
Toward the end, the interviewer asked if I had any questions, and I inquired about the job description and
current projects. The technical section was mixed with a few soft skills questions as well, such as how I would
handle a team member not contributing in a group project or how I would manage conflict within a team.
It's worth noting that the interview structure varied based on the panel. Some panels focused only on technical
questions, others on soft skills and management, while my panel asked a blend of both.
After this round, a few candidates were called for a second interview, but I wasn't. I thought I might not make
it and was already gearing up for the next opportunity. However, after a long wait of around six hours, the
final results were announced. Fifteen students were selected, and I was one of them.

--- PAGE 4 ---
I believe what made this process seem so smooth was because of the multiple interviews I had faced

understanding, or questions which are smaller in length (straight up questions asking what to do rather

selected for the next round. They released the selected list at around 12:30pm with my name not being

and was exiting college entrance....But to my surprise they released another set of lists with my name
being in the list!!
Destiny had other plans today
), I sat near TPO waiting for my interview round which was
scheduled second last in my panel: (
I knew that I would have to wait but the waiting game was on peak that day. People had their HR
round, but my 1st round had not even happened so ofc I became nervous. Also every person in my panel
was saying the interview went damn good thus adding on to my nervousness.
Ok enough with the environment setup, It was around 5.30pm, I was told to wait inside, having been
faced with so many interviews till now, I was not at all nervous, I kinda had an idea of what the
interviewer was gonna ask me based on responses received by previous people. I went in with a smile,
sat down, there was only one panelist being the head of assurance & data quality, having 20+ years of
experience. He asked me for my intro, then we moved on to my internship project. I explained from
scratch with a real life example and application of my project, then he asked me about my internship
experience.
He then asked me to code an SOL joins and group by question on a second laptop. I knew SQL in
depth so solving this question was a piece of cake, I solved it in under 2 mins and ig he was surprised
somewhat, then he moved on to a Pandas group by function (value_counts), I was solving it but the
provided laptop had 15% battery so I told him that the laptop battery is quite low and that if i can go
outside and fetch charger for it. He said yes, and I brought back a charger but due to brand mismatch, it
didn't fit and then he joked saying you have limited time now to solve it and we shared a genuine laugh
on this and I solved the question.
He then asked me about my family background, where I stay, why this role interested me and other
--- PAGE 3 ---
basic questions. The whole interview surprisingly lasted not more than 15 mins. At the end, I asked him
a few questions about how ISS sources its Data, what type of projects he currently is working on and if I
got selected for this role, what would be that one piece of advice he would give me. The interview ended
on a very positive note.
(I was tensed ki interview went only for like 15 mins, will I even be selected as I was also one of the
last guys, but everything happens for a reason and within 20mins of the interview ending, I got a call
saying my HR was scheduled in some time:))

3. [HR Round] [17 shortlisted, 12 Selected]

I don't know what happened but HR rounds generally tend to be allocated no more than 25-30 mins.
But for me the case was different, my HR lasted for around 45 mins.
The HR round was taken by the MD of ISS (India region) and HR head (Asia Pacific Region). I was
greeted and was asked to hand in my resume. The HR comforted me by asking if I had anything as the
round started at 7pm to which I replied yes. At first she asked me if I knew their names, to which I
confidently replied Yes and told them their names. (For this, attending PPT with focus is very very
crucial). They were happy that I knew their names and joked about me getting selected solely on this :)
She liked that I was attentive enough to know their names.
They then asked me for my intro, then HR asked me for my internship project (As HR had asked,
hence I explained in layman terms excluding the TECH part out of it), then we had a brief discussion
on my family background, she asked details about my parents education, what my father does, what my
mother does, it was more of an informal chatting session (so much that I told her about my mom's yt
cooking channel and she note the name down
Then the MD of ISS asked me about the role offered, what part of it attracted me? He specifically
asked me to give info about what parts were mentioned in the JD (be sure to go through Job Description
before your interviews as you got to have clarity about the job profile and firm you are applying for). I
answered all this questions, correlating my answers with ISS values (to score brownie points
He then asked me that there would come a moment in future where you would be satisfied with the tasks
you are performing and that what would be the amount of time that I would take to move on to next
profile/ role (basically asking me the no. of years i would take to switch roles/ switch firm). I don't know
what Aristotle got in me & I answered philosophically by saying that the no. of years doesn't matter,
what matters is the quantity and most importantly the quality of projects that I get to work on. (he
seemed happy, which ultimately boosted my confidence)
The HR then asked me about traveling as I stay at Thane and goregaon is as you know far away...to
which I replied that I have been traveling to and fro from azad nagar to thane for 2.5 years and goregaon
would be the same. She then started explaining to me about the employee benefits @ ISS and work
culture, while also stating that If I'm selected for the role, I would be locked for the firm. (at this point i
had a strong feeling that I was selected for ISS & was bringing it home, but everything's
unpredictable and you gotta be calm until the final list is released). As many people were yet to give
the HR round, they told us to go home and the final list would be released before midnight. The
interview ended with me asking them for advice about this role (if I'm selected) and a general feedback
of the interview. This one too ended on a really positive note.
At the end 12 People were selected (including me) and were offered the Job!!

Initially they had kept a cutoff of 8.5 CGPA for applying to any of the 4 roles, which was
further lowered to 7.5/8 . For software testing role it was reduced to 7.5, for other roles it was
kept 8.

1. Online Assessment [Approx 155 students appeared]

The assessment was conducted offline in college, and was on google forms. There were approx. 70
questions which had to be completed in 90 minutes. The marking scheme was +1, -0.25 and there
were 4 sections- Java based (18 Q), Python based (17 Q), SQL based (5)  and Aptitude questions
(30).
Java questions were related to enums, multithreading, filtering, streams, scope of variables, OOPS
etc. Python questions were mostly OOPs related and some basic but tricky ones. Both these sections
involved code snippets to determine the output. Aptitude involved CAT type questions on  volume,
distance speed, simple compound interest, graphs, etc.
For Aptitude use a bit of guesstimates and elimination methods . For some questions just by looking
at options you could figure out what could be the possible solution and that would save some of
your valuable time. There were a few tricky questions which were difficult to understand, leave
those questions for later. I solved dsa questions in C++ so Java and python sections were a little
tricky for me but you can solve all the logical questions and some questions were syntax and
functions related for that you can refer to 1000 python questions for an interview on Sanfoundry.
Remember that not all students are familiar with both python and java and so even if you are unable
to solve their questions dont panic and focus on logical questions from all the sections.

2. Technical Round [49 students selected]

After the OA, 49 students were shortlisted for the technical round. There were a total of 8 panels,
with distribution based on role preference. My panel included 9 candidates, and I was the fourth
one to be interviewed. The interview began with an introduction, followed by questions about my
projects, why I applied for the Analytical Verification role, how I became interested in analytics and
when and how I started studying data analytics. Try to answer this question passionately and show
genuine interest in the role. I shared about how I watch a lot of sports like Cricket and Football and
there is a lot of data analytics involved over there. I also talked about data analytics while investing
in stock market.  Then I talked about my projects and my internship experience which were mainly
about database design and data analytics.
While talking about projects don't reply in a monotonous tone as it will appear memorized and
may not seem genuine. Prepare for questions about the Tech stack, what problem you solved by
the project, real life use cases etc.
He also asked me to rate my proficiency in SQL and Pandas on a scale of 1 to 5. After that, the
interviewer handed me a laptop with a question and asked me import an excel file in Pandas. I
logged in my colab account and imported the file. Then he asked me to describe the excel sheet. I
used df.describe and df.info function. He then asked me to once see the excel file to know about
the columns and then asked a query about the file. Instead of opening in excel I used df.head
command and opened the file in colab itself. He then asked me to return count of number of
matches held at each venue. I didn't remember the syntax so I explained him the logic and talked
how I leverage AI technologies for syntax and to know about different functions faster and get the
task done efficiently.
Then he asked me to write a SQL query on an online compiler. The question was easy; I had to
identify the relevant tables from a large set and solve the problem using joins and group by
functions ( The question was to find the best product for each company and the number of sales
for that product ). Towards the end, the interviewer asked about my future plans, my family
background, and my understanding of the role. The interview lasted for about 30 minutes.
The one who went just before me was asked 7 to 8 coding questions and his interview went for 1
hr. So if you are not confident about your technical skills you can still drive the interview to projects
side.  Also don't panic if your interview was for a shorter duration as how long your interview goes
doesn't determine your selection. Also remember to at least ask one question to the interviewer. I
had prepared a staple question that I had asked in all my interviews about integration of AI tools in
their tech stack and day to day operations and based on their answer I more often then not asked
another follow up question.

3. HR Round [17 students selected ]

There were 2 panellists in this interview, the MD of ISS and the HR. They first asked me about my
family background, if I had any plans of higher studies?. After that the MD asked me that why did u
decide to apply for this role, what do you know about data analytics, etc. I explained how I have
observed data in sports and stock market. I also mentioned my internship experience and about my
projects which were based on data analytics. Then he asked about data pipeline of my project. I
explained how I obtained my data, how I made changes etc. Then HR asked about my greatest
academic achievement. Other generic HR questions were asked, this was a pretty chill interview
round where you just have to be honest and frank but remember to not mention any negative
aspects. My interview went on for 25-30 mins.
Finally 12 students got the offer!!!(Including MCA candidates)

A total of 3 rounds were conducted - 1 Online Assessment Round, 1 Tech Interview Round & Finally 1 HR
Round. All were conducted on the same day. The CGPA Criteria for SDE was 8.5, later reduced to 8. Only
for testing role it was further reduced to 7.5. May not be the case for next year if they don't want more
applicants in testing so it is preferable to maintain a pointer of 8.5 and above

1. [Online Assessment] [155 appeared, ~ 49 selected] Invigilated by Company Officials

The Online Assessment had 70 Questions in total & lasted for 90 mins. 40 Technical Questions (18 Java, 17
Python, 5 SQL) & 30 Aptitude Questions (primarily quantitative questions). There was 1 correct mark for
every right answer & -0.25 for wrong answer. There was no specific weightage to any section as such and all
questions had equal marks. Physical Calculators were not allowed but on screen you could use what your
laptop OS provided.
Tech Questions in Java were mainly around the actual application of language in industry & snippets were
given for which output was asked in majority of the questions. There were things like ConcurrentHashmap,
Consumer objects & stuff which I had never even heard of as a part of our curriculum & other things such
as. I first attempted those questions around OOPS which I was confident of. Did a couple of questions by
eliminating options & left the rest. I also attempted two questions based on their extreme similarity to
javascript. One was somewhat similar to resolving Promise and another one based on filtering & a sort of
then syntax. I was okay with losing 0.5 marks just in case they were wrong.
I then moved to the next section on Python. It was very heavy on OOPS in python. I had only done OOPS in
Java & C++ in detail & only knew the basics in python so was slightly taken aback. I still attempted the
questions which involved concepts common to all languages. Skipped a question which involved multiple
inheritance because I was not aware it was allowed or not. Other questions were around lists, sets & strings
and were very easy.
Next I moved to the SQL section. Here questions had given the schema & the task to be performed & we
were asked to select the correct query among 4 options. Questions were of easy level but they were listed as
--- PAGE 2 ---
continuous sentences & not written line by line in indented form so it was difficult to find the differences
between them.
I completed the above 3 rounds in around 30-32 minutes.
Finally I went to the Aptitude round with 1 hour in hand. It has questions primarily around permutations &
combinations, ratio proportion, simple & compound interest & interpretation & calculation based on
bar-graph and equation based questions on speed, time, distance. Boat moving upstream, downstream type
of Questions. I attempted the easy questions first, then went over the questions which would require more
time in calculation in the second iteration. I was able to do almost ~80% of the questions here.
Tip: Don't attempt questions you are not very sure of in tests with negative marking. In mcq tests which do
not have any negative marking don't leave any questions unanswered.

2.
[Technical Interview] [49 appeared, 17 shortlisted] 2 panelists in my interview panel
(For me it lasted for 35-40 ish minutes, in some panels the interviewer only took interviews for 6-7 minutes)
I was asked to wait some time before I went after the next candidate (I later found out that they went through
all the links of my projects and my github profile) They asked me to give my introduction in brief
mentioning my academic background, projects & explain the project I am most passionate about mentioning
the team size, my role & my contribution in the project. Then they asked me a few cross questions around
our approach & since it involved chatbot, how did we train it etc. I answered about my role in front end so
the second panelist asked questions such as Why React? Framework vs Library, Is NextJs a framework or
library with reason & then it clicked to me that he was using words from my answer itself to move on to the
next question, for subsequent questions I was careful of not using tech terms that I was unsure of. He then
asked me about my MongoDB over SQL databases, what is scalable, what is not, how is data stored in
mongodb, if i could redesign in hindsight would I use SQL or NoSQL. What benefits one provides over the
other, ACID properties in databases. Then the first panelist asked me how confident I was in java & other
languages. I told him we had some of it as a part of our curriculum but for DSA I used C++ & Javascript for
webdev. He gave me his laptop with a java file and asked me to code solver function for a problem -
Q. Given a string like "Hii, today is the greatest day ever with balloons giggling" and asked me to find the
word for which max characters are getting repeated. I thought the answer should be "giggling" as g repeats 4
times but he clarified that "greatest" should be the answer as two characters 'e' & '' are repeated & that the
frequency/ no of times individual characters repeated did not matter.
--- PAGE 3 ---
I proceeded by writing my approach on paper & basically thinking out loud as I was writing it. He then
asked me to optimize my approach by moving from set to map. I did so & when he was satisfied he asked
me to code it. I acknowledged that I am not able to recall the Java syntax of inserting into a map but I am
confident that I could do it in cpp & asked his permission to do so (This is where on his laptop I saw all my
profiles & links were opened in new tabs). He agreed & I coded it quickly in cpp & when I ran the code I
got an error saying map[character] cannot be accessed. He said maybe you aren't able to do it in cpp too but
I quickly figured out that I had written map[character] instead of frequency[character] (simple mistake in
cpp) & ran it and it worked. He then asked the other panelist to ask questions. The panelist asked me
questions about OOPS in Java & I realized that he was asking the same questions that were there in the OA
in the morning. I explained my approach to those questions & MCQS. Here is where he asked about the
question which has syntax similar to javascript & how I was able to do it. I honestly accepted that I did not
know it & I used common sense & some simple programming logic to do it. He then asked about a Question
on ConcurrentHashMaps which I had earlier left in the test. I said I did not know what they were but also
added that I knew what hashmaps were. We discussed some things about hashmaps in general & then he
proceeded to ask the first panelist to ask me questions. Panelist asked me how comfortable I am with SQL
& I told upto joins, aggregate functions & subqueries. He then asked me a simple Question
Q. Find employees with max salary in each city
I started writing the query but midway asked for clarification if multiple people could have the max salary.
And then wrote it accordingly, he told me that there was a simple syntax error which I was not immediately
able to resolve so they pointed it out. I said yes I overlooked it by mistake as I was focusing on only the
max(salary) part instead of the group by clause. One last thing they asked was a very famous puzzle similar
to Chicken, Fox and Grain Riddle (Solution Using Original Images) - DigiNo I gave a step by step approach
in a diagram form. They then asked me what questions I had for them. I asked them about the projects
interns work on & tech stack they use & which dept. is allotted to them etc.

Tips:

• Do not lie on your Resume but you can smartly change phrases so that your resume looks good.

• Do not throw the sheets/papers in which you did your OA questions. They can be asked in an

interview.

• Make sure if you are adding any links then they are clickable in your resume

• Prepare well around your resume projects & its tech stack. You can ask your friend to keep on cross

questioning you on them

• Prepare a couple of scenarios (even if fake) about disagreement in the team, or any times that you

have shown leadership/ team spirit. These questions are very common too.

• If you don't know the answer or you are not able to recall it, try to put it across politely instead of

saying something wrong

• Think out loud when solving a DSA problem/ SQL query but when saying a theory answer try to sort

of structure it in your mind first. Make use of technical terms & examples where possible

• If possible have examples of OOPS in a different setting, not those regular Animal or Car Inheritance

sort of things. This makes your answer slightly novel & interesting.
Resources :

• For Languages: Same as in above section

• For Project Related: Depends on your Tech Stack. Go through GFG and Interview Experiences

across all drives, see what all questions they have been asked.

• Technical Interview Questions - A Complete 2023 List

--- PAGE 4 ---

• The Ultimate Guide to Acing Your Technical Interview - InterviewBit

3. ¡HR Round] [17 appeared, 12 Selected] 1 HR & 1 MD in panel

(For me this lasted 15-17 ish minutes, for others it was around 25-30 & event 35 mins in some cases)
This was the last round where they first introduced themselves & then asked me to introduce myself stating
my academic background, some information about my family & my most favorite project. Then I was cross
questioned on my Minor Degree in Management & why I was doing it etc. Then there was quite some
discussion on my project, what I learnt from it. What was the team like, how I resolved any conflicts etc.
After that they pointed out that I had a great academic record so why not go for masters. I answered by
stating that I need to support my family & my focus is completely on doing a job. Post that some discussion
around where I live & will I be able to commute to Nesco to their office. I said I travel to college daily &
Nesco is also almost at the same distance & assured them I will be able to do so. The MD then asked about
my preference in technology & I answered that I did not have preference as such & tried to showcase that I
can wear multiple hats by telling him that I do DSA in C++, web dev in javascript, have done Java, Python,
Blockchain programming as a part of curriculum & electives. He then asked if I was okay with
programming in. Net or app dev, I showed my enthusiasm & assurance that I will learn it if the project needs
it. Post that they asked if I had any questions for them. To the MD I asked what training is provided to
interns & what projects/tech they work on. To the HR I asked that I had gone through their website and
wanted to know more about the ISS University program that they have.
Around 10 PM the results were announced & 12 people were selected across all roles.
lips :

• Keep a Smile on your face when answering questions & Listen actively

• If asked about masters/further education say that you want to focus on job whatever be the reason

that suits you

• Go through the company website & understand what the company does

• Find something interesting & of interest to a fresher & ask questions about it to the HR

• Make sure you know the names of HRs/panelists in general, if not ask the TPCs

• Some general etiquettes like greeting when you enter, putting the chair back to its place when you

are about to leave.

There were 3 rounds: Online Assessment, Technical Interview and HR Interview

1.  Online Assessment [155 students appeared for the test]

It was a 90-minute assessment conducted on Google Forms. It consisted of 70 MCQ questions, and
there were four sections - Java (18 questions), Python (17 questions), SQL (5 questions) and aptitude (30
questions). The correct answer would give you 1 mark, -0.25 for incorrect answer and 0 for not attempting.

2. Technical Interview [50 students were shortlisted]

The interviewer asked me to introduce myself, and I mentioned that Java is my primary language for
competitive programming. He then asked me what 'immutable' means in Java. I explained the concept of
immutability and used the String class in Java as an example. I mentioned that when two variables are
initialized with the same value, such as String name1 = "Hina"; and String name2 = "Hina"; they both point
to the same location in the String pool because the String object is shared. If the value of a ny String variable
is changed, it app ears as if the value is edited, but in reality, a new instance is created, and the reference is
updated to point to this new instance.
Then he asked me how I would create a custom class that behaves similarly. I initially said by using a
constructor, but he was not satisfied with that answer. He explained the question again by writing a scenario
on the paper. In this scenario, there was a class A with a variable declared and a constructor, and he specified
that each time a new object should be created and the value cannot be edited. When he mentioned that the
value cannot be edited, the final keyword came to my mind, but I was confused because String allows us to
reassign the value, though a new object is created. He gave me a hint by asking what happens when a class is
final. I said that we cannot inherit from it, and then he asked how we assign values I said using a setter method.
Class A will be final so that other classes cannot extend it and change its value, and the setter method will be
removed to ensure immutability. This approach follows standard industry practices, where each class typically
includes a constructor along with getter and setter methods.
He then asked me how to assign a value to a variable in class B from an object of class B within cl ass A,
ensuring that the value is assigned only once. I initially suggested making the variable in class B final.
However, he pointed out that changes to class B were not allowed. I then suggested using the constructor of
class A to initialize class B's va riable by passing the value through class A's constructor, which in turn calls
the constructor of class B. I asked him if this approach was correct, and he said it was only partially correct I
then requested him to explain the correct approach.

The interview lasted for 10 minutes. The panel interviewed each candidate for 10 to 15 minutes.

3. HR Round [ 17 students were shortlisted]

The HR and Technical Head were present who took our PPT.
HR asked me to tell me about my education and family background.  If I was comfortable with the hybrid
model and the location? What are your other interests?

The Technical Head asked if I had appeared for the CET and what my percentile was. Since I scored lower on
the company's aptitude test, he asked if I wasn't prepared  and what the reason was.  He also asked whether I
preferred backend development or full stack. I said full stack, so he requested that I explain one of my projects
where I used full stack technology. I explained it in detail, mentioning why I chose a particular tech stack and
what I learned from it.

They also asked what else I had studied on my own, apart from what was taught in college.
The final question was, "Do you have any questions for us?"

12 students were offered the job

journey.prep:
1)Start your placement preparation as soon as possible. Focus on core subjects such as DBMS, OS,
Computer Networks, and OOPS. Make concise notes for future revision. Additionally, rescarch common
interview questions to get familiar with frequently asked topics and concepts.
2)Prepare your resume well. The resume should not include things that you may not be able to answer if
asked about in the interview. Listing things you can't explain may come across as dishonest and leave a poor
impression. At Least be aware of the basic concepts of the technologies mentioned. Also, fine-tune the
resume with minor changes according to the role.
3)The first step of the placement process is usually the company's presentation. Be attentive and note key
details about the company's history, products, and services. Clarify any doubts regarding roles and
responsibilities to make an informed decision and position yourself as a good fit for the role.
3)For OA's,practice makes the most difference. Start giving contests/timed-tests to improve your
problem-solving approach and identify areas where you need improvement.
4)For interviews, it's important to demonstrate your strengths and walk the interviewer through your
approach rather than rushing to get the correct answer immediately. Stay calm and confident, as it reassures
the interviewer that you can handle stressful situations effectively.

5) Don't lose hope, just focus on identifying how you can improve your chances of getting selected.

Understand your strengths and weaknesses, and continue to work on them throughout the process.
Feel free to reach out in case of any queries: Sankalp Dayal
journey.howSecured:
A total of 3 rounds were conducted- 1 Online Assessment Round,1 Technical Interview, and 1 HR
Round. All were conducted on the same day. The CGPA Criteria was 8.5,later reduced to 8,Only for testing
role,it was further reduced to 7.5. But make sure that your CGPA is at least 8 to be eligible for applying for
all 4 roles in the future for ISS-STOXX.

1. [Online Assessment] [155 appeared, ~ 49 selected] Invigilated by Company Officials

The test was conducted in College on Google Forms. 70 questions - 90 minutes. It had +1, -0.25
marking scheme.
Test was divided into 4 sections -
Java 18 questions
Python 17 questions
SQL 5 questions
Java and Python questions focused on OOPS concepts, frameworks,exception handling, and Lists. In Java
section, there were questions where output of the code was expected and most of them were based on
Streams. A basic understanding of map, filter, flatmap functions was enough to solve them.
For SQL Section, queries were asked for the given table and the required output. The queries covered
various topics like joins, date functions, subqueries. The questions were on easy to medium level but they
were listed as continuous sentences, making it slightly time-consuming and needing a double check.
The Aptitude round consisted of the normal Quantitative Aptitude questions such as Percentages,
Ratios, Time-Distance, Boat upstream-downstream, Probability etc. The questions were on an easy level with
few medium ones. The key was to identify questions were you are most confident and are well versed with
required formulae or logic.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The key point to note for the online assessment is to identify the questions where you can maximize your
score while minimizing risk due to negative marking. However, for assessments without negative marking,
attempt all questions.
Also, start preparing for Aptitude before the placement season. Keep a journal with important formulae or
time-saving techniques so that you can attempt maximum questions in a limited time frame. For the Java and
Python section,just keep your basics clear along with a routine of solving MCQs to discover new topics or to
revise the studied topics.

2. [Technical Interview] [49 appeared, 17 shortlisted] 2 panelists in my interview panel

The students were divided into groups based on their first preference. My panel consisted of 9 students and
initially one panelist, but a second panelist joined during my interview. All the students in my panel were
applying for the SQL Developer role.
The interview began with the panelist asking me for my introduction, followed by why I chose the SQL
Developer role. Then, I was asked to solve a question and write the output on paper. Although I can't recall
the exact table values, the problem was focused on left and self joins, with the challenge being the presence
of duplicate entries and their impact on the joins. The conversation then shifted to questions about different
types of keys, their distinctions, and SQL constraints.
Then certain scenarios were presented to me and was asked about my initial approach. On further discussions
with the panelist, we arrived at an optimal way to approach the scenario. One of the scenario was:-
1)There's some data in T1 - i) Copy all data from that in T2. ii) Copy only the latest data (last row).
2)There's a table present with multiple records already. Add a new column with a NOT NULL constraint.
The interviewer also gave me a series of SQL questions, where I had to write queries for calculating the
highest salary in each department, dropping a column, and updating the salary column by adding a 10%
bonus.
For this round, a solid understanding of SQL constraints, keys, subqueries, window functions, and stored
procedures was essential. Additionally, clearly communicating your thought process helps the interviewer
understand how you approach problems. This can guide them to offer hints if you get stuck..Practice as
many sql questions to consolidate your understanding of these topics and their nitty-gritty.
3.[HR Interview](17 students were shortlisted for this round)
This round had two interviewers: an HR representative and the MD of ISS. This was the final round,
beginning with them asking for my introduction. We discussed my academic background, whether I plan to
pursue a Master's degree in the near future, and my reasoning for opting for a Minor in Management. Next, I
was asked to elaborate on one of the projects listed on my resume. They then inquired if I had read the job
description for the SQL Developer role and whether I was comfortable with the responsibilities. When asked
if I had experience working with databases, I referred to one of my projects where I used MySQL. This led
to an in-depth discussion about the database aspects of the project and whether its objectives were
--- PAGE 3 ---
business-oriented. Following that, there was a conversation about where I live, how I commute to college,
and whether I would be comfortable commuting to Nesco. Afterward, they asked if I had any questions. I
asked the MD about the governance solutions they provide to clients, and I asked the HR about what a
typical day would look like if I joined ISS Stoxx.
Around 10 PM the results were announced & 12 people were selected across all roles. However,I was not
selected.

4. 4th September 2024

Nearly a month after the process date, I received a message from the point of contact for the ISS Stoxx
process, that the company had asked whether I had been placed or not and was ready to extend the offer.
Later that night, I received a message confirming my selection.

8.0, and for Software Engineering in Test and Analytical Verification, it was further reduced to 7.5 and
above.
There were 3 rounds: Online Assessment, Technical Interview and HR Interview
1.
Online Assessment [Around 150 students appeared for the test]
It was a 90 minute assessment and was conducted on Google Forms. It consisted of 70 MCQ questions, and
there were four sections - Java(18 questions), Python (17 questions), SQL (5 questions) and aptitude (30
questions). The correct answer would give you 1 mark, -0.25 for incorrect answer and 0 for not attempting.
The Java section consisted a lot of finding the output of the code kind of questions. Make sure you have
OOP concepts clear, especially how they are implemented in Java. I recommend practicing from websites
such as GFG, Interviewbit, Javatpoint, etc. There were questions about streams, filters, multithreading,
concurrent hashmaps, anonymous functions, enums etc but if you were familiar with the basics, you could
guess the answers. However, it would be better to be sure so, if your main language is Java, look into all
those concepts and how they work.
Similarly, python questions were also of similar kind, make sure you know all the python specific concepts
such as slicing, mutable - immutable data types, shallow copy - deep copy, OOPs in python (they're
implemented differently than in java), list comprehension, which functions are in-place and which return a
new lists, etc.
SQL questions were about choosing the right query out of four options, so make sure you know SQL queries
and which can be used with which and not with others, what can give errors, etc.
Aptitude questions were mathematical, some were easy but tricky, while others involved solving. You were
allowed to use the desktop calculator but not the physical calculator, for some reason. Only attempt what
you are confident in this section and scroll through all the questions once because some are dead easy
--- PAGE 2 ---
compared to others. Don't worry if it doesn't go as well as others, if your technical score is good, you should
be fine.
You were allowed to switch sections, but make sure you use the next and back buttons on the form and not
the browser back button. Also, to be cautious, make sure to submit the test at least 5 minutes before the time
runs out as the answers won't be auto submitted.

2. Technical Interview [Approx. 50 students shortlisted]

The panels were formed based on the first role preference you were eligible for. My interviewer was
probably in a hurry, everyone in my panel completed their interview in about 15-20 min, while other panels
were going for about an hour for each student. The interview started with my introduction and not even two
lines in the introduction, when I mentioned backend development, he asked me what backend development
is and the questions began.
Explain the four pillars of OOP, what the final keyword in Java means (explain all 3 cases when used with a
variable, method, and class), can an abstract class be final, what is immutability, if there is a variable A =
"Dheeraj" and another B = "Dheeraj," how many objects are created (only 1, because of string pools in
Java), what will happen if A is set to "Muppineti" (another string is created, and now A points to it), what is
the difference between Left Join and Inner Join in SQL, and finally, he asked me to explain my most recent
project and my role in it.
I sensed the interviewer didn't want long answers, so I kept my responses short and concise, refraining from
giving examples, and it went quite smoothly. He didn't ask me if I had any questions for him, so I said thank
you and left.

Tips :-

• I got lucky and your case most likely would be different, so prepare a good introduction and only

mention things you know really well, as the next questions would probably be from those.

• Don't over explain things, keep concise answers with good examples.

• Know everything you mentioned in your resume really and make sure you can explain every word in

it.

• If you're not sure about something, it's okay just to tell the interviewer upfront so they can move on

to the next question.

• Be ready for some easy DSA questions and definitely be ready to write SQL queries. Do SQL really

well, especially joins and group by.

• Be calm, take your time and answer confidently.

3. HR Interview [17 students shortlisted]

I was the first person for this interview and there were two panelists. It was a short interview and it began
with a tricky question, what do you know about us? The context is, I didn't pay attention during the
Pre-Placement Talk, and these two were the ones who gave it, so I was supposed to know them. So, don't
make this stupid mistake - pay attention and take notes on everything. I just answered what I knew about the
--- PAGE 3 ---
ISS (which was not much, please do your research) and luckily they didn't make any notes for this. And
then the interview began.
They asked me about my family background, education, why I chose my degree and to explain any one of
my projects. Use the STAR method of answering, especially for the projects. They asked me if I was looking
for AIML in my job, and for such questions make sure you read the JD carefully and answer accordingly. I
said I am more interested in overall backend development. And to which they asked if I would be open to
work also in frontend. What I did remember from the PPT was that they wanted someone who was flexible
in terms of technology, so I said yes, even though it's not my strongest asset, I am open to it. They asked if I
had any plans for further studies (in most cases, you want to say no, as they are looking for loyal candidates
who will stick with the company, so prepare a good answer). They asked about the disparity between my
technical and aptitude scores. They asked where I lived, and whether there would be any travelling issues.
Finally, they asked me if I had any questions, so I asked about the team structure and how the projects were
assigned to the teams.
In the end, 12 students got the offer!

1) How was your test?

2) What is your primary language?

3) Why did you choose JAVA? [ Try to use few benefits of JAVA and then include what motivated you

to use JAVA (I said about how the 2nd sem course on OOPS with C++ motivated me)]

4) Why JAVA is called as Object Oriented Language? (4 pillars of OOPS)

5) Define all 4 pillar of OOPS

6) Use three classes Shape, Rectangle, Square to explain all those concepts (Write code on paper).

Many follow up questions were asked on this.
Few of them are:

• Initially i didn't mentioned whether my Shape class is abstract or Interface.

So they asked me when do you use Shape class in this scenario? Then i introduced interface
in my code.
Following with what is Abstract class and Interface in JAVA. Differences between them.
While giving answer I introduced Diamond problem in JAVA. ( Issue with Multiple
Inheritance in JAVA). Then they asked me can you define methods in abstract class and in
interface.

• Then one of the interviewer gave me 4 codes of creating an object of the class (Considering

shape is not an interface) then told me to tell how they would run or behave. While answering
one of the code i introduced super keyword. And there were follow ups on this as well.

7) Then they gave me a simple question to write a code to print 1 to n numbers without using for loop.

8) Then they move forward with SQL query. They just asked one sql query to me but i was expecting

more follow ups on the basis of tables they gave me.
Employee Table
Department Table
emp_id
name
salary
city
dept_id
dept_id name
Find the max salary on the basis of each city and the name of person getting that salary.

9) At last they asked me a well known puzzle: Puzzle Mislabeled Jars - GeeksforGeeks

10) Finally they asked me if I have any questions for them.

I asked them two questions:
Q1) I asked them that they had mentioned in their ppt that ESG's was introduced in 2021 in ISS, so

years? (My interviewer was working in ESG from last 3 years)
Q2) What if government releases a new policy that has to be implemented by the next day itself? As
clients would be expecting the changes by the next day. So what do ISS would do if they got into
--- PAGE 3 ---
some situation like this? [This was a random question I thought (I personally think it was not a good
question but luckily interviewers were appreciating the above questions)]

3. HR Round [ 17 students appeared for this round]

In the final round, there were two interviewers: the HR representative and the Director of ISS. The
interview lasted approximately 25 minutes.

1. They asked me about my day.

2. Then asked me about my Introduction including my family background, what i do in my free time

and where do I live?

3. Then told me to take one project which you like most or enjoyed most and give me a brief

introduction about it. [I mentioned my Major project as it was the one which i have been working on
for 4 months and gave them a brief introduction]

4. Then asked me about challenges faced in this project [I discussed how I was working on Texas

instruments microcontroller and how I was able to gather information from the documentation of diff
microcontrollers of the same family to sort the issues which i was facing]

5. As i had mentioned about playing/watching cricket as my hobby in my introduction, HR asked about

the recent series between India and Sri Lanka [ I told her that after T20 world cup 2024 I have not
watched any live match. I do know about this series but i am unaware of the results ]

6. She asked me if I had sat for any other companies that visited the campus?

7. Are you comfortable with travelling?

8. Then she told me that would you be open for the different role as well because they are hiring in

general and not for a specific role?

9. At last they asked Do you have any questions?

I asked few question:

• What would be the differences be between my collaboration with teams at ISS and the

collaboration which I did in one of my project discussed? Then I asked a follow up: Can you
elaborate more on global collaboration at ISS which you mentioned?

• After that I elaborated more that how i documented my Major project (as it was govt funded

project and would be active for more 2-3 years and the requirements from sponsors do
change. So we have documented it in a way that if anyone had to work on that project can
continue it easily with help of our documented work). So at ISS the documentation is
completed after the project or while working on that project like I did?
Finally 12 students got the offer!!!

For JAVA and Python, most of the questions were OOPs based. There were some theoretical questions on

Tips - Study and understand OOPs properly. Few easy-medium SQL questions on Leetcode will be more

than enough to select the correct answer for the SQL questions. Aptitude questions can be practiced on sites
like GFG.

2. Technical Interview [Approximately 50 students were selected for this round]

The interviews took place on the same day as the OA. I was the first person to be interviewed in my panel
out of four students. A lot of OOPs based questions were asked during this interview. I was asked to explain
polymorphism and its types, abstraction, if multiple inheritance is possible in JAVA, what is an interface, etc.
Also many sub-questions were asked based on my answers to these questions. Then I was asked to write the
pseudocode on paper for certain problems.
The questions were-
--- PAGE 2 ---

• Given a paragraph as a string, find the count of each word within the paragraph. [I gave a hashmap

based solution for this question where words can be separated each time a space, dot, comma, etc
occurs. I had to handle edge cases like when there are two consecutive spaces or how to save the
final word that does not encounter a space, full stop at the end, etc.]

• Given a list of objects of a class 'Student' that consisted of various attributes, I was asked to find the

students with marks higher than 90. If the list is sorted based on marks, how would I optimize my
solution. [First I gave the basic O(n) solution that checked the marks of each student object. If the list
is sorted, then it can be optimized using binary search]
Then, certain theoretical questions were asked on the concepts of CCN (Eg- How is a connection established
between client and server), DBMS (Eg-What is the order of execution of queries in SQL). I was asked
questions in detail about various HTTP methods and their use. No questions were asked about my projects.
The interview took around 45 minutes.

The HR interview was very short and consisted of two panelists. I was asked to introduce myself and then,
questions were asked on my family background, educational background, hobbies, etc. Interviewers asked
me why I opted for placements instead of pursuing higher studies. They asked me about a time in my life
when I was able to learn something new. Then they asked me where I lived and if I would be comfortable
with traveling to the office everyday. This round took only 15-20 minutes.
Finally, 12 students were selected by the company.

1. Start Practicing DSA: Focus on standard questions and fundamental concepts. You can use popular

resources like the Striver Sheet, NeetCode, and AlgoMap to guide your practice. Remember, it's
important not to spend all your time on DSA; balance your preparation with other areas too.

2. Balance Your Preparation: While DSA is crucial, don't get consumed by it. Focus on

understanding key concepts and solving standard problems, but also allocate time to strengthen your
skills in SQL and the tech stacks you've used in your projects. This will ensure you're well-rounded
in both theoretical and practical aspects.

3. Prepare for Aptitude and Core Subjects: Don't overlook the importance of aptitude tests and core

subjects such as DBMS, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, and Python. These are often tested
in the initial rounds, and strong performance can set you apart carly in the process.

Process had 4 rounds (OA + 3 Interview Rounds (2 Tech + 1 HR))
1.
Online Assessment [ 156 students appeared]
The online assessment consisted of 73 questions with a total duration of 90 minutes, conducted on Unstop.
The assessment was divided into three sections, each allocated 30 minutes:

1. Aptitude Section: 40 questions covering Basic Maths, Logical Reasoning, and Probability.

2. Core Subjects Section: 30 questions focused on subjects like DBMS, Python, Computer Networks,

and Operating Systems.

3. Coding Section: 3 coding questions:

o (a) A String subsequence problem. Link
o (b) A sliding window problem (medium-level LeetCode question).

• (c) A Graph traversal problem. (level Order)

I managed to fully solve the String subsequence question and partially solve the Graph traversal question,
where only three test cases were not passing. Due to the limited time, I couldn't attempt the sliding window
question.
Key Takeaway: Time management is crucial in this round. Try to attempt as many MCQS as possible, and
for the coding section, focus on completely solving 1-2 questions to maximize your score.

2. Tech Interview-1 [ 40 students shortlisted]

In this round, the interviewer first asked me to introduce myself and then discuss one of the projects from
my resume. Following this, I was asked to write an SQL query to find the 10th highest salary of an
employee. I was also given another SQL query involving group by and a subquery, and I was asked to
predict its output. As I have used pandas in one of my projects he asked me the basic syntax question to
define a dataframe and save as a csv file.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Next, the interviewer asked for the easiest way to swap two variables in Python. We then moved on to a
discussion about various cloud platforms, where I mentioned that I have basic knowledge of AWS and plan
to learn more in my current semester, as I have chosen Cloud Computing as one of my electives. The
interviewer also asked about SaaS and laaS, which I wasn't familiar with, so I explained that I haven't
studied them yet but am eager to learn.
The discussion then shifted back to SQL, focusing on advanced concepts such as dimension tables, fact
tables, and factless tables. I was able to explain only the basics, as I wasn't deeply familiar with these topics.
The interviewer was very friendly and took the time to explain the concepts I didn't fully understand.
Towards the end of the interview, I was asked about my hobbies. I also asked the interviewer two questions
before the interview concluded.
Tip: Take your time to fully understand the questions before answering. If you don't know the answer to a
question, honestly admit it and express your willingness to learn.

3. Tech Interview 2 [ 18 students shortlisted(12 for FE role + 6 for ML role) ]

This round was focused on my resume. The interviewer started by asking me to introduce myself and then
requested that I explain the K-means algorithm, which I had used in one of my projects. I provided an
explanation using a numerical example. Following this, I was asked about my MERN stack project.
The interviewer then asked me to write a Node.js code snippet to fetch data from an API. Afterward, we
discussed JWT and cookies, including how I implemented them in my project. I was also asked to explain
the difference between encryption and hashing.
Next, the interviewer asked about Socket.io and WebSockets, which I had used in my project, and asked me
to write code to enable socket communication between two users. We then discussed the chat schema I used
in the project.
Finally, I was given a simple DSA question to reverse a string without using any extra space. I wrote the
code on paper using the two-pointer swap technique and thoroughly explained my approach. The interview
concluded after I asked the interviewer a question.

3. HR Round | 6 students shortlisted (4 for FE role + 2 ML role) ]

At the start of the round, the interviewer introduced himself and explained that this wasn't a formal
interview but rather a discussion. He then gave a brief overview of Quantiphi. After that, he asked me to
introduce myself, focusing on my interests, hobbies, family background, and aspirations to join Quantiphi,
while excluding any technical skills and project details.
The interviewer then proceeded with some basic HR questions, such as:

• Why are you interested in this role?

What motivates you?

• Do you want to pursue higher studies?

--- PAGE 3 ---
It was a casual discussion overall.
Tip: Be very transparent about who you are. Don't hesitate or fabricate answers. Be curious and answer with
confidence.
Total 5 students were selected and I was one of them for the FE (Data Engineer) Role.
Backstory:
The placement process can be quite hectic, so it's essential to be well-prepared. Starting in July, I began
applying to every company that I could. Overall, I completed 12 online assessments and went through 5 tech
interviews and 2 HR interviews. After facing consecutive rejections, I started feeling a bit demotivated.
However, each interview taught me valuable lessons and helped me improve for the next one, building my
confidence and sharpening my skills.
Then, I had an opportunity to apply for a Consultant role at Oracle, which is a mixture of tech+nontech,
whereas I was more interested in core tech roles. However, I felt I had no choice but to go for it. After
clearing Oracle's online assessment, I found out that the interview would be scheduled a week later for
oracle. Just before the interview day, I had another online assessment for Quantiphi. I took the assessment
and cleared it. The next day, I had two interviews scheduled one for Oracle and one for Quantiphi.
The Quantiphi interview was scheduled first on that day. Since I had been preparing for Oracle all week, I
didn't expect to clear the Quantiphi interview. But fate had other plans. I managed to clear all the interview
rounds for Quantiphi and, as a result, didn't need to attend the Oracle interview. This was fortunate since I
was more interested in the tech role at Quantiphi.

journey.prep:
• Read their requirements and thoroughly prepare your resume to fulfil their requirements as it is an

ATS based selection process.

• Remember to always ask at least 3 questions after the interview is close to a conclusion; this would

let the interviewers know your interest in the process as well as in the company.

• Read gfg logical reasoning problems to prep better for OA as well as interviews.

• Know as much as possible about the company from their website or via the ppt

• Finally remain calm do not get baffled if you answered a question incorrectly just moveon to the

next, remember the interviewers knows only as much as you know.

• Answer as honestly as possible. Consider these rounds more of a behavioral test wherein your every

single gesture is being monitored and evaluated upon. Try not to be nervous or anxious

• Have in depth knowledge of your projects and all the skills that you have mentioned in your resume.

Learn the topic well before mentioning it on your resume.

for the application. Out of which only 40 people were selected after the resume shortlisting round. A day
later this was followed by an online quiz that was heavily based on logical reasoning as well as probability
and numerical questions along with code snippets and MCQ. After this round around 14 people were
selected to the interviews.

algorithms particularly in python. I was asked questions based on arrays, tuples and concepts of oops like
encapsulation and multiple level inheritance. Then I was asked to write down code on a sheet of paper, the
question was to write a function to calculate the factorial of the given number. The interviewer was
particularly interested in how I would be dealing with any possible errors thrown by the system(try and
catch). Later i was asked about one of my projects followed by a detailed guesstimate round, i would
recommend to memorize the guesstimate sheet given below:
https://180dcsrcc.in/guesstimate-cheat-sheet-2023/
Later on i was asked some questions on basic calculation of probabilities and basic maths. At the end of the
interview they asked me if i had any questions, i asked them 3 questions primarily about work culture and
job position. The interview lasted for about 30-45 mins
2.
Lech/Business Round] [4 candidates appeared for this round]

thoroughly asked about my AIML project and research paper which I was able to explain in depth. I was
asked about image processing and CNN used in my projects along with its model design. Then the topic
shifted to my research paper and my possible motivations for writing the same. I was able to convince
him that it was not a product of my plans for higher studies. Then the topic shifted entirely to ML
wherein I was asked to explain a detailed workflow of how I would approach an AIML problem given
10 parameters. The follow ups were very thorough as the interviewer dealt with AIML on a daily
basis. We talked about how I would clean data using plots and contours along with suitable regression
models for contiguous and non-contiguous data. Next I was asked about how I would optimize a model
now after making it .We dealt in the concepts of mean error and adjusted mean error along with
examples and formulas for calculation of the same. Furthermore I was asked about my knowledge in
automation using VBA which I didn't know about so I explained how I would approach the problem
using Selenium and Pandas. Later I was asked about my ability to maneuver through a new problem
without any external help or support like stackoverflow or chatgpt, i was able to walk him through the
process ( after these questions I asked him 3-5 questions about his role in JPMC along with possible use
of AIML Furthermore I asked about my role in the company) . He was satisfied with my answers after
which I proceeded to the next round.
An in-depth knowledge of AIML and automation would be required at this stage. The interview lasted for
about 45 mins and after 25 mins I was selected for the HR round.

3. [HR Round] [2 appeared for this round]

The HR interview was conducted by 2 female panelists. Both made me comfortable and I was asked
general questions about myself, my family and my interest in the fintech industry. I was asked about the
role and if I understood what it entails. I was asked why JPMC, which I was able to answer based on
their company values and ideas. I was asked questions on my resume as well as I was given a scenario
wherein I had to resolve a conflict. The questions were basic although read through their ppt and
company values on their website. After this I asked 3-5 questions about the work balance, values and
about the role as well as my designation.
2 candidates were selected after this role.

what JP in JP Morgan is and what is the history of JP Morgan Chase & co."
Know the company its work policies, lines of business and history. The rest interview

different types of risks", and "Can you elaborate on Credit Risk and Market Risk". The
one question which was asked in all interview rounds (at least to me) was "Why risk
management and finance, Why not core/tech". Also, Read the Job Description (JD)
before the interviews, I was asked questions based on JD. Also, they ask you which role
you prefer and why. (we had Projects & solutions and middle office & reporting as two
different roles.)

Useful Tips:

1) You are the one who decides the flow of the interview. So answer what you know

and be ready for cross-questions. Do not say anything that you have absolutely no
idea about. In fact do not mention anything in your resume that you can't explain.

2) CONFIDENCE IS THE KEY. BE CALM.Be clear while you speak and Be precise. Do not

talk a lot, if they want you to elaborate about something they will let you know.

3) Have real-world examples prepared, especially regarding risk types and risk

management failures. For instance, be familiar with the Lehman Brothers collapse,
its role in the 2008 financial crisis, and the associated risk type.

an excellent reputation or the company culture aligns with me." Instead, provide a
specific example, such as how the firm navigated the 2008 crisis, and then elaborate
on your reasons.

aware of all major financial n risk-related news.

Process Date: 10th July -2024

Rounds involved in the Process:

1) Resume Screening

2) Aptitude Test

3) Group Discussion

4) Interview Round-1

6) HR Round

Resume Screening

• Make a standard single column resume

• Highlight the Key points: So that the interviewer will notice them

After the resume screening round, 97 students were shortlisted

Aptitude Test

• 10 Questions on Finance and Accounting

• 10 Questions on Market Awareness

• 15 Questions on Aptitude

• 10 Questions on VARC (Verbal Ability and Reading Comprehension)

Finance and accounting Section has Questions related to various financial ratios
and financial statements
Market Awareness questions were related to current affairs ie both financial and non-
financial topics.
Aptitude: Questions were from the topics: Time and work, PNC, Simple/compound interest
ratios and proportions etc.
VARC: Questions were asked based on a given Comprehension, Fill in the blank's questions
and sentence error correction questions

I would recommend practicing a lot of aptitude questions beforehand and focus on time
management while attempting the questions. Think beforehand about which section will you
attempt first and allocate time accordingly.

Group Discussion
Following the aptitude test, 73 students were Shortlisted for the GD. The topic for the GD
was announced beforehand it was "India-the 5th largest economy". As you know the topic
beforehand prepare thoroughly and write good points. Make sure to include statistical
metrices related to the topic.
Groups of 12 were made and we discussed for about 20 min make sure to make 2-3 entries
and also listen to what others are saying. If possible, add on to their points as well

Interview Rounds 1 and 2
Around 31 students were shortlisted after the GD. Following are the questions which were
asked to me (not exhaustive):

1) Explanation of the three financial statements and how are they related

2) About recent M&A's and their deal structure

3) Nifty and Sensex closing and how the value of Sensex is calculated

4) About brent crude oil price, INR To dollar exchange rate, 10 gm 24 karat gold price

5) About WACC and how it is calculated whether cost of equity will be more or cost of

debt and why?

6) About enterprise value and how it is calculated they will give some numbers and ask

you to calculate the enterprise value

7) As I had mentioned about Beta in one of my projects. I was asked what is beta how it

is calculated and they gave me two companies and asked me about beta w.r.t those
companies

8) Again, they asked me to write the three financial statements line items. Then they told

that if we increase the depreciation by x amount as compared to previous year and
assume a suitable tax rate, what will be the affect on the three financial statements.

9) About minority interest

10)  About what is cash conversion cycle?

11) Many puzzles and mental ability questions were also asked

While solving the puzzles even if you don't get the right answer do not worry just tell
them about your approach and thought process. They will try to confuse you many times
but if you are confident about your answer stick to it.
Prepare the standard questions like introduce yourself, why finance etc.

HR Round
The round began with my introduction. Seeing one of my courses the interviewer asked
me what do you understand by the term "Portfolio Management". Then I was asked to tell
a scenario in which I optimized the result of a project using a better dataset something on
these lines actually I forgot the exact question. Then the interviewer explained a bit about
the JPMC work culture and asked me of my understanding of the role and what I expect
my day-to-day work would be?  Then I was also asked that why I was not going for an
MBA. Then I was asked a bit about my family background.

At the end 11 students were selected for the Banking role

• At the end of each round the interviewers will ask you that do you have any

questions for them. Make sure to ask good questions regarding the role.

a lot

• See regarding the various valuation models

• Also have an understanding of the recent M&A's IPO's and how the IPO process

works

• Have an understanding of the mental ability questions like calculating square roots

of decimal numbers, percentage of certain number (for this remember certain
standard fraction values like 1/8,1/6,1/4 etc.)

• Also have an understanding of RBI related terms like SLR CRR repo rate reverse

repo rate base rate

• About difference between Fiscal and monetary policies

• Read Mint, Economic times regularly

Accounting & Corporate Finance section had questions related to bonds, ratios etc.

3. Group Discussion [72 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

This was an offline round scheduled on 10th July. The topic for the Group Discussion was given a day
prior. Our theme was "India - the fifth largest economy". It was a very broad topic so it was difficult to
understand what kind of sub-topic would be asked. Try to research properly and make sure you have
covered all the important points. Students were divided into 6 panels. The moderator was changing the
topic in every 10 mins. Try to make at least 2-3 entries, but also make sure you add real value to the
conversation and don't repeat any points. Try to remember the major talking points and think of a
general outcome for a conclusion in case the moderator asks you in the end.

4. Interview Round 1[36 students were shortlisted for this round]

The interviews started at 11:30 am. The interview started with an introduction and as I had mentioned an
IB course that I had undertaken, they enquired about my learnings from the course. They asked me about
the Case Study Competition that I had won, I wasn't able to recollect every fine detail, so make sure to
revise everything that is mentioned in your resume in detail. Then the other panelist asked me a series of
questions on accounting fundamentals. As I knew that I didn't have in-depth knowledge in the field of
accounting, I made sure to answer all the questions to the best of my abilities and also tried to let them
know that I am much more proficient in Investment Banking concepts. Thus, they asked me a lot of
questions related to IB and to test my knowledge of the field. They also asked me questions on Index,
Inflation, Repo Rates, and yesterday's market closing price. They also asked me if I knew what valuation
is to which I answered yes and then they asked me to explain the DCF Model, WACC, and Terminal
Value. Thereafter they asked me a few puzzles and the interview ended with me posing a question to the
panelists.

5. Interview Round 2

The round was scheduled after only about 5 minutes from the completion of my Interview Round 1. Like
the previous Interview, it started with my Introduction. Coincidentally he asked me a lot of the same
questions from the last interview. Concepts like Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Cash Flow Statement,
Index, Inflation etc were asked. He then enquired about the latest current affairs in the field of Finance
that I was aware of. There wasn't any major news at that time, but I recalled reading that Nifty had
recently crossed a historical benchmark and so I mentioned that. He then asked me if I invest in Stocks
or do I follow the stock market to which I replied No, but he still asked me to name the top 5 biggest
stocks in India by market cap. He also wanted me to list the top 5 economies by GDP barring India. He
then asked me the reason behind the growth of India's markets, why Investments in India had increased,
and also asked about India's and USA's Inflation rates. He then asked me a puzzle to which I gave the
correct approach but he wanted me to give him the definite answer by doing the maths behind it. The
interview ended with me asking a question to the interviewer.
--- PAGE 3 ---

6. HR Round

It was a very chill round and lasted for not more than 5 minutes. The interviewer asked me to introduce
myself and then asked me what I think my job would entail if selected. Then she enquired about where I
stay and also asked about my further education plans to which I said no, but I mentioned that I had plans
to obtain the CFA certificate. Finally, she asked if I had any questions for her.
