Each round is an elimination round

1. Resume Screening

2. Aptitude Test(Online)

3. Group Discussion (Group size 12)

4. Interview Round 1

5. Interview Round 2

6. HR Round

1. Resume Screening:

General tips with regards to resume:

• Make single column resume using Latex (might as well use other one but this is the standard one)

• Do add your photo when it comes to submitting resume to JPMC

• Make sure you have some keywords related to finance in your resume.

97 students were shortlisted for the aptitude test.

2. Online Assesment:

45 Questions (No negative marking) - 45 minutes

1. Section 1 - Corporate finance and Financial Accounting (10 questions)

2. Section 2 - Market Awareness (10 questions)

3. Section 3 - Quantitative Aptitude (15 questions)

4. Section 4 - English Usage (10 Questions)

72 students were shortlisted after the round. Shortlist given a day prior to the interview process.
Preparation: https://www.indiabix.com/

3. Group Discussion:

Topic: India - The 5th Largest Economy
Divided into groups of 12 candidates each. The GD topic was given a day prior with the shortlisted
candidates, but the groups were allotted just before the interview started.
The given topic is just the theme for the GD. During the GD they gave topics one by one and asked to
discuss the same. The discussion started with what is GDP. Then the topic shifted to what factors have
worked for the uplifting of our economy. Then there was discussion around what are the challenges India
faces going ahead or what could go wrong. Lastly the topic shifted to the GDPs of other countries.

Tips:

• Have adequate and impactful points related to the topic.

• Try to bring in new points that would create an impact on the discussion.

• Having some numbers or examples to support your views would be a plus (but not too many).  You

should reason on the numbers and examples.

• Do memorize the points as your panelists may or may not allow you to carry any material for the

GD.

• Panelists were quite chill and made sure everyone got a chance to express their views.

4. Interview 1:

Duration: 1 hr approx. (much shorter for others)
The interview began with how was your day did you have your lunch etc to calm you down. Then the
questions started with "do you invest in the markets?". Name a stock you invested in, how you identify
where to invest. Here I mentioned some financial ratios so was asked about the same. Also mentioned
about revenue and profit growth yoy so I was asked what would be considered as a good profit or sales
growth in percentage. Then there were questions related to financial statements. If a pen is
manufactured and it is sitting in the inventory, how will it affect cost of goods sold  and how would
depreciation affect EBITDA.  Then I was asked about the nifty and sensex price just before the
interview and then what is nifty and sensex . Do check this before going in for the interview. Then I
was asked about recent IPOs. I mentioned about an IPO in which JP MC itself is a book-runner. He
then asked me for a second IPO and I mentioned the to be biggest IPO that is Hyundai (JPMC was
book-runner in this too). He then asked me about the valuation, amount they are raising and also why.
I was then given 2 guesstimates and one question related to calculating average speed. I was asked
about any masters plans or any certifications plans like CFA or CAT etc.  Then I was given a set of 3
companies: a mature manufacturing company, a tech startup which is not yet profitable and another
mature company and was given a set of 4 financial ratios and told to match them as to what would be
the best ratio to analyze which company. I was able to match 2 companies but gave wrong answer for
this third one. Then what beta is and sectors having beta less than and greater than 1. I was able to say
for greater than 1 but wasn't able to answer for less than 1 (answer was FMCG sector).

5. Interview 2:

Duration: 25-30 mins
Just in 5 mins time of my first interview I was called for a second interview. This one was pretty chill
and started with the same as the previous question which is do you invest and how do you analy ze
companies to invest and tell some other company you would recommend  to invest in and why. Then
the financial ratios for analyzing the company. I was asked about the valuation methods. Then what I
understand of the job role and about the tasks to be done in the role. After that questions around
WACC, what it is, why and where is it used . Then a question about the paper I had presented and
mentioned in my resume. Lastly about any plans for CAT or CFA or masters.

6. HR Round:

Duration: 15-20 mins
Do carry a special resume prepared for JP. This did help me in the HR round. The HR noticed that I
had made a separate resume and looked happy with that. Started with an introduction, then about the
job role and what I understood of it. I had mentioned about the forage investment banking simulation
in my resume on which I was asked how was the experience and did I do it gradually or in one go.
Ended with asking about where I was based out of.

1. Resources

> CFI courses - Accounting Fundamentals, Corporate Finance, Financial Analysis

• YouTube - DCF valuation, How are 3 financial statements linked, 2008 financial crisis, SVB

bank collapse, what is SENSEX AND NIFTY, how is GDP calculated, Adani-Hindenburg
saga, etc.
> Puzzles - GFG puzzles
> IPOs and Mergers and Acquisitions - You Tube, Moneycontrol, Economic Times, etc.

• Guesstimates - YouTube playlist

• Aptitude - YouTube playlist, Indiabix

> Basics of stock market - YouTube: Akshat Srivastava, CA Rachana Ranade, etc.
--- PAGE 4 ---

2. Being from an engineering background, we do not have in-depth financial knowledge. It is thus

important to prepare sincerely for this role. I would recommend CFI finance courses as they are free
and are very credible.

3. Please do not start your preparation at the last moment. I was preparing for both tech and non tech

profiles and hence had a lot of stress managing DSA, development, finance, EXTC subjects, etc. Do
not repeat my mistake. Ideally, I would say prepare for only one profile in depth and if you want to
try both then have a sufficient time window with you.

4. Start reading about current affairs, global markets, recent IPOs, and mergers and acquisitions every

day at least a month prior to the placement start date. This won't take much time, 30 min everyday
while having dinner is enough.

5. During interviews, always maintain proper posture, have a smile on your face, do not panic even if

you are not able to answer and at least let the interviewer know what approach you're thinking about.

6. Participate in non-tech competitions. This would help you learn more about a topic than doing a

course. In my case, we participated in a M&A competition without any knowledge, but we learnt and
researched for 15-20 days and won the competition.

7. The entire placement cycle is very hectic and stressful but it is important to stay in the present and

study without worrying about external factors like market situation, recession, etc. Believe me, it
never goes to waste. If you have prepared honestly, you will get opportunities.

8. If you have any doubts, I'll be more than happy to help. You can reach out to me directly on

WhatsApp or Linkedin.
All the best!

- Resume shortlisting

- Online Assessment - 6th July, 2024

Remaining rounds all happened on 10th July:

- Group Discussion

- Interview Round 1

1. Resume shortlisting

> JPMC evaluated all resumes and sent the shortlist to the TPO.
> Use LaTeX to draft your resume and check the resume score on Resume Worded. In my opinion, a
score above 65-70 is good enough.
> Do not exaggerate things, keep it simple. Be sure that you know and understand everything
mentioned in your resume.
> Personally, I only mentioned non-tech projects and courses in my resume. If you have a tech project
that is finance-related, you can include that too.
(97 candidates were shortlisted for the Online Assessment)

2. Online Assessment (97 candidates)

> This was a 45-minute test with 45 questions to attempt without negative marking.
> There were four sections: Corporate Finance (10 questions), Market Awareness (10 questions),
Quantitative Aptitude (15 questions), and Verbal Reasoning (10 questions).

• The Verbal Reasoning section was easy, Quantitative Aptitude was moderate and lengthy, and

Market Awareness and Corporate Finance were moderate.
(72 candidates were shortlisted for Group Discussion)
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Group Discussion (72 candidates)

> One day before the GD, we were given the topic "India - Sth largest economy". It was a broad theme
with many points that could have been included.

• We were divided into groups of 12, and the discussion lasted about 20-25 minutes. There were two

interviewers present who constantly evaluated and guided the discussion in the right direction. They
also assisted those who did not get a chance to speak.
> Try to include numbers and examples in your points as it helps establish credibility and demonstrates
analytical skills and a statistics-based approach.

• Listen to what other people are saying and follow general etiquette.

• Remember, evaluation is based not only on your content but also on how you conduct yourself.

(31 candidates were shortlisted for interview round 1)

4. Interview round 1 (31 candidates)

> These 31 candidates were divided into six panels, each with one interviewer.

• I was asked to introduce myself and discuss things mentioned in my resume. The interviewer took

the resume, so be sure you know everything mentioned. He asked me about my Minor degree course
in Management from SPJIMR and the topics covered in it.

• He then asked if I knew financial accounting and the three financial statements. How are they linked

together? If we increase the depreciation cost by 'x' and the tax rate is 'y', how would it affect the
income statement and cash flow statement? I answered the question after providing an example and
solving it on paper. He tried to question my answers each time, but it's important to back your
knowledge and intuition in such scenarios.

• I did a DCF valuation project, so he asked about valuation methods and the steps in DCF valuation.

He asked for the formulas for calculating Terminal Value and Enterprise Value.

• We then moved to quick math questions like 97 × 103, 49 × 51, square root of 0.01, etc., and

obviously, using pen and paper was not allowed. These questions can be solved using basic math
formulas like a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b).
> He then asked me two puzzles. First, he asked me to calculate the total number of squares on a
chessboard (1x1 squares + 2x2 squares + ... 8x8 squares), and using pen and paper was not allowed.
The second one was about water in a lake doubling every day and the lake being full on the 8th day;
when was the lake 25% filled? Practicing GFG puzzles would be more than enough. It would help in
other interviews as well.

• He then asked about SENSEX and NIFTY and how their values are calculated. He also asked about

the current values of Gold, Crude Oil, SENSEX, and NIFTY, so be sure to check the closing values
from the previous day.
> Finally, he asked if I had any questions for him. Be sure you have 2-3 questions ready for different
rounds.
> Even if you are stuck on a question, be sure to talk about the approach you are trying. Do not pause
for an extended period. If you don't know the answer to a question, try for some time, and ask for
hints if you still do not get it. At the very least, show that you are genuinely trying.
> The interview lasted for about 40-45 min.
(Interviews were conducted simultaneously, so we lost track of how many advanced to round 2)
--- PAGE 3 ---

4. Interview round 2

• As soon as I finished my first interview round, I was called for the second round without even a

minute's break.
> This was a relatively relaxed round and lasted only about 15 minutes.
> The interviewer asked me to introduce myself and walk him through my resume.
> He asked about the selection process for the Minor in Management from SPJIMR.
> We had won a couple of national-level competitions in finance and consulting, so he asked about that
experience. The finance one was related to merger and acquisition, so he asked about the process of
an M&A deal.
> I was also asked about my internship as a React Developer and the reason behind shifting from
software development and electronics to the finance domain. This is a very standard question that
will definitely be asked. I explained how participating in non-tech competitions helped me make this
decision.
> In the end, he asked if I had any questions for him. Again, keep 2 questions ready for each round.
(15-16 candidates were shortlisted for HR round)

5. HR round (15-16 candidates)

> This round was more like a casual conversation and was pretty chill.

• I was asked standard HR questions: Introduce yourself, walk me through your resume, future plans

regarding higher studies, family background, and what do you understand about this role, etc.

• The interviewer then asked if there had ever been a scenario where someone was immoral or

dishonest and how I approached the situation. This question is to test your ethics. If you have not
faced such a situation, do not lie, and instead explain what you would do if it ever happened.
> In the end, I asked the interviewer a few questions about how different teams collaborated on
projects, job location, etc.
> Although I was not asked, remember the core values of JPMC.
> This round lasted about 15 minutes.
Finally, 11 candidates were selected for the internship.

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
1. Resources

> CFI courses - Accounting Fundamentals, Corporate Finance, Financial Analysis

• YouTube - DCF valuation, How are 3 financial statements linked, 2008 financial crisis, SVB

bank collapse, what is SENSEX AND NIFTY, how is GDP calculated, Adani-Hindenburg
saga, etc.
> Puzzles - GFG puzzles
> IPOs and Mergers and Acquisitions - You Tube, Moneycontrol, Economic Times, etc.

• Guesstimates - YouTube playlist

• Aptitude - YouTube playlist, Indiabix

> Basics of stock market - YouTube: Akshat Srivastava, CA Rachana Ranade, etc.
--- PAGE 4 ---

2. Being from an engineering background, we do not have in-depth financial knowledge. It is thus

important to prepare sincerely for this role. I would recommend CFI finance courses as they are free
and are very credible.

3. Please do not start your preparation at the last moment. I was preparing for both tech and non tech

profiles and hence had a lot of stress managing DSA, development, finance, EXTC subjects, etc. Do
not repeat my mistake. Ideally, I would say prepare for only one profile in depth and if you want to
try both then have a sufficient time window with you.

4. Start reading about current affairs, global markets, recent IPOs, and mergers and acquisitions every

day at least a month prior to the placement start date. This won't take much time, 30 min everyday
while having dinner is enough.

5. During interviews, always maintain proper posture, have a smile on your face, do not panic even if

you are not able to answer and at least let the interviewer know what approach you're thinking about.

6. Participate in non-tech competitions. This would help you learn more about a topic than doing a

course. In my case, we participated in a M&A competition without any knowledge, but we learnt and
researched for 15-20 days and won the competition.

7. The entire placement cycle is very hectic and stressful but it is important to stay in the present and

study without worrying about external factors like market situation, recession, etc. Believe me, it
never goes to waste. If you have prepared honestly, you will get opportunities.

8. If you have any doubts, I'll be more than happy to help. You can reach out to me directly on

WhatsApp or Linkedin.
All the best!

The pre-placement talk was scheduled online on 2nd July. Try to ask questions and give answers if you can.

1. Resume Screening: Deadline 4th July

2. Online Aptitude Test : 6th July

3. Group Discussion

4. Interview round 1

5. Interview round 2

6. HR round

Rounds 3-6 were scheduled on 10th July.

1. Resume Screening

We had to submit all details and resume via the JPMC portal. You are also allowed to attach a cover letter,
although not mandatory, try to submit one.

• Use latex template and add only things you are confident about. Keep it single column, one page.

• You can take a slightly modified resume on campus which may contain 2 columns, you will need

around 5 to 6 copies as your panel may have more than one interviewer.
97 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Online Aptitude Test

The test window was 11-11:30 am and the duration was 45 mins. It had 4 sections, with no negative marking
and navigation was allowed.

• Basics of Finance and Accounting : 10 questions

• Market awareness: 10 questions. Questions were not necessarily finance based but general current

affairs.

• Quantitative Aptitude : 15 questions.

--- PAGE 2 ---
Questions based on Profit and Loss, Workers and Time, AP GP, Probability, etc. (Normal Aptitude
questions)

• Verbal Skills: 10 questions.

Passage based, rearranging, standard questions.
The test was lengthy so try to attempt things you know and equal parts from all sections rather than acing
one section.
72 students were shortlisted. The result was announced only a day before the interview so be prepared.

3. Group Discussion [ 72 selected students were divided into 6 panels of 12 each. We had Around 30

mins]

• The topic was revealed on 9th July, a day before the process, and it was 'India the 5th Largest

Economy'

• We were allowed to take notes with us for reference.

• We had 2 panelists. They told us to start with an introduction of the topic and the general idea we had

about GDP and the growth over years.

• After 7-8 points were discussed, they started introducing subtopics like which states were

contributing more, which were lacking behind, how the global scenario and decline in the China
market was affecting our economy. Lastly they asked us what could go wrong and prevent the
economy from rising. They asked me to conclude.

• Make sure you have at least 3-4 entries. The duration you talk for is not imp as long as you have

good points. Try using numbers to elevate your points. They were taking names and making sure we
all had chances to speak.
The better you perform in GD, the earlier your interview will be scheduled. I was the last person called for
round 1, so don't give up hope as it will be a lengthy process.
31 students were shortlisted for round 1
9 more were waitlisted but were not given a chance to give the interview.

4. Interview Round 1 [ My round lasted for about 25-30 mins]

There were 5 panels. My interview being scheduled last happened after lunch. I had only 1 panelist but some
people had 2 panelists.
I was first told to introduce myself, keep these basic answers ready as I was asked this in each round. He
started by asking me what I thought my role would be. Then he asked about stock markets so I told him
about Sensex and Nifty. Do see the previous day's closing for both. He asked me if I invested and then about
which sectors I would invest in. Then he asked about RBI and its policies, inflation and the name of RBI
governor. If you don't know something do not guess, just say you haven't read about it. Then he moved on to
financial statements. He gave me scenarios and I had to create the balance sheet and income statement, cases
like buying inventory, selling for revenue, all basics. He asked me about Enterprise value and market
capitalization. Then he moved on to puzzles. He asked a sum on avg speed, puzzle on probability (10 teams
against each other, find no of matches) and a puzzle on work and time.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Only a few students weren't taken for round 2, all others were given a second chance.

5. Interview Round 2 [ This round was for 15-20 mins]

There were 3 panels. I was called for the second round immediately after the first round so do not assume
you will get time to prepare between rounds.
I had two panelists. They asked me to introduce, and a few things from my resume. Then they told me to
explain financial statements and how they were interlinked. Then they gave a case with profit and tax which
was a little tricky. In between they asked about line items on IS, cash flow types and working capital. I could
not solve it completely but I explained the approach at every step and they were satisfied. Then they asked
about enterprise value and if it could be negative giving scenarios. They also asked about valuation methods
and told me to explain the multiple based approach. Then they moved on to the overall Indian market
scenario and just needed a generalized overview.
Around 16-18 people were selected for the HR round.

6. HR Round [ Around 10 mins ]

This was the easiest round. She asked me to introduce myself and to tell about my family. Then she asked
me why I was opting for a finance role and if I wanted to go for higher studies or any certifications in the
future. She also asked me what my plan was if I didn't get selected. Always say that you still want to do
something in finance and show you are passionate about it. Do not say you have higher studies plans even if
you do. Praise the company as much as you can and show how eager you are to join. She asked me if I had
any questions so I asked her about the growth opportunities and how to work for them. I think that
impressed her because then she asked me another question regarding any unethical scenarios I had come
across and how I dealt with them, which I could answer from committee experiences.
My HR round was also towards the very end so you never know who they will select.
The process on the 10th started around 9 and we got the results by 5:

30. 11 students were selected for the Banking role.

●  The  CGPA  criteria  may  or  may  not  be  mentioned  but  understanding  that  having  a  good  pointer  above

8 always helps. If you don't have one, try. But don't lose heart.

●  Prepare a lot for the GD, don't take it lightly ( Some others were much more prepared than me)

●  Focus on profile building from the get go.

●  Participate  in  case  studies  when  you  get  time,  and  good  ones.  So  that  you  end  up  learning  things  in

enough time)

model with a common size statement, dcf model and ratio analysis in it)

●  Be  clear  in  your  finance  basics.  They  don't  expect  you  to  be  perfect  at  finance,  but  the  basics  are  a

necessity.

●  Be polite and well mannered at all times, it creates an impression.

●  Dress  well.  Light  shirt  (preferably  white),  dark  trousers.  If  you  have  a  suit  or  a  tie,  wear  it.  It  isn't

over-dressed.

●  Part time internships are a thing, so if you can handle one of them then why not try.

●  Interact with other people aiming for the same company, you'll grow together with them.

●  Don't get too over-confident ever about your selection, just keep working and praying.

●  Read  newspapers  and  follow  the  news  regularly!  Not  just  10  days  before  the  interview,  but  for  the

months to come.

●  Feel free to reach out to me in case of further queries.

*ALL THE VERY BEST*
journey.howSecured:
1. Pre - Placement Talk: 2nd July

2.  Resume Screening: 4th July

3.  Online Aptitude Test: 6th July

Further Rounds took place offline on the 10th of July -

4.  Group Discussion

5.  Interview Round 1

6.  Interview Round 2

7.  HR Round

1.  Pre - Placement Talk

This  seemingly  unnecessary  round  is  actually  very  important.  This  is  the  first  impression  the  candidates  get
to  make  on  their  recruiters  so  make  the  most  of  it.  In  our  case  they  wanted  to  keep  the  talk  interactive  so
kept  asking  us  questions,  in  which  case  as  aspiring  employees  you  ought  to  try  and  interact  with  them.  But
try not to repeat points made by anyone else before you as it might not leave as good an impression.
Also,  keep  all  your  doubts  tailored  to  the  role  and  ask  good  questions.  One  more  thing,  in  case  they  do  not
ask  you  any  questions  or  don't  try  to  keep  it  interactive,  it  might  be  best  to  save  the  questions  towards  the
end as they might actually go for a common Q&A session.
The  pre-placement  talk  is  being  mentioned  as  the  first  round  as  it  is  a  very  crucial  opportunity  to  get  noticed
by the hiring managers so make the impression you would want them to remember you by.
Key points summarized -

●  Follow the decorum of the interaction, whether online or offline.

●  Ask good questions and try to answer any questions asked by the recruiters.

●  First impressions last.

2. Resume Screening

Your  resume  is  as  crucial  a  part  of  the  entire  selection  process  as  any  other.  Building  your  resumes  is  a
process  that  starts  not  from  the  day  application  deadline  is  released  but  from  the  1st/2nd/3rd  years  itself.  So
start ASAP. Try to tailor your resume to the role you are applying for.
All  the  resumes  have  to  pass  through  an  ATS  so  you  can  check  your  score  on  a  website  called
"ResumeWorded". My resume had a score of 60.
Key points regarding resumes -

●  They should be 1 page resumes as that's what is expected from freshers.

●  Make single column resumes in Latex format.

●  Try to keep all of the relevant coursework / competition / projects / internships in your resume.

●  Having 1-2 good finance projects on your resume helps.

●  If possible try to get a relevant internship so you have something more to talk about.

●  Participate in case study competitions.

●  Do some finance certifications and add them onto your resume.

All  these  points  are  just  suggestions  and  not  necessities  in  order  to  qualify  for  further  rounds.  I  will
elaborate  more  on  a  few  points  in  later  sections  of  the  document.  Results  were  declared  1  day  prior  to  the
OA Test i.e. on 5th July.

3. Online Aptitude test  (  97  candidates qualified for this round)

The  online  test  was  conducted  on  CoCubes  platform  for  us.  With  a  total  of  45  marks,  it  consisted  of  4
sections -

●  Finance  &  Accounting  (10)  :  This  section  contains  mostly  accounting  and  corporate  finance

questions. I think it had 1 question about puttable bonds.

●  Market Awareness (10)  : This section contained quite a few economy questions and current affairs.

●  Quantitative  Aptitude  (15)  :  This  was  a  quant  section  in  which  there  were  mostly  permutation,

probability and algebra questions. So this one is out and out mathematics.

●  Verbal Reasoning (10)  : This is an English section, pretty simple if you try to stick with the basics.

The  time  given  was  45  mins,  so  there  is  a  time  crunch  as  the  quant  section  is  tough.  So  try  to  segregate  the
sections  into  time  slots  so  you  don't  miss  out  on  any  section  in  the  end.  The  results  for  this  round  were
announced a day before the final day i.e. 9th July. So don't lose heart in the process and be prepared.

4. Group Discussion  (  72  candidates qualified for this round)

The  topic  for  the  group  discussion  was  revealed  on  9th  July  around  5pm  and  the  next  day  we  had  to  report
around  8:30  am  so  make  sure  to  do  your  research  prior  to  the  d-day.  Our  topic  was  "India:  the  5th  largest
economy".
Key points -

●  25-30 mins.

●  6 panels of 12 each.

●  You  can  carry  a  sheet  of  paper  with  you  as  reference  (but  avoid  looking  into  it  and  speaking  as  it

doesn't send the best message to the panelists).

●  We had 2 panelists and our group discussion was a moderated discussion.

●  Note  down  points  that  the  others  are  making  as  it  shows  your  sincerity  and  also  comes  in  handy  if

you're asked to conclude.

●  Try  to  have  at  least  3-4  entries  in  the  entire  discussion  and  at  max  1-2  entries  per  subtopic  (we  had

7-8  subtopics)  in  a  moderated  group  discussion.  Any  less  and  you  seem  underprepared;  any  more  and
you run the risk of coming off as too aggressive.

●  A  group  discussion  is  about  coming  to  a  conclusion  as  a  collective  unit,  so  try  not  to  refute  and  rebut

other candidates' points.

●  Be polite and extremely relevant.

●  Quality and relevance of points  matters a lot more than how many times you spoke in the GD.

●  Lastly, prepare well and from multiple viewpoints.

5. Interview Round 1  (  31  candidates qualified for this round)

Here  starts  the  real  interesting  part.  This  is  mostly  a  basic  finance  round  +  puzzles  +  mental  math.  The
interviewer  wants  to  check  your  basics  in  finance  and  how  quick  you  can  think.  At  times  guesstimates  are
asked  as  well,  but  I  don't  think  in  our  batch  a  lot  of  people  were  asked  those.  There  were  5  interview  panels,
mostly consisting of 1 panelist each, mine had 2 panelists though.
My Round 1 -

●  I wasn't asked any puzzles or mental math questions. Mine was an out and out finance round.

●  I  was  asked  about  bonds  (price  yield  relations,  yield  curves  &  inverted  yield  curves,  macaulay  &

modified durations)

●  Leading, Lagging indicators and their examples and relation with economic distress situations.

●  Next  was  the  accounting  section,  in  which  I  was  asked  the  relationship  between  the  3  basic

statements and how we make them.

●  I  was  asked  the  reason  for  positioning  the  3  statements  the  way  they  are  positioned  in  a  financial

model.

●  Lastly  in  the  accounting  section,  I  was  asked  what  impact  a  change  in  depreciation  would  have  on  all

3 statements with and without taxes and how it would affect the interest expenses.
Rounds  like  mine  would  be  one  of  the  rarer  occurrences  as  mostly  others  were  asked  puzzles  and  mental
math  questions  too.  So  be  prepared  with  them  as  well.  I  wasn't  given  any  sheet  of  paper  to  carry  out  the
rough work, for the accounting scenarios.
Some suggestions -

●  Have a good accounting background.

●  Be aware of financial markets.

●  Corporate finance is a key topic along with accounting and equities.

●  Do not worry about bonds much, as very few people were asked about them.

●  Go through and solve puzzles on your own.

●  Try to solve mathematical problems without actually writing them down, it'll help in the interviews.

6. Interview  Round  2  (Can't  say  how  many  qualified  for  this  round  as  the  interviews  were  conducted

parallelly)
I  got  the  longer  end  of  the  stick  in  round  1,  as  after  that  round  ,  my  round  2  was  mostly  relaxed.  Round  2  is
generally the Pro-Fit round. In that I was asked questions on my resume. My internship and my projects.
I  was  first  asked  to  introduce  myself  and  then  I  was  asked  which  are  the  top  3  stocks  in  India  by  market  cap.
When  I  answered  that  the  question  was  broadened  to  top  5  which  I  couldn't  get  right.  But  it's  fine  as  long  as
you try your best and are somewhat close.
The  questions  in  round  2  were  more  on  the  practical  side  of  things  and  I  was  asked  to  create  a  dummy
corporation  and  explain  what  it  does  and  what  its  costs  are  and  where  each  specific  item  is  put  in  the  cash
flow statement.
The  second  practical  question  was  about  mutual  funds  as  my  internship  was  regarding  those.  I  was  asked  to
act  as  a  financial  advisor  to  the  recruiter  and  ensure  a  suitable  investment  allocation  for  him  depending  on
his investment horizon and risk tolerance.

7. HR Round  (  15-17  candidates qualified for this round)

Lastly, the HR round. Here all of us were asked mostly the same questions. Namely -

●  Introduce yourself

●  Talk about your family

●  Higher education

●  Have you been in a situation where things were ethically not right, if yes how did you deal with it

●  What is your understanding of the role

●  Do you have any questions for me

It  is  important  to  understand  here  that  in  the  HR  round  it  doesn't  matter  what  you  say,  but  rather  how  you
say it. So practice how you're going to answer these as well.
(  11  candidates were finally shortlisted for CIB &  2  for fintech)

a.  Resume  worded:  Resume  Worded  -  Free  instant  feedback  on  your  resume  and  LinkedIn
profile
b.  Latex format:  Overleaf, Online LaTeX Editor

2.  Online Test -

a.  India Bix:  Aptitude Questions and Answers - IndiaBIX
b.  Quantguide:  QuantGuide - Interview Prep Platform for Quants

3.  Group Discussion -

a.  Youtube

c.  News

4.  Interview Rounds 1 & 2 -

a.  CFI:  Corporate Finance Institute
b.  Forage:  Free  Virtual  Work  Experience  Programs  from  Top  Companies  -  Forage
(theforage.com)

participation is crucial. Engage by asking thoughtful questions pertinent to the recruitment process or the
role. Be ready to provide concise answers to showcase your interest and presence.

1. Resume Screening: Deadline 4th July

2. Online Aptitude Test: 6th July

3. Group Discussion

4. Interview round 1

5. Interview round 2

6. HR round

Rounds 3-6 were scheduled on 10th July.
Resume Screening

1. JP Morgan typically asks for your resume with a one-day deadline, so have it prepared in advance.

2. Utilize tools like Resume Worded to check your resume's score. Aim for a high score; mine was 81/100.

3. Justify your achievements with numerical data and clear explanations to enhance your resume's

impact.

4. Ensure your resume includes strong action verbs and is crystal clear and concise.

5. Incorporate relevant

investment banking keywords to match the job description.

6. Make sure there are no grammar, punctuation,

or formatting mistakes in your resume.

7. Only include information that you are confident about. Interviewers can ask detailed questions on any

aspect of your resume, so avoid adding unnecessary details you're not prepared to discuss.

8. You can use both LaTeX or Word to make your resume. I used Word for mine.

9. Also, submit the cover letter along with your resume on the JP Morgan portal.

Online Aptitude Test

1. The test window was 11-11:30 am, and the duration was 45 minutes. It had 4 sections, with no

negative marking, and navigation was allowed:

2. Basics of Finance and Accounting: 10 questions

3. Market Awareness: 10 questions. Questions were not necessarily finance-based but general current

affairs.

4. Quantitative Aptitude: 15 questions. Questions were based on Profit and Loss, Workers and Time,

AP GP, Probability, etc. (Normal Aptitude questions).

5. Verbal Skills: 10 questions. Passage-based, rearranging, standard questions.

6. The test was lengthy, so try to attempt questions you know and balance your efforts across all

sections rather than acing just one.

expect CAT-level questions, so be patient and really quick.

prepared.

Group Discussion [72 selected students were divided into 6 panels of 12 each. We had Around 30 mins]

1. Preparation:

• The topic was revealed on July 9th, a day before the process.

• We could take notes for reference.

2. Group Discussion (GD):

• Two panelists were present.

We started with an introduction of the topic, our understanding of GDP, and India's growth.
Discussed key points like state contributions to the economy, lagging states, the impact of the
global scenario, and potential issues for India's economic rise.

• Concluded the discussion as instructed.

3. Key Tips for GD:

• Have at least 3-4 strong entries; focus on quality.

o Use numbers and statistics to support your points.

• Participate actively; panelists tracked participation.

o Be diplomatic and avoid interrupting or arguing.

• Summarize effectively when asked.

4. Interview Scheduling:

o GD performance influences interview scheduling; better performance means an earlier slot.

5. Preparation Tips:

• Start preparing as soon as you get the GD topic.

o Consider the global aspect of any topic.

Interview Round 1 [ My round lasted for about 25-30 mins]
First, they asked me to introduce myself. They then mentioned the CFI course about accounting that I had
completed. They started by asking how financial statements are linked. Then, they gave a case about
depreciation, asking how depreciation affects the statements. Additionally, they brought up the concepts of
debt and interest, inquiring how these elements are interrelated and their impact on the statements.
They also asked me about the Sensex and Nifty and for my opinion on overvalued stocks. Finally, they
presented two probability puzzles for me to solve. If you are stuck on any puzzles, at least tell them your
thought process. Don't keep your thoughts to yourself; share your approach. Interviewers are interested in
your approach, not just the correct answer. Luckily, I was able to solve both puzzles even though I had not

you don't know an answer, explain your approach, and if you're unsure, simply state that you don't know the

The entire selection process took place in their office, creating an atmosphere of anticipation and focus. We
were asked to report by 11 AM, and the day's events concluded by 6 PM. It was a long, eventful day, broken
down into multiple stages, each testing different skills.

1) Aptitude Test:

The first challenge was an aptitude test--24 questions to be solved in just 30 minutes. The difficulty level
ranged from easy to medium, but there were a few tricky ones that kept us on our toes. The questions were a
blend of mathematical concepts, including probability, logical problems, and a few coding-related ones that
touched on data structures. There were also SQL queries to interpret and questions on OOP fundamentals.
While most questions could be managed with a clear head, a couple demanded extra thought and were likely
designed to test deeper problem-solving abilities.

2) Coding Test:

Next came the coding test. We were tasked with solving five questions within 35 minutes. For each, we had to
write pseudo-code, except for one that required a direct answer--an interesting problem about doors and
multiples (100 doors, each opened or closed based on multiples of numbers from 1 to 100, and we had to
figure out how many would remain open). One problem was a variation of the classic LeetCode "Stock Buy
and Sell - 1", while another dealt with finding anagrams from a set of strings. Then, there was a question on
matching parentheses--definitely a logic-based brain teaser. There was one more problem, but I can't recall
the specifics at the moment. The challenge here was heightened by the fact that everything had to be done on
pen and paper, which meant no quick fixes or auto-corrections--just raw thinking and careful planning.

3) Interview Round 1:

For some, the first interview was in-person; for others, it was conducted online. This round primarily focused
on projects and SQL knowledge--indexes, queries, and the like. The interviewer dove deep into every project
or skill mentioned in my resume, dissecting each one to understand my level of expertise. It wasn't a nerve-
wracking experience, though. The interviewer was genuinely curious and very patient, creating a friendly
environment that allowed me to explain my work in detail. I could tell they were looking for depth and clarity
rather than just surface-level understanding.

4) Interview Round 2:

The second interview was a bit more technical. It started with logical reasoning and basic data structures and
algorithms. I was asked to insert values into a binary search tree and predict what the final tree would look
like. Another question asked if binary search could work on an unsorted array, which led to a discussion about
sorting and search algorithms. There were also two puzzles thrown in for good measure, designed to test my
problem-solving agility. SQL came up again, with questions about different types of indexes and how they
function. Inorder tree traversal was another key topic, and I had to demonstrate my knowledge in a way that
showed both theoretical understanding and practical application. And at the end, space and time complexity of
various sorting algorithms. When should one prefer a particular sorting algo.

5) Interview Round 3:

The final interview was a brief, informal chat, lasting less than 10 minutes. It was more about assessing my
thought process and less about grilling me on technical concepts. One interesting question that came up was:
"You are organizing a football tournament, how would you create a database schema for efficient
management?". There were also questions about the workings of DFS (Depth First Search) and BFS (Breadth
First Search), but they were presented in a very relaxed manner.

By the end of the day, I had learned a lot, both from the questions posed and the experience itself. One crucial
tip for anyone going through a similar process: always have a few questions prepared for the interviewer.
Whether you ask the same questions in every round doesn't matter; it shows genuine interest in the role and
the company.

3 students were selected.

1. Online MCQ (14/08/2024 - 15/08/2024) on HackerEarth

2. Machine Coding

3. Interview

1. MCQ Round [Around 150+ students applied] [Online]

There was a criteria of 7+ CGPA for applying at BrowserStack and everyone got the HackerEarth MCQ test
link which was valid for 2 days and I have given the test on the 2nd day i.e., on 15th Aug.
There were around 20 MCQs which we have to solve in 50 minutes (can be solved within 10 min) consisting
of HTML, CSS, JS, OS, DBMS. If you have basic to moderate knowledge of these fundamentals then you
can solve these MCQs pretty easily.
And a very important point, they not only see your MCQ score but also shortlist based on the resume as well
so make sure you have decent development skills mentioned in your resume. (my resume link)
After this round,
34 students shortlisted for BrowserStack and 22 for EdraLabs (sister company of
BrowserStack). I don't know on what basis they divided the students because the test was common. I was
among 34 students.
There was a clash between JPMC - CR and BorwserStack interview process and hence 14 - 16 people who
got shortlisted for both the companies were asked to choose one just a day before the interview and only 4
students chose BrowserStack including me.
I don't know about the EdraLab process but it was online.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Machine Coding Round [24 people appeared for this round] [Offline] [ 2hrs ]

This round was conducted in their office at Goregaon. We were divided into 6 batches, 3-6 people per batch
and then they sent a problem statement which was the same as last year. They have been using the same
problem statement for the past 2-3 years which you can find on gfg, github, etc.
This was the PS:
https://medium.com/@ibrahimanis/implement-log-watcher-similar-to-tail-f-command-7b0674d4b767
Sometimes they also ask this PS:
https://github.com/harssRajput/browser-stack-round/tree/main/browser_controller
I was prepared for the Log watcher problem as I have already read the GFG interview experience of this
company. We were given 2 hours to build the solution and there were 2 mentors for each batch. Basically
they will help you build the solution but make sure you clearly communicate your ideas and tell them about
the approach bes this will help you in case your solution doesn't work properly. And they will visit you in an
interval of ½ hour to help you guide the solution.
This problem involved using Socket. IO and Node.js file structures, which aren't commonly used by students
when building projects. However, practicing and incorporating these into your projects can give you an edge
in this round. Although they allowed the use of Google and ChatGPT, not being able to explain your code is
seen as a significant red flag. They were more interested in your thinking or approach to solve the problem
rather than seeing the results. You can use any tech stack python, node, java, etc.
After building the solution, my mentor asked how I would optimize it if the log file were several GBs or
larger. I started detailing my approach, and he provided hints whenever I veered off track. Unfortunately, due
to the limited time left, I wasn't able to fully implement the optimization despite having a clear direction.
And in the final evaluation he was satisfied with my approach and asked me to submit the code.
After lunch, students began receiving calls for the interview round, with only one student per batch being
selected. Four people had already been called, and I was getting really tense because no one from my panel
had received a call yet. Finally, after some time, I received a call for the interview. (fat gayi thi)
Be honest with your mentor. Tell him everything that you're trying to do with a clear approach.
Only 5 people received a call. But after some time one more person got a chance for the interview.

3. Interview Round [6 people appeared for this round] [30 - 40 mins]

There were three panels, each with one panelist. My round was conducted by a Senior Engineering Manager
who had been with the company for 6-7 years. After introducing himself, he immediately asked me to
explain the projects I had worked on. After giving a brief overview of one of my projects, he started asking
in-depth questions about my role, the backend development, and the reason for choosing the tech stack. For
instance, I used MongoDB to store data, and he questioned why I chose it over SQL. He also asked why I
created the project. These questions were focused solely on that one project.
Participating in Hackathons can help you build these projects so you don't have to spend time building them
alone. And try to talk about hackathons experiences as well.
--- PAGE 3 ---
He then asked me to explain another project, focusing on why I built it, what I learned, and the new tools
and technologies I used. For this project, I had utilized Redux Toolkit (RTK) so he asked me what I achieved
by using RTK .
I also gave details about Redux Toolkit (RTK) and RTK Query, explaining how I manage the overall state of
the application. I discussed the store, custom hooks, dispatch, and selectors to give him a clear
understanding of the state management in my project.
If you have in-depth knowledge of a particular tool or technology, you should definitely mention it and
explain it thoroughly. Sharing the ins and outs can leave a strong impression and create a positive impact
during the interview.
After that, he inquired about my major project. I explained every detail thoroughly, providing proper
examples. He then asked, 'If this already exists, why are you building it?' I responded by explaining the
technical challenges, why previous efforts in this area weren't successful, and how our approach is different.
My major project was related to machine learning, and while I only had upar - upar ka knowledge of some
aspects, I was able to clearly explain the idea and how it worked. It's always beneficial to have a good
understanding of your major project because many companies tend to ask questions about it.
He then asked me about threads and processes in the operating system, followed by the difference between
the WHERE and HAVING clauses in SQL. I explained it with a real-world example, and he seemed
satisfied. Next, he gave me a technical scenario: 'If you type www.google,com in your browser and the page
doesn't load, how would you debug it?' I walked him through my troubleshooting steps, and he asked
counter-questions along the way.
He then gave me a new scenario: 'You have a ITB file and need to find the count of a word, for example,
"interview." How many times does this word appear in the file?' I suggested dividing the file into chunks and
searching each chunk simultaneously. However, he pointed out this might fail when a word is split between
chunks. I then mentioned using MapReduce for handling such big data problems (thanks to GFG interview
experiences), but I admitted I couldn't fully explain its working. He appreciated my honesty and said, 'It's
fine.'
After that, he asked about my hobby projects. I mentioned that my web development projects were my
hobby project bes he didn't know I was from EXTC. When I revealed that I was an EXTC student, I
explained the projects we work on are completely different compared to these dev projects. Initially, I was a
bit scared because this company originally wasn't allowing EXTC students to sit for their process-only CS
students. But a heartfelt thanks to the TPO team for convincing them.
That wrapped up my interview when he asked if I had any questions for him. I inquired about what I should
learn from now to make the most of my internship.
Always remember to ask genuine questions at the end.
This was the final round, after which HR gave feedback to everyone. When it was my turn, I felt a bit
anxious about whether I had been selected or not. To my relief, HR informed me that they were happy with
my performance and would be pleased to extend an offer. Only 3 people got the offer.
That was it!

journey.prep:
1. The first and most important step to cracking any Interview is DSA Prep. Maximum

companies will have their first round as the Coding Round, so if you don't have a strong
hold over DSA, there is no point in preparing for the further rounds.

2. Start your DSA preparation early and make sure you participate in contests on

Hackerrank, Leetcode. This will give you the environment to think under the time
pressure, which will hugely help you in Online Assessments. You can also time your
solutions for practice.

3. Refer to the Top 150 Qs list on Leetcode:

https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-interview-150/
And for difficult topics like Dynamic Programming and Graphs, refer to Striver's A-Z
Sheet:
https://takeuforward.org/strivers-a2z-dsa-course/strivers-a2z-dsa-course-sheet-2/
Watch the solution videos of the initial questions and then solve problems of the topic by
yourself.

4. Most Qs are an alteration of some typical concepts that you need to be aware of. You

can practice these standard questions multiple times, so that the logic is memorized.
Some of these typical questions are:
https://eetcode.com/problems/two-sum/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-increasing-subsequence/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-subsequence/description/
--- PAGE 5 ---
https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-subarray/description/

5. You can start revising the computer fundamentals subjects(OOPS, DBMS, OS), one

month before the placements begin. Revising from resources on GFG, InterviewBit will
be sufficient. Make sure that you are confident about these subjects as they show that you
have a strong understanding of the concepts.
Some resources:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-dbms/?ref=lbp
https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/
https://www.javatpoint.com/oops-interview-questions
https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/

6. Knowing how to solve at least medium level SQL Queries is very important in

interviews. Have a clear idea of the use of JOINS and aggregate functions. For
practicing SQL Queries, you can use: https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/
SQL Queries:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sql-query-interview-questions/
https://www.interviewbit.com/sql-query-interview-questions/

7. Don't run behind increasing the number of questions you have solved on leetcode/any

platform. Quality> Quantity. The more quality questions you solve, the more your
understanding increases. Interviewers will test your understanding.

8. Communicate with your interviewers to let them know your train of thought while

approaching a question. They want to judge how you come to the solution, rather than
only the solution.

9. Be thorough with the content of your projects. Only mention projects that you have

complete knowledge about.

10. Prepare the answers to standard HR questions in advance, so that it saves you the

thinking time in front of the interviewer.

11. Be confident and mindful throughout your interviews. Try to ask the interviewers their

names and remember them. Try to involve the interviewers in your thought process.

1.
Online Assessment [ Around 290 candidates appeared for this round]
The online assessment was held on the Hackerrank platform with a duration of 75 mins. There
were 3 Questions in the test, as follows:
Q1: We are given an array of integers. We had to find the maximum length of the array for each
element, where the height of the current element is the maximum. We had to return the
maximum length for each element.
For eg. [3, 1, 2, 4, 7, 3]
So for the 1st element, 3, 3 has the maximum height till we reach 4 at index 3. I.e. 3 is the tallest
in the array 3, 1, 2. So the maximum length will be 3. Similarly for element 7, it's the tallest in
the entire array, so for that element the answer will be 6.
I implemented this using two pointers left and right, and calculated the maximum size for every
element. This resulted in a T.C. of O(N). However, I was able to pass 13/15 test cases here.
The optimized approach would have been using a Monotonic Stack, ON). The question used the
same concept as: https://leetcode.com/problems/trapping-rain-water/description
https://leetcode.com/problems/largest-rectangle-in-histogram/description/
--- PAGE 2 ---
Q2: Given two arrays of strings of equal size. For each string in the array at the same index, we
had to say if the strings were almost equal. Almost equal strings are those which have the same
length and the difference between the frequency of each character should be <= 3.
For Eg. s1 = [''abcb", "fgfh"], s2 = ['aacc", "bfd"]
I used a hashmap to solve this. For the strings, the freq of each character of both the strings was
stored. Then, the difference was calculated and the output was stored as YES or NO for the
satisfying conditions.
This was an easy question and with the implementation of the hashmap, I could solve all test
cases.
Q3:This was an SQL Query. Three tables were given. I don't exactly remember the question.
There were many things that needed to be calculated from the three tables by using the
appropriate JOIN. Aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM were also required. GROUP BY and
ORDER BY statements were required as well.
I wasn't able to crack the complete answer, so I couldn't submit this.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 49 candidates were shortlisted, 46 appeared ]

This round went on for 30 mins.
I was asked to introduce myself and after that, the interviewer proceeded with questions about
my resume. He asked about one of the projects which I had implemented in a Hackathon. I was
able to answer in detail about this as well as one more project. He asked me in detail about why I
chose the particular tech stack and asked me to implement the database structure of one of my
projects. He asked me what SQL and NoSQL databases are and asked me the structure of the
database in MongoDB and how I would store and display multiple addresses corresponding to
the same user. I answered by showing the JSON format of MongoDB Documents, and that I
would display all the addresses using the map function.
He then asked me to implement the following scenario using any programming language: There
is a fruit basket and the customer can enter 1 fruit (its name and quantity = 1). At the end he
wanted me to display the total quantity of each fruit in the basket. Firstly, I gave a solution using
unordered map in C++, and explained to him how unordered map will be efficient for this
approach. He then wanted me to implement this using some self designed structure. I got the hint
of the OOPs based approach, and explained to him the use of Class FruitBasket, its attributes and
creation of an object corresponding to each fruit name. Detailed explanation wasn't required
here.
I was further asked an SQL Query: There is an Employee Table(EmpID, EmpName, DeptID)
and the Department Table(DeptID, DeptName). I was asked to find the number of employees
corresponding to each department. This was fairly a simple SQL query and I wrote it down using
the JOIN and GROUP BY operations would give the correct result. He further added by asking
--- PAGE 3 ---
to represent the departments which have no employees as well. For this, I suggested using the
LEFT JOIN. He was satisfied with the answer and didn't ask me to write it down.
At the end, I asked him about the use of Generative Al being used by MSCI recently, which I
read in a news article. I asked about how MSCI is introducing Al into their technologies.

3. Technical Round 2 [ Around 25-30 candidates were shortlisted for this round ]

This went on for 30 mins as well.
The interviewer again asked me to introduce myself. Then, she asked me about the same project
I was asked in Round 1. I gave a detailed explanation of my contributions to the project. She then
asked me an OOPs question. There is a Library and we have to implement the various operations
of Borrowing a book, Returning a book and so on. I gave the solution using a Class Library and
the operations as methods. But she told me to implement separate classes for Books and Users.
So I wrote the pseudocode down and formed objects of Class Books and Users and implemented
the borrowing and returning operations inside the books class. She was satisfied with this
approach. She then asked me to explain Inheritance in OOPs.
Further, she moved on to ask me to implement the Queue Data Structure. I wrote the code down
using an array, and a rear and front pointer. I implemented the push and pop operations of the
queue. She gave me a sample test case to dry run the code. I could successfully do it.
Then, she asked me why I had used MySQL for a particular project. I answered it by explaining
the ease of representation in SQL in the form of tables. She followed up by asking me if I would
be able to use MongoDB instead for relational data, and how would the structure change. I
answered with a yes, and how MongoDB would represent the data in one single document for
certain entities rather than separate tables
She moved on to some HR questions. She asked me where I see myself in 5 years. Then she
asked me about my role models in personal and professional lives, and what inspires me to
pursue tech.
At the end I asked her about the huge amount of data that MSCI is handling, and what are the
measures taken for the security and management of the data.

4. HR Round [16 candidates were shortlisted for this round]

This was a typical HR Round.
The questions that were asked were:

1. Introduce yourself while not highlighting your tech achievements.

2. Why did you decide to pursue tech?

3. What are your hobbies?

--- PAGE 4 ---

4. What would you do to resolve conflicts in a team? And have you faced any such conflict?

5. Asked me about my family background, and if any family members were/are a part of

MSCI

6. Preference of location

7. Why I wish to work in a financial services company even though I have a Tech

background
At the end, I asked her about the roadmap for freshers in MSCI, and if MSCI initiates any special
programmes for freshers. I also asked her about the best thing about the culture at MSCI.
Finally, 6 Students got the offer.

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
1. The first and most important step to cracking any Interview is DSA Prep. Maximum

companies will have their first round as the Coding Round, so if you don't have a strong
hold over DSA, there is no point in preparing for the further rounds.

2. Start your DSA preparation early and make sure you participate in contests on

Hackerrank, Leetcode. This will give you the environment to think under the time
pressure, which will hugely help you in Online Assessments. You can also time your
solutions for practice.

3. Refer to the Top 150 Qs list on Leetcode:

https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-interview-150/
And for difficult topics like Dynamic Programming and Graphs, refer to Striver's A-Z
Sheet:
https://takeuforward.org/strivers-a2z-dsa-course/strivers-a2z-dsa-course-sheet-2/
Watch the solution videos of the initial questions and then solve problems of the topic by
yourself.

4. Most Qs are an alteration of some typical concepts that you need to be aware of. You

can practice these standard questions multiple times, so that the logic is memorized.
Some of these typical questions are:
https://eetcode.com/problems/two-sum/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-increasing-subsequence/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-common-subsequence/description/
--- PAGE 5 ---
https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-subarray/description/

5. You can start revising the computer fundamentals subjects(OOPS, DBMS, OS), one

month before the placements begin. Revising from resources on GFG, InterviewBit will
be sufficient. Make sure that you are confident about these subjects as they show that you
have a strong understanding of the concepts.
Some resources:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-dbms/?ref=lbp
https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/
https://www.javatpoint.com/oops-interview-questions
https://www.interviewbit.com/oops-interview-questions/

6. Knowing how to solve at least medium level SQL Queries is very important in

interviews. Have a clear idea of the use of JOINS and aggregate functions. For
practicing SQL Queries, you can use: https://leetcode.com/studyplan/top-sql-50/
SQL Queries:
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/sql-query-interview-questions/
https://www.interviewbit.com/sql-query-interview-questions/

7. Don't run behind increasing the number of questions you have solved on leetcode/any

platform. Quality> Quantity. The more quality questions you solve, the more your
understanding increases. Interviewers will test your understanding.

8. Communicate with your interviewers to let them know your train of thought while

approaching a question. They want to judge how you come to the solution, rather than
only the solution.

9. Be thorough with the content of your projects. Only mention projects that you have

complete knowledge about.

10. Prepare the answers to standard HR questions in advance, so that it saves you the

thinking time in front of the interviewer.

11. Be confident and mindful throughout your interviews. Try to ask the interviewers their

names and remember them. Try to involve the interviewers in your thought process.
Feel free to reach out: https://www.linkedin.com/in/awani-khodwe-64762422b/
ALL THE BEST!!! :)
--- PAGE 6 ---

journey.prep:
1. Try to maintain a good CGPA . CGPA criteria might not be mentioned directly but sometimes

companies may use it. CGPA above 8 looks impressive on the resume.

2. Make a good resume. Use a standard template , I used :

https://www.overleaf.com/latex/templates/jakes-resume-anonymous/cstpnrbkhndn
Check the ATS score of your resume on:
https://resumeworded.com/ (score above 60 recommended).

3. Please do not lie on your resume. Add only those projects/technical skills in your resume that you are

completely sure about. Keep 4-5 points ready for every experience/achievement you have mentioned.

4. Do a thorough research of the company and the role that you are applying for. Based on your research

prepare some good questions that you can ask to the interviewer after the interview.

5. Read the job description carefully. You can form some of your answers using keywords mentioned

in the JD.

6. Prepare for some standard HR questions  beforehand. So that you do not panic one day before the

interview. Please do not use too much AI for this. First, note down your points, and then you can use
AI to help refine them.

7. For DSA:

 Please focus on understanding each question thoroughly rather than just trying to solve as many
as possible. Even if you have successfully solved a question on your own , review solutions
shared by others to learn different approaches.
 Do standard questions first. Try to solve POTD on Leetcode or GFG  everyday.
 Giving contests helps to improve time management which is very important in DSA rounds of
companies.
 Always check the constraints  carefully. If you can't come up with the most optimal solution
right away, write the brute force solution first to secure partial marks.

8. Take core subjects seriously. If you are from EXTC background like me :

 I would suggest taking DBMS as your 6th Sem open elective. Since it is a very important subject
for placements plus it is very easy to score in exams.
 Also make sure to focus on CCN in Sem 6. This will help you in placement preparation for this
subject, as it is often part of the technical questions asked during interviews.

9. Have a good understanding of the programming language that you use the most. Get all the basics of

that language clear (if you are not able to answer them in an interview it creates a bad impression.)

10. Keep discussing your approach with the interviewer whenever you are solving a question. If you get

stuck somewhere they will help you.

11. If you and your friends share the same goal, motivate each other, take regular follow-ups on progress,

and push one another to stay on track.

12. Please do not get demotivated by rejections  , treat them as learning experiences to identify and

improve upon your weak areas. Many aspects of the placement process involve luck, so don't doubt
your capabilities. I faced rejections from JPMC (FinTech) and PhonePe interview rounds just 5 and 2
days before my MSCI interview. What helped me was focusing on what I could control--improving
and preparing for the next company.

13. Everything falls into place eventually! Do not stress about the results , give your best whenever you

get an opportunity.

journey.howSecured:
1. Pre Placement Talk

2. Online Test

3. Technical Interview 1

4. Technical Interview 2

5. HR Interview

1. Pre Placement Talk

The Pre Placement talk was organized on Microsoft teams platform by MSCI on 8 th July. It was
compulsory for everyone who applied for MSCI.
They gave us a brief introduction about MSCI's work , values and cultures. I would suggest make
notes or at least take screenshots during this presentation as you will be questioned on this in further
rounds.
If you have genuine doubts get them cleared.

2. Online Test [Everyone who applied was eligible for this round]

This was an online test on Hackerrank Platform. Duration of the test was 75 mins.
There were 3 questions : 2 DSA and 1 SQL based.

i) First question was similar to: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/maximum-people-a-person-can-see-
while-standing-in-a-line-in-both-direction/
I solved this question using two pointers and 14/15 test cases passed.

ii) Second question was easier: There where 2 arrays : projects and bid of size n. Every element in
projects had corresponding element in bid. We had to return the sum of minimum bid for each
project. Project ids would be from 1 to n. If any project id is missing,return -1.
I solved this question using unordered_map and passed all 15 test cases successfully.

iii) I do not remember the exact question but it was a bit challenging. Different concepts like Self Join,
Concat() function and group by were applicable in the same query. I was not able to solve this.

49 students were shortlisted for the next round but only 46 gave interview as 3 got placed in PhonePe.

3. Technical Interview 1  [46 students appeared for this round] (45 minutes)

First question interviewer asked me was "What do you know about MSCI ?"
After which she scanned my resume and asked me to explain my final year project which I had
mentioned in it. Then she moved on to another project and since I had used MongoDB as a database
in it she asked me "What are different types of databases and in what format are you passing data to
the database?"
Then she asked me to explain ACID Properties  of database transactions and gave me 3 SQL
questions to solve. I had to write these queries on a paper. They were easy and could be solved with
basic understanding of joins, subqueries and aggregates.
Questions:
There were two tables employee and departments. Department id was used as foreign key in employee
table.
i) Find the employees who are either in HR or Engineering Department. (Solved  using inner
join and OR/IN keyword).
ii) Total salary of employees in each department. (Solved using sum() and group by).
iii) Employee with the second highest salary (Solved using order by and limit keywords then
suggested another approach using subqueries and third approach using dense rank function).

After this she moved on to ask DSA questions:
i) First question asked was : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/problems/top-view-of-binary-
tree/1 .
I had done this question before but wasn't able to remember the approach initially. I kept
on talking with the interviewer and explained her my understanding of the question. Then
I asked her for a hint.
After the hint I was able to form the entire solution. So I took a sample test case and
explained her my solution with a dry run. She asked me to write a pseudo code for the
same and explain its time and space complexity.
ii) She gave me a scenario : There are two classrooms A and B and her aim was to keep
number of students in both classrooms same. If excessive students enter one class she
would shift them to the other class to keep numbers equal. In this way lot of students keep
coming in and going out.
Her question was: In this scenario which data structure should be used?
Since there are lots of insertions/deletions so I suggested that linked list can be used.
Then she asked what if there are N classrooms. I tried to answer the question but she
explained me why my approach was wrong and told me the answer she expected was B+
Trees.
iii) She asked me if I know about AVL Trees, to which I admitted that I don't.
Moving on to OOPS she asked me questions revolving 4 pillars of OOPS. To be precise the questions
were:
i) What is encapsulation?
ii) What are types of inheritance?
iii) Difference between multiple and hierarchical inheritance.
iv) What is meaning of overloading?
v) Can constructers be private?

Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her about the women leadership
forum community in MSCI and some questions related to what tech stack do freshers work on.

4. Technical Interview 2 (30 Minutes)

Interviewer asked me to introduce myself. Then she directly moved on to the projects that I had
mentioned in my resume and asked few questions about each of them . This included general
questions about the projects as well as on the tech stack used. She also asked me to write a specific
piece of code that was used in one of my projects.
Then she asked me which was my favorite subject and why. After I answered this , she directly
moved on to OOPS.
Questions:
i) What is the need of object oriented programming?
ii) What are classes and objects?
iii) If  I asked you to design a hospital management system using classes and objects what
all classes will you include in it? How will you implement appointment booking
functionality? I was asked to define the classes and its data members by writing a pseudo
code for them on a paper.
(I got stuck at few places while answering this but I kept on discussing my approach , with
her guidance I was able to come up with a valid solution.)
After this she asked me to write a C++ code to check if a string is a palindrome or not.
Then she asked me few non-technical questions:
i) Tell me something that is not on your resume.
ii) What are your interests and hobbies?
iii) Who is your role model?
iv) Where do you see yourself in next 5 years?
Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her how does MSCI provide
risk management tools and services to its clients and are they customized for the client ? Follow up
question to that : Since MSCI provides solutions as both services and tools ,  is MSCI a product based
or a service based company? She answered everything in detail.

5. HR Interview [17-18 students appeared for this round] (15-20 minutes)

My panelist was really sweet and this round felt more like a conversation than an interview.
Questions asked were:
i) What do you know about MSCI?
ii) Give me a brief introduction about yourself as a person, as a student, a little bit about your
academic journey and the projects you have worked on. ( Please keep your points short
and crisp for such questions so that the interviewer doesn't get bored.)
iii) What will you bring to MSCI if you get selected ?
iv) What are your plans for further studies?
v) Is there any particular domain in which you want to peruse your career?
vi) Preferred job location

Interview ended and she asked me if I had any questions for her. I asked her about different employee
engagement activities at MSCI. I also asked her for advice on building a successful career, as I am a
fresher and this would be my first corporate job.
6 students were offered the internship.

journey.prep:
1) Practice dsa by giving leetcode contests consistently and upsolve post contests.

2) See the execution time, constraints etc carefully for each problem. Sometimes, brute force

solutions get accepted. If you don't get an optimal solution, submit brute force and then move on.

3) DSA > JAVA > OOPS (practical implementation) > SQL > DBMS > OS > CIN

4) Take non-tech questions seriously, start preparing and mirror practicing before.

5) Remember the names of the interviewers and keep a note of it.

6) Takes notes or atleast screenshots during ppt of a company.

7) Give mock interviews to seniors, connect with alumni on linkedin and get mocks done.

8) Don't skip any company. Because campus placements are 50% skill + 50% luck, your selection

depends on the panel taking your interview.

9) Focus on optimizations in striver sheet problems, these optimizations might not help in online

assessment but would help in interviews.

10) Please make your resume using overleaf latex and not google docs.

11) Keep three types of explanations for projects

a) Short description
b) Explanation with technical jargons and project flow for a tech interview
c) Simple and easy to understand explanation for a non-tech person.

12) Maintain notes for revision, I recommend google docs, make a folder for placement prep and

separate google docs for each subject/technology/topics etc. Keep adding relevant screenshots.

13) Practice TOP 50 sql questions on leetcode.

14) Be well versed with schema and api responses for 3rd party apis / your own projects that you have

used.

15) Be ready for questions like why 'ABC technology and not 'XYZ' technology. Give metrics while

explaining

16) I recommend you to memorize solutions to standard and non-intuitive questions like josephus

problem, celebrity problem, tower of hanoi etc

17) Useful links:

a) Post contest leetcode: https://www.youtube.com/@ARYANMITTAL
b) Web dev: https://www.youtube.com/(@,WebDevSimplified
c) ML: https://www.youtube.com/@campusx-official
d) Projects: https://www.youtube.com/@piyushgargdev
e) Devops: https://www.youtube.com/@TechWorldwithNana
--- PAGE 4 ---
Tips if you have months left for placements:

1. For project, either of two types would help

a. Project with normal implementation but great cause, eg- My friend had developed a full
stack project for something related to police officers and stations. Was appreciated by senior
officer for the same
b. Project with complex implementation but normal cause, eg- I had a project which
compiles code and executes to give output (like leetcode). This problem statement sounds
normal and doesn't have much real world use case. But, I developed a good architecture for it
with modern tech like docker, rabbitmą, redis etc. I also had numbers to talk about, like 100
concurrent executions in 10-12 sec etc.
c. Plz don't waste time in generic problem statements and don't try to make projects in every
domain like BCT, ML, WEB. Learn the basics of each, but eventually master one thing. No
one cares in which domain you are making projects until the problem statement is cool

2. Try to get an internship (at least one). Don't go for html/css based internships, try to get in modern

techstack or atleast in vanilla js or jquery roles. If work is good and you are contributing, unpaid
internships are also fine (but remote).

3. Java or c++ or python is the most stupid question, Any language works

4. Dev vs CP vs DSA is also a stupid question. Try to identify in which domain you will be able to

get achievements. For eg- Eventually, I realized that I won't be able to win hackathons or do
something in open source, so I focused on leetcode (DSA) and had a Guardian rating when I applied.

5. Try to get CGPA above 8

6) Given table A and B with a single column in each have N and M tuples respectively. How many
